Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī! Her physical body having been consumed by fire, she exists as a subtle body of a sinner;
being led away by the messengers of Yama, she opens the path of Yama.
Because she was a companion of Yama, she was restrained by the Lord of Yama;
consequently, she experienced suffering for the sake of opening the path to Yama.
Then, dispatched by Yama, she went to heaven, to the abode of the gods.
"You have no place here, O sinful one!"—thus were they rebuked by the messengers of the gods.
"For you who have violated the day of Hari, there is no dwelling in the abode of the gods.
Then, O Lakṣmī, that deluding woman became distressed, seeking a place to dwell.
She proceeded toward Pātāla, where she was obstructed by those dwelling in Pātāla—
by gods, sages, Daityas, Dānavas, and likewise by Ṛṣis;
by Pitṛs, humans, Yakṣas, and by Bhūtas, Pretas, and Piśācas.
She was seen by the holy fords, mountains, excavations, oceans, and forests;
likewise by the principles (tattvas), the world-protectors, the Manus, and those who dwell in the waters—
by all those founders of sacred sites on Mount Raivata, Mohinī was beheld.
She was seen by the dull-witted and the conscious alike— as were the stars, the planets, the trees, the creepers, and likewise the grasses— to be the slayer of sons and the slayer of husbands.
She was driven away from her respective places by beasts and birds as well.
Therefore, not protected by anyone, the daughter of Brahmā cried out and went into the presence of Janaka, reporting her own suffering:
"O Father, there is no place for me in the three worlds, including all that is mobile and immobile. (1.292.10)
Wherever I went, they all insulted me,
humiliated me, and expelled me from their hermitages.
Then, by my father’s command, I went to the house of Rukmāṅgada.
This has been seen and determined: it is an object of contempt for the whole world.
O father, having tormented her husband, having killed her dear son, and having destroyed Sandhyāvalī, she has reached this state. (12–13)
Neither for a human nor for a lord is there any means for my liberation, even from this state;
specifically, due to the curse of Vasu, I have become a partaker of misery.
If you, together with the gods, [will release] that twice-born Vasu from his curse...
"If you please me out of affection for me, then may I attain an auspicious state.
For those consumed by the curse of a brahmin, the Gaṅgā bestows liberation.
I am the wife of Rukmāṅgada, a widow and a doer of evil."
And the priest Vasu, a brahmin, is my refuge from that king;
may he lead me to the sacred fords and wash away my sins.
May he also turn back the curse, and then I shall attain a happy state.
Hearing her speaking thus, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds,
accompanied by Śiva, Indra, Dharma, Sūrya, Agni, other gods, and sages,
placed Mohinī at his front and went into the presence of the Vasus.
On Mount Raivata, in the forest by the Svarṇarekhā river,
Brahmā himself, out of reverence, placed Vasubhava Vāmana in the sky.
When an impossible task has arrived, even the youngest [Viṣṇu] performs it.
"O Lakṣmī, the salutation of the youngest brother shall not be considered an offense.
(21) Having seen them, Vasu rose and offered obeisance to Brahmā and the others.
All the gods then requested that which would bring happiness for the sake of Mohinī. (22)
Have mercy, O best of ascetics; become one who leads Mohinī to her goal.
She has become the patroness of this sacrifice and is living in the king's house. Therefore, O ascetic, you must act for the welfare of my daughter.
"Desiring the welfare of the gods, I myself dispatched her here. Indeed, by Rukmāṅgada, both the realm of Yama and heaven have been rendered empty;
therefore, I sent Mānasī to provide them with a place to dwell."
For the sake of deluding Rukmāṅgada, he attained the state of Hari;
that destination of Dharma is so exceedingly subtle that people do not know it at all.
By this [action], they have earned the rare union with Hari.
The king, together with his wife and sons, was led to the abode of Hari.
(27) By this beloved wife, having been tested exceedingly, he was led to Acyuta;
for that realm which cannot be attained by others has indeed been reached by her. (28)
He indeed is the son, she is the wife, she is the daughter, and he is the father;
he by whom liberation is attained is the kinsman, the friend, and the teacher. On the day of Hari, one must not eat, even if constrained by opposition to the vow.
O Vasu, having considered that deed— which was indeed of the nature of sin— to have strengthened the king's delusion here, you have reduced Mohinī to ashes,
leaving only her subtle body consumed by your curse. (1.292.30–31)
Therefore, pacify him; forgive her and bestow your favor, O Sage.
Attain tranquility; let there be no further grinding of what has already been ground by the lords of the gods.
Abandon cruelty, embrace peace, and show grace, my son!
Having heard this, the tranquil and forgiving Vasu, the royal priest, said:
"I have reflected upon this and concluded that the dwelling of Mohinī is certain; let her do whatever was intended for which she was created. (33-34)

"This Mohinī was created for the purpose of sending them along the path of Yama, for the purpose of breaking their vows, and so that those who have fasted on the day of Hari might go to the abode of Brahmā. Therefore, she must indeed accomplish that task."
By her, the husband, the co-wife, and the son were sent to Vaikuṇṭha.
Let this Mohinī reside in such a place;
by her proximity, people shall always observe the Ekādaśī vow. (36–37)
May those who have undertaken the excellent vow to please Lord Hari attain liberation without obstacles.
But those who are deluded regarding this vow and wander astray on its day—
may their sins lead them to the world of Yama, and may the work of Yama befall them accordingly.
"Wherever she stands, that vow indeed becomes broken.
"That cannot be considered a true vow; rather, let it be a violation of the vow.
Having reflected thus on the matter here, I have determined the meaning correctly.
The garment of a widow or a seductive woman (mohinī) accomplishes all purposes;
however, by wearing it during any vows, one becomes corrupted.
Therefore, on the day of a vow, wearing her garment is certainly not appropriate.
However, her residence should be at the end of the first day of the vow.
Let the end of that first day be rendered auspicious by her dwelling there;
since her birth was from Brahmā (Vidhātṛ), she is indeed considered Vaidhasī.
Wherever that [piercing] occurs at the end of a lunar day (tithi), it is called a *vedha* (piercing).
A lunar day characterized by such a piercing is the first [of the two], which is defective and bestows sin;
it should be understood as the destroyer of religious vows (*vrata*) and the giver of the city of Yama.

If a lunar day (tithi) does not exist at sunrise but exists at sunset, and it is to be observed as the fast-day (upoṣyā), it bestows the fruits of Yama’s realm; therefore, one should not perform a vow on such a day, for it yields a contrary result. (45–46)
At sunrise, in the forenoon, the seventh or the tenth lunar day occurs;
likewise, in sequence, the fourteenth or the eighth occurs.
In the afternoon, the eighth of the dark fortnight and the eleventh likewise occur.
The Pūrṇā or Amā Rāmanavamī begins in the evening.
In this manner, at the respective times, it likewise occurs at the conclusion of the seventh,
the end of the tenth, the conclusion of the fourteenth, and similarly at the end of the eighth.

Let the deluding one dwell there; those sinful lunar days are always [inauspicious]. Therefore, the vow should be observed in sequence: the eighth-day vow on the seventh day is indeed declared to lead to the realm of Yama and to be a refuge for the sin of *vedha*.
Indeed, a vow on the tenth day, or a vow on the eleventh day, brings about sin. Likewise, a vow on the fourteenth day, a full-moon vow, or a new-moon vow—
any vow performed at night— is a source of sin that leads one to the world of Yama.
Therefore, if the lunar day (tithi) constituting the vow occurs at sunrise as the first part and at sunset during the night as the other, it should never be observed as a fast.
For Māhinī dwells there at the end of the day, beginning with the seventh [lunar day].
The seventh and subsequent lunar days are not to be observed as fasts, even if one is otherwise engaged in evening vows;
for they have been offered to Mohinī for the purpose of filling the flow of Yama’s path.
They are based on the Vedas, yet they are the refuge of sin, being presided over by Mohinī.
And this is the final decision regarding a confusion of the vow when it extends into the evening:
"The vow must not be performed at all"—thus was it firmly established by the gods.
Now, if the seventh or the tenth lunar day occurs before sunrise, [the following applies].
Likewise, the fourteenth or the eighth [lunar day] proceeds in due order.
At sunrise, the Kṛṣṇajanmāṣṭamī, the Ekādaśī, the full moon, the new moon, or the Rāmanavamī likewise proceed when the sun is present. (57–58)
Thus, in due course of time, at the end of the seventh [tithi], likewise at the end of the tenth,
at the end of the fourteenth, and at the end of the eighth,
let Mohinī dwell there at dawn, conjoined with the junction of those respective lunar days.

The lunar day (tithi) which begins at sunrise and constitutes the essence of a vow is called "pierced" (viddhā); it is thus delusive by its very nature. Therefore, a vow performed on a pierced lunar day becomes a source of merit that bestows heaven.
Thus, because it was so determined by the gods, the vow when pierced does not lead to heaven;
nor can it bring about liberation, for it bestows only exhaustible merit.
Therefore, those devotees who desire liberation must not perform the vow when it is pierced.
The eighth and eleventh lunar days must always be observed in their pure form;
likewise, the full moon and the new moon, as well as other lunar days consisting of vows,
should always be taken in their pure state for the purpose of a vow, and never when they are pierced by another day.
Or rather, it was not determined by the gods at that time whether [the day] was pervaded by the evening [tithi];
a devotee who fasts on a pure Hari-day attains liberation.
Others, however, maintain that the fasting should be on the day [of the tithi] itself, avoiding only a pierced lunar day.
On the ninth, the twelfth, and likewise on the first day;
then sequentially on the tenth, and again on the eighth of the dark fortnight;
then on the eleventh, the full moon, and the new moon—these are the days for the birth of Rāma. (66–67)
That vow which is pure indeed bestows liberation on the day of Hari;
know that a pure vow centered on Hari is considered to grant heaven.
That which ends with Mohinī grants the realm of Yama; indeed, one's destination corresponds to how one performs the rite.
Having thus reached this conclusion, a place was assigned to Mohinī.
The concluding portion of the first lunar day (tithi) invariably leads to the path of Yama;
however, if there should be two lunar days [overlapping], the vow must be performed on the following day.
When there is a loss of a lunar day (*tithi-kṣaya*), the pure (*śuddhā*) day that follows is to be observed for a vow by one seeking its merit;
however, a day that is pierced (*viddhā*) by the loss of the previous night’s portion must never be observed by people.
For the "piercing" (*vedha*) at midnight is intended to assist in the observance of the restraints (*yamāḥ*), yet it is delusive.
Indeed, before the sun [rises], the Mohinī [form] exists solely for the benefit of the gods.
The Śuddha, Āviddha, and Antaritā [forms] exist for the benefit of those seeking liberation.
Furthermore, in all the worlds, the tenth lunar day belongs to Yama.
"You must always remain at her edge; thus you have been addressed as Mohinī. O Mohinī, let half of the fruit of this vow indeed belong to you.
O Mohinī, let the entire fruit of the night-vow indeed belong to you."
O deluder, let that alone be sufficient for the destruction of your own sins.

Travel across the earth as the holy pilgrimage sites (tīrthas) themselves for the destruction of your own sins; for there are pilgrimage sites, O deluder, for the destruction of the sins of sinners! (75–76)
And they shall take away your sin even while staying at a sacred ford without observing a vow;
likewise, those who dwell at a sacred ford without vows share in sins as indelible as adamantine cement.
Your purification will occur among them again and again for all time.

"O Mohinī! This place has been granted to you for the purpose of establishing Yama and for the accumulation of sin, at the end of the time of night. [And this] has been granted for the purpose of establishing heaven and for the accumulation of merit. (78–79)
"O Mohinī! A place has been granted to you until the rising of the sun tomorrow morning.
However, for the sake of those seeking liberation, you must dwell far away in every respect.
O beautiful woman, do not look upon the vow of the seekers of liberation with your own eyes!"
"If that were so, you would again suffer destruction by means of a curse.
Having been thus instructed by Brahmā and the others, Mohinī became pleased;
she considered herself to have achieved her purpose through that place and her pilgrimage.
"Even when the body has been reduced to ashes, the work of Yama, the work of the gods, and the work of liberation were indeed perfectly accomplished by means of the subtle body.
Seeing that her purpose was thus fulfilled, she became exceedingly joyful.
The king accomplished his own task, and Mohinī accomplished her own.
The task of Yama, the task of the gods, and the task of liberation were set in motion.
Then, regarding the act of Rāhu swallowing the sun and the moon—
Indeed, during the time when Rāhu is within the path of vision, Mohinī remains in the piercing (vedha).
That time of piercing is ordained by the lords of the gods for her to stay.
Therefore, it is traditionally taught that all activities such as eating during the piercing are full of sin.
The deed committed for the sake of a seductress leads the doer to the realm of Yama;
thus the path of Yama is traversed by her as well.
In this manner, the piercing (vedha) of lunar days is established according to the preceding vow. 87–88.
"The sin belongs to the doer, while the deluding one [Māyā] partakes of the fruit"—
having established this rule, O Lakṣmī, and having reached her own station as the most deluding one,
she, being greatly delighted, bowed to the gods and prostrated before her own domestic priest.
Situated at the end of the tenth day and so forth, it causes delusion for people.
Therefore, the tenth day that touches sunrise is always censured;
even that which does not touch sunrise leads only to delusion.
Speaking thus, the lords of the gods departed for their respective abodes.
Then the daughter [of Brahmā] earnestly entreated the Creator for the recovery of her husband whose body had been consumed by fire,
and she also repeatedly requested Vasu and the family priest.
Brahmā, the creator of all the worlds, spoke also to Vasu:
"O Vasu, dear son, understand this: what does your patroness say?
Out of anger, you have reduced this Mohinī to ashes."
She entreated him: "Produce a gross body and indeed grant it to me;
once her purpose is accomplished, this ascetic woman must be protected by both you and me.
Furthermore, Viṣṇu considers her to be the enemy of the day and a doer of evil."
"Let whatever means may purify her be ordained for her sake.
Having heard that, the priest directed him to a distance of one *yojana* away;
there Brahmā sprinkled the ground produced from Mohinikā’s bones with water from his water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*).
Then, from those ashes, her body was produced again by the Creator;
endowed with a body, she bowed down to her father Vasu and indeed entreated him again and again for the washing away of her sins.
Then Vasu instructed Mohinī on how to undertake a pilgrimage to sacred fords (tīrthas),
as well as the specific rites for the Gaṅgā and other holy sites.
Thereupon, Mohinī set out for the sacred fords together with Vasu.
The Gaṅgā, Gayā, as well as Godāvarī, Jagannātha, Prayāga,
Kurukṣetra, Haridvāra, the excellent Badrikāśrama,
Puṣkara, Tryambaka, Rāmeśvara, and likewise Narmada.
Having visited Vṛndāvana, Siddhasārasvata, the site of Dvāravatī,
Prabhāsa, Kuṅkumavāpī, and Raivata— all these sacred fords (tīrthas)— Mohinī returned to Vasusthala together with Vasu. || 102-103 ||
Having bathed in the Nārāyaṇa lake, she went to Rukmāṅgada-pura;
then, having bowed to the sacred site of the mountain on the Vastrāpatha to the west of Raivata,
she proceeded to the world of Satya in the abode of Brahmā by means of that very body.
The goddess Mohinī, born of Brahmā, is bodiless and clothed in piercing [wisdom]; she is the deity presiding over the ego of Time. She is the lunar day Ekādaśī born of Viṣṇu;
she was fashioned by the Creator through the power of her rivalry with the one born of Viṣṇu.
"And this [Ekādaśī] always stands at the end of the tenth, as if competing with it. Thus, O Lakṣmī, I have told you the reason for the "pierced" (viddhā) Ekādaśī;
for that purpose, the Deluder (Mohinī) was created by the Creator and placed therein.

"Subtle-bodied and a destroyer of vows—what else do you wish to hear? (108). Thus ends the ninety-second [chapter] in the first section, the *Kṛtayugasantāna*, of the *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*, within the *Brahmāṇḍa*. This chapter describes how Mohinī, having failed to obtain a dwelling place, requested Brahmā and Vasu; how she obtained a residence granted by them at the conclusion of the lunar day preceding the vow; how she became productive through the flow of results from the worlds of Yama, the gods, and Brahmā; and how, by employing both the "pierced" (*viddha*) and "pure" (*śuddha*) types of days, she was again born as a deity with a physical body.
The two hundredth chapter.
Chapter 292: *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā*, Section 1 (The Lineage of the Kṛta Yuga).
Chapter 293.
[The Author: Chapter 294.
Śrī Lakṣmī said:
The twelve months have been declared, as well as the days of religious observance within them.
Even more than those, there was a thirteenth [son] who was two and a half years old. || 1 ||
"O Lord, I am eager for all to hear his life story, the ritual procedure, and [the nature of] the deity, which is to be accomplished through the fullness of the moon. (2)
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, to this divine narrative concerning Puruṣottama, wherein no solar transit (saṃkrānti) occurs during the lunar month. 1.

When the sun remains in the enjoyment of a single zodiacal sign and does not transit into another, this month, being devoid of a solar transit (saṃkrānti), is considered an intercalary month (adhika). || 2 ||
The lunar month is completed between two new moon days;
the solar month, however, is completed between two transits [of the sun]. (3)
In a lunar month, there are twenty-nine solar days (sāvana), as well as twenty-six ghaṭikās and fifty palas. 4.
Furthermore, in the saura [day], thirty days, twenty-six ghaṭikās, and nineteen palas are indeed consumed. (5)
Thirty-one viguṇas and fifty-two kṣaṇas are enjoyed by those two in the lunar [year]; the time that remains after subtracting the solar [period] is as follows. (6)
When a conjunction of those remaining times occurs,
this thirteenth lunar month, being complete, is considered an intercalary month (adhika).
Indeed, in thirty-two solar months plus sixteen days, there are exactly thirty-three lunar months plus sixteen days. (8)
An additional month is produced; this is considered the intercalary lunar month.
Generally, in five years, two such intercalary lunar months are reckoned. (9)
Furthermore, that intercalary month occurs every eight years, or in nineteen,
or indeed in one hundred and forty-one years.
"He indeed comes"—such is generally the established rule;
this was determined by the sages of old for the purpose of performing meritorious deeds. (11)
Listen to this story, O Lakṣmī! It originated from our home. This is called the *malamāsa* (intercalary month), so named because it is a collection of residual impurities (*mala*). (12)
Through union with Puruṣottama and through taking refuge in Puruṣottama, this month is Puruṣottama;
its deity is Puruṣottama. (13)
The glorious Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is the Supreme Brahman, higher than the highest;
the Blessed Lord, the sovereign of the imperishable, is eternally served by Brahmā and the liberated souls. (14)
Hari himself is the original source of those who possess the nature of incarnations, from whom all the manifestations such as Vāsudeva and the others are produced. (15)
Because from that [reality] the abodes such as Goloka manifest, wherein lies the supreme pinnacle of all, and wherein everything is established. (16)
Since everything—whether insentient or sentient—is manifested by Him and consists of Him, He is this venerable Blessed Lord, the King of Kings, the Supreme Sovereign. (17)
The presiding deity of the month of Puruṣottama is Puruṣottama himself, who dwells in the imperishable supreme ether, served by the assembly of liberated souls. (18)
Seeing the helpless intercalary month, the Lord, overcome by compassion and the protector of those seeking refuge, accepted it as one who had come for shelter. (19)
By virtue of being its locus, the illustrious Malimluca, having attained equality with the Imperishable (akṣara) from that [source], is stainless and the Supreme Person (puruṣottama). || 1.293.20 ||
All the months first roared repeatedly:
"There is nothing like us to deliver one from danger in the three worlds. (21)
But as long as the intercalary month was presided over by Śrī Hari, those twelve months became humbled of their pride. ||22||
O Mahālakṣmī, what more need be said? For one in whose presence Nārāyaṇa himself remains pleased, his fortune, merit, and life-story are beyond description. (23)
Whatever merit is produced by other means—through recitation, fire-offerings, or giving—it becomes infinitely more effective when performed here in every respect. (24)
This intercalary month is considered to bestow an abundance of all merit;
whatever [is performed] at Gayā, the Gaṅgā, Haridvāra, Puṣkara, and other such places [during this time], [yields great fruit]. (25)
The fruit of that performed during the intercalary month is eternal;
it is equal to the fruit obtained from bathing at Kurukṣetra during an eclipse, and to the satisfaction of the ancestors attained by offering funeral cakes (piṇḍas) at Gayā. || 26 ||
The fruit of that is such satisfaction resulting from the observance of the intercalary month (adhimāsa).
Whatever great fruit there may be from the chariot procession (rathayātrā) in Jagannāthapura,
that fruit shall be obtained by bathing during the month of Puruṣottama.
Whatever fruit is obtained from bathing in the Sarayū and visiting the sacred sites at Sāketa, that same fruit—and indeed even more—is produced by bathing on this very first day. (29)
Whatever fruit is obtained by bathing at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean in Dvārakā,
that same fruit is attained merely by bathing on the first day (pratipad) during the intercalary month (malamāsa).

Whatever fruit may be obtained from bathing in the Svarṇadī river at Badarikāśrama, a greater fruit than that shall be obtained by bathing on the first day of the intercalary month (malamāsa). || 31 ||
Whatever fruit is obtained from bathing in the waters at Rāmasetu on the southern shore, that same fruit shall be attained by bathing on the first day of the intercalary month (malamāsa). 32.
Whatever fruit may be obtained from bathing at Raivata or Svarṇarekhā, or whatever fruit may be obtained at Prabhāsa from immersion in the presence [of the deity],
the fruit of bathing on the first day is even greater than that.
Whatever fruit is obtained at Kuṅkumavāpī and at Aśvapaṭṭasara, [that same fruit is obtained here]. (34)
The fruit of that [merit] is even greater on the first day of the intercalary month at the Śuklatīrtha of the Narmadā and at the Oṃkāreśvara Tīrtha. || 35 ||
Whatever fruit is obtained at the western Puṣkara, at the Nārāyaṇa lake, at the Mānasa tank, and also at Prayāga—[that same fruit is attained here]. || 36 ||
Whatever fruit is obtained at the Yamunā, at Mathurā, and also at the Gaṇḍakī; and whatever fruit is obtained in the fields of Hari and Śambhu, and in the ocean of Kapila; || 37 ||
Whatever fruit is obtained at the Godāvarī, likewise at Kumbhalagna, at Kṛṣṇājala, at the Sindhu, at the Tāmraparṇikā, and also at the Kāverī;
as well as at Mahodaya, at Somāmā, and on the festival day (parvan) at Paṭṭana— [that fruit is attained here]. 38.
Whatever fruit is obtained through bathing elsewhere, that same fruit is obtained here by bathing on this very day.
On the first day of the month of Puruṣottama, being composed,
one should meditate upon Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person, during the Brāhma-muhūrta.
One may bathe in a river, a pond, a lake, a spring, at home, in a well, a large tank, or a flowing stream; that merit shall be eternal. || 4.1 ||
Indeed, in this world, there is nothing else like the intercalary month (adhikamāsa) for destroying sins, nor anything else so supreme for acquiring merit and bestowing heaven and liberation. 42.
On the full moon day, on the first day of the month, and also on the new moon day;
and likewise on the eleventh and the final day of the month during the Puruṣottama festival.
Indeed, there is nothing else equal to bathing that produces such unbroken merit;
for by bathing in those [waters], people truly shake off their mass of sins. (44)
By the accumulation of merit, they are born on earth like the two shores [of the ocean];
indeed, by merely bathing there, one shall obtain residence in heaven for ten million kalpas. ||45||
By worshipping Hari there, one shall go to the eternal Vaikuṇṭha;
by offering the *naivedya* of Puruṣottama, the fourfold liberation is attained. (46)
There is no doubt that one obtains this; Śrī Kṛṣṇa himself declares it.
Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, accompanied by Lakṣmī, indeed bestows everything. ||47||
On the first day of the intercalary month (malamāsa), for one who bathes and likewise worships, his ownership over the abode in Goloka proceeds just like that of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. 48.
If a morning bath is taken in rivers on either the full moon or the new moon day, it is considered by Viṣṇu to yield fruit equal to the avabhṛtha-concluding bath of a sacrifice. 49.
If a bath is performed at midday, it bestows the merit culminating in the Aśvamedha sacrifice;
a bath in the evening yields the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice.
Having bathed, the observer of the vow should invoke Hari Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, who is fashioned of gold, and likewise bathe him slowly with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta). ||51||
The merit acquired by observing the Ekādaśī vow on a festival day during an intercalary month (malamāsa) is attained merely by bathing; what else is required for its accomplishment? (5.2)
Whatever fruit is obtained by the gift of a hundred thousand cows marked with the *lakṣaṇa* sign, of ten thousand buffaloes, and of elephants at Kurukṣetra— [that fruit is attained here]. (53)
Whatever fruit is obtained on the Kaurava land from the gift of a hundred thousand horses, that same fruit is attained by bathing at dawn on the first day (pratipad) of the intercalary month. 54.
Indeed, the impurity of the twelve months is called *mala*; the intercalary month (*malamāsa*) has been established as that which is capable of washing away that impurity. //55//
Then one should bathe Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), after having massaged him repeatedly with pure water and the essence of oils. 56.
Then one should bathe Puruṣottama and wipe him with cloths;
one should offer a yellow lower garment and an upper garment with golden borders. (57)
The crown, the earrings, as well as sandalwood paste, saffron, collyrium, necklaces, signets, and bracelets. ||58||
Having offered flower garlands, waist-bands, ornaments, garments, as well as substances, decorations, and finery, one should perform worship. ||59||
One should offer incense, lamps, as well as ear-ornaments, crests, and garlands; likewise, one should present flower clusters, bulbs, golden staffs, umbrellas, and chowries.
Food offerings consisting of well-prepared sweet and cooked meals, fruits, delicious and savory drinks, betel leaves, and water. ||61||
Then one should offer [the deity], perform the lustration ceremony (nīrājana), and request forgiveness;
one should perform circumambulation, prostrations, and offer praise while lying flat like a staff (daṇḍavat). ||62||
Having offered a handful of flowers to Śrī Hari, the Supreme Person, one should repeatedly pray for the fulfillment of the vow of the intercalary month (mala-māsa). ||63||
O Lord, by your grace, I shall perform the vows of fasting, eating once a day, eating only at night, or subsisting on fruits during the intercalary month; may I do so for you, O Master. (4)
O Hari, being pleased, grant that this may reach completion without obstacle;
perform your daily bath every morning at a sacred ford, a well, a house, or a river. (65)
"O Supreme Person! I shall perform acts of charity and worship according to my ability, so that all such devotional service may be free from obstacles for me. (66)
Have mercy, O Great King; destroy idleness from your body, and by your power, wash away the impurities of the mind here. (67)
O Supreme Lord, burn away my own sins;
O Keśava, Supreme Person, grant me liberation for myself. (68)
O Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, O Lakṣmīnātha, O Lord of Prabhā, O Lord of Pārvatī and Māṇikī, bestow prosperity upon my home! 69.
Having thus prayed to the Lord of Gods, one should either put him to sleep or dismiss him;
at midday one should feed him, and likewise in the evening one should feed and worship him.
One should perform the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) for the Guru while swinging him on a swing, and likewise swing Hari—namely Bālakṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, and Harinārāyaṇa. (71)
Or he should delight her in a beautiful body of water, in a garden, or even in a palace;
and in her presence, he should have dancing, singing, and instrumental music performed.
One should indeed give gifts of food, clothing, water, flowers, and fruit;
one should feed children, holy men, and Brahmins, and offer morsels of grass to cows. ||73||
One who has not taken a vow should recite the accounts concerning Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the stories of Puruṣottama, or the narrative of the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā. 74.
One should fashion a rosary with beads named Kṛṣṇa, Hari, Kṛṣṇa, and Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, and repeatedly perform japa, worship, remembrance, and chanting. (75)
Prostration, servitude, attendance, and even the massaging of the feet; sweeping, service, and the washing of the abode of Viṣṇu. (76)
One should perform auspicious service to the guru, which nourishes the observance of vows;
for when the guru is pleased, the vow becomes complete and one's heart's desire is indeed fulfilled. //77//
This entire collection is complete and bestows heaven, liberation, and other blessings.
[It is for] Gaurīs, virtuous women, chaste wives, boys, girls, and women both married and widowed. (78)
One should feed those who are helpless and without refuge, bestow gifts upon them, and provide a home, a livelihood, a field, a garden, or a salary. ||79||
One should provide various kinds of assistance so that he may attain satisfaction;
by that, indeed, the month known as Puruṣottama shall bear fruit.
One should always offer auspicious water-born flowers to the deity in the temple, as well as uncooked grains, vegetables, salt, sugar, and so forth. || 8.1 ||
Fruits, rice, mung beans, split pulses, ghee-wicks, clarified butter, oil, wild grains, black pepper, and excellent cumin. ||82||
One should provide ginger, methikā, curd, milk, and buttermilk; as well as leaves, bhājikā, dates, and excellent surājikā. (83)
Roots of plants, almonds, pieces of wood, as well as clods of earth, bricks, bamboo vessels, metal vessels, and earthen pots; ||| 84 ||

One should provide mouthfuls of grass for the sake of cows and other animals, and even for crows and other birds; likewise, one should give grains for the sake of ants and the like, as well as flour and similar food. ||85||
At Śrī Puruṣottama, one should give chickpeas to those living in the water, cakes to dogs and other such creatures, and water to the trees and creepers. (86)
One should offer water upon Śiva for the sake of long peppers and jujubes; one should likewise present water for the sake of bilva fruits, śrīphalas, and banyan trees. (87)
One should offer water and food to the *tulasī* plants, the lotuses, and the flowering creepers as well; one should provide them with a livelihood that ensures their protection. (88)

In this manner, one should also cause gifts of garments and other articles to be given; moreover, remaining peaceful and observing celibacy while sleeping on the ground, one should do so again when [the lunar day] is increasing. ||89||

Having indeed become virtuous for a month and being endowed with vows like a virtuous woman, one should perform meritorious deeds for oneself both in this world and for supreme liberation hereafter. (1.293.90)
The husband, the wife, the female servant, the son, the daughter, and kinsmen;
the wives of kinsmen, mothers, fathers, and grandfathers. ||91||
The mother, the maternal grandmother, as well as boys and girls, disciples, sisters, dependents, guests, and those who have sought refuge [in him]. (92)
All those people in the house, one's own kinsmen, and the members of the family should indeed observe the vow during the month of Puruṣottama. ||93||
By eating once a day, or by eating only at night, or with fruit, or with food obtained unasked, or with water, milk, curd, or even with *nīvāra* grain and the like. ||94||
Having maintained their bodily sustenance even with fried vegetables, they should perform the vow of the month of Puruṣottama according to their capacity. (95)
One should perform [the rite] with a single meal, or even with food obtained through alms; or one may subsist by gleaning grains, or one may live on water alone. ||96||
Or one should consume the food of the gods in the evening after having worshipped Janārdana;
there should be constant sight of the gods and the nectar of the feet of the virtuous. ||97||
It should be drunk, worn upon the head, and likewise used for smearing the dust [on the body];
the water from the feet of Hari should always be drunk by both woman and man during the vow. (98)
One should practice reclining on a bed, the avoidance of desire and anger, the avoidance of shaving, and the avoidance of sexual intercourse. (99)
The tongue must perform austerity through renunciation of what has been acquired and earned; likewise, the man must avoid touching women, and the woman must avoid being touched by men. (1.293.10)
Indeed, during the intercalary month at Śrī Puruṣottama, one must avoid [certain activities] in every way;
one should not go outside the temple precincts, or one may go only for the purpose of visiting the sacred sites (tīrthas). || 101 ||
One should dwell in a garden, in a grove, or likewise in a field; in a forest, in a wilderness, on sacred ground, among virtuous people, and in the company of chaste women. (102)
Dwelling on ground dedicated to renunciation, or on the bank of a sacred ford, or at its boundary, or in an excellent leaf-hut, or dwelling in the open sky is considered superior. (103)
Hearing and chanting the names of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, as well as remembering Him, serving His feet, worshipping Him, and likewise bowing down to Him— 104.
One should practice devotion in the form of such activities as servitude, the offering of oneself and one's possessions, and constant contemplation of Kṛṣṇa, when impurity is predominant. 105.
This impurity (mala) takes or seizes liberation (mukti); therefore it is called *māsa*. Since illusion (*māyā*) is dissolved by this, this impurity is declared to be *māsa*. (106)
The month in which Lakṣmī measures (māti) me is therefore proclaimed as Māla;
indeed, the letter 'ma' is the final syllable of the name Puruṣottama. (107)
The first letter of Lakṣmī is dropped, leaving "Ma"; joined with Śrī, it becomes Kṛṣṇa. Hari is the washer away of impurity (mala), by whom even "Mala" is dissolved. 108.
Whatever gift or meritorious deed is performed during the intercalary month (malamāsa), its merit becomes exceedingly great; for indeed, the intercalary month is truly superior. 109.
Where Nārāyaṇa Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person, resides daily in every house and accepts auspicious worship. (1.293.110)
In this month, Śrī Puruṣottama Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is accompanied by Ramā, Lakṣmī, Pārvatī, Prabhā, and Māṇikī. 1 11.
From Goloka, from Vaikuṇṭha, and from the unmanifest abode, he indeed comes to this world for the sake of being seen by the people. 1.12.
Who perform virtuous deeds such as worship, adoration, vows, and the like;
and who, during my month, perform ritual bathing, worship, and the giving of gifts? (1.13)
In this way, the Lord always beholds from the path of the sky those devotees who perform their ablutions and offer worship to the deity of the planet. 1.14.
Beholding with divine vision those men who were givers of gifts, protectors of the observances, and beloved by people, Puruṣottama was accompanied by Śrī. (1.15)
When pleased and satisfied, Kṛṣṇa bestows his favor to perform what is beneficial, to go to one's home, and to dwell there for a long time for the sake of prosperity. 1.16.
O Lakṣmī, at my earnest request, make the dwellings of those observing the vows of Puruṣottama-māsa completely filled with every prosperity! 1.17.
May you never dwell in the house of those who despise the intercalary month;
and wherever I have no abode, may that place never be yours either. (1.18)
Having thus instructed [them], Hari, having received the food offering (naivedya) presented both in the morning and at midday, indeed returns again to his own abode.
In the evening, Hari himself returns with his own wives to each house to accept services such as the offering of lights and other honors. (1.293.120)
Having received ghee-lamps, incense, flowers, water, and excellent food—all these—he departs from his own abode once he has been bid farewell. (121)
Thus, the all-pervading Lord Śrī Hari beholds them constantly for an additional month out of compassion for his devotees; therefore, the two Lords, Śrī Puruṣottama, are worthy of worship. 1.22.

Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Duties of Vows, Austerities, Charity, Bathing, Worship, and Observances on the First Day," within the *Śrī-Puruṣottama-Māsa-Māhātmya*, in the first section concerning the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga of the *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*. 1.293.

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
O Lakṣmī! The Lord of the month of Puruṣottama is indeed a treasure-house of mercy;
I shall now tell you how he came to be known by the name Puruṣottama. 1.
Once, on the full moon day, sages likewise arrived at the hermitage of Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa for the purpose of beholding Śrī Hari.
The sages possessed of divine knowledge and masters of the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences—Patnīvat, Lomaśa, Mārkaṇḍeya, and Nārada. (3)
Vyāsa, Paila, Sumantu, Devala, Asita Kāśyapa, Jābāli, Sumati, Yājñavalkya, and Pippalāyana. (4)
Vāmadeva, Sutīkṣṇa, Parvata, Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Āpastamba, Śarabhaṅga, Kapila, Raibhya, and Āruṇi. (5)
Kātyāyana, Rathītara, Ṛbhu, Māṇḍavya, Ekata, Dvita, Trita, Agastya, Mudgala, and Kratu Gautama. (6)
Kauśika, Gālava, Babhru, Atri, Śakti, Budha, Vasu, Bodhāyana, Pṛthu, Dhūmra, Śaṅku, Saṃkṛti, and Ārtihan. || 7 ||
Kauṇḍinya, Śini, Vibhāṇḍaka, Paṅka, Dhūmapa, Jamadagni, Kaṇāda, Garga, Mauna, and Bhārgava; || 8 ||
Bharadvāja, Karkaśa, Śatānanda, Śaunaka, Viśāla, Viṣṇuvṛddha, Jarjara, Tanu, and Jaya. (9)
Pāra, Pāśadhara, Pūra, Jaṅgama, Jaimini, Makha, Uddālaka, Mahāṣeṇa, Āmalakī, and Piṅgala. (10)
Śāṇḍīraka, Prabhu, Atri, Karuṇa, Śvetaketuka, Romapāda, Kadru, Jājali, Cyavana, and Śama. (11)
Dīrghatamas, Pṛthuśravas, Śvetāśvatara Āsuri, Jaigīṣavya, Āvaṭya, Dharma, and Bharga Aiśvara. (12)
Vasiṣṭha, Marīci, Pulaha, and Pulastya—
these and thousands of others [went] to the hermitage of Nara-Nārāyaṇa.
Those most devoted to Brahman, who act for the welfare of the world and whose nature is to benefit others, arrived in the company of millions of disciples in order to behold him. (14)
Having prostrated themselves like a staff before Nārāyaṇa and proclaimed his victory, all those who had reached the further shore of the Vedas, being duly honored, sat down in his presence. (15)
And they [beheld] that Lord Nārāyaṇa—tranquil, gentle, clad in bark garments, with a serene countenance, and the refuge of the fourth puruṣārtha. (16)
[He is] an ocean of the bliss of all divine and auspicious qualities without exception;
he wears the vertical sectarian mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra), possesses divine matted hair, and is endowed with divine splendor. ||17||
Resplendent with divine necklaces and other ornaments, wearing a garland of *tulasī*, reciting the mantra of the Supreme Brahman, the garland-maker, the refuge, the infallible Acyuta. (18)
They beheld him, who had conquered his senses, whose very form was asceticism, whose face was adorned with the discus of splendor,
and who had made Badarī his entire essence, appearing as if in deep meditative absorption.
Then the gods and the ancestors likewise arrived there, as did all the rivers, sacred fords, holy sites, and forests. ||20||
Forests, cities, lakes, and likewise oceans,
as well as perfected beings and yogis, all arrived there filled with great joy.
Some were without food, some subsisted on fruits, and some on foam;
some took air, water, or leaves as their sustenance, while others subsisted on mere breath.
Desiring to see Nārāyaṇa, they attained supreme peace upon seeing him;
they all bowed down to that great sage, Nārāyaṇa. (23)
Then, seeing [the Lord] intensely focused on the Supreme Brahman, with a throbbing and abundant radiance, they all stood before Śrī Hari. ||24||
The Yugas and the Sandhyas, the years and likewise the sacrifices, as well as the months, fortnights, days, and nights, all came together. (25)
The units of time—kalās, kāṣṭhās, muhūrtas, ghaṭikās, and likewise praharas—arrived, accompanied by their masters and possessing excellent forms, like a wealthy family. ||26||
Among them, Kārttika indeed has Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa as its presiding deity,
and Mārgaśīrṣa also has Ramā-Vāsudeva as its presiding deity.
Pauṣa has the Sun known as Viṣṇu, the embodiment of the power of the solstice (saṃkrānti), as its presiding deity;
Māgha has the Moon, the victorious spring and lord of Madhu, as its presiding deity. ||28||
Phālguna has Mahārātri-lakṣmī as his presiding deity;
Caitra has Pārthivī-śakti, Sītā, and Śyāmā as his presiding deities. (29)
Vaiśākha has Hetyug-durgā and Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha as its presiding deities;
Jyeṣṭha has Gaṅgā-Mahālakṣmī and Trivikrama as its presiding deities. (30)
Āṣāḍha has Mahāvidyā Lakṣmī Vyāsa as his presiding deity;
Śrāvaṇa has Vārṣikī Dolā Ramā Kṛṣṇā as his presiding deity. ||3 1||
The month of Bhādrapada has Mahāgaurī and Vāmana-Brahmā as its presiding deities;
Āśvina has Śāradā-Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa as its presiding deities. 3.2.
In the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, they shone together with their Lord;
indeed, among them there was not even one who was unprecedented or devoid of a master. (33)
Through the greatness of their union with their respective lords, all are endowed with auspicious fortune;
they abide in their respective offices, bestowing fruits upon everyone. (34)
Thereafter, the lordless intercalary month arrived; it was redundant, like a dog's tail, and loathed by all. (35)
Dark-complexioned and filthy, deprived of food and drink, lacking both bathing and worship, he was untouchable and despised by all. (36)
There, everyone spoke to him, who was indeed helpless and loathsome:
"This intercalary month is unfit [for sacrifice], as it is devoid of the sun's transit. (37)
Unfit to be touched due to his nature as filth, he is censured in auspicious rites;
he is the dissolution of effort, the loss of gain, and one bereft of fortune. (38)
"From where has he come? Let those who possess lords keep him at a distance!
Dakṣa gave twenty-seven daughters to the Moon. (3.9)
From that, this impurity of theirs indeed arose;
it emerged in the form of their leavings, causing the three defects.
"Let this impurity, which has lasted for two and a half years, be removed.
Hearing these words of theirs, his mind was seized with anxiety.
With that burning heart, he became as if about to die;
and standing at a distance, he remained as if untouched, beholding me situated in Badarī.
Having all beheld him, they became established in meditative absorption; Māla, maintaining his composure, responded to my hand gesture. (43)
He reached the abode of Vaikuṇṭha, where I dwell and rejoice;
having arrived for the sake of my liberation, he then beheld me. (44)
Weeping with a broken heart, he fell prostrate upon the ground like a staff;
with palms joined in reverence and eyes closed, he spoke these words for his own welfare.
O Lord, ocean of compassion, bestower of refuge to the wretched!
Protect me, a miserable man who has been insulted by others and has come before you as a defiled one. 46.
O lover of the distressed, protect me—who am without a lord, defiled, excluded from auspicious rites, and forever cast out by the gods. (47)
Satyavrata, Gajendra, Dharma, Sureśvara, and the others—O Viṣṇu, protector of all, O Supreme Lord, protect me! 48.
Having spoken thus, with eyes clouded and gaze cast downward, he remained silent;
seeing him in such a state, Hari, filled with compassion, spoke.
Child! Do not be dejected; I shall rescue you, so do not grieve.
Speak your sorrow and I will dispel it; you truly ought not to lament.
One who has come for refuge to me is not destined for even a trace of suffering;
having reached the sorrowless, blissful Vaikuṇṭha, you shall no longer be a partaker of grief. 5.1.1.
Having found consolation, Malamāsa spoke, bowing to Hari:
"You are omniscient and the inner self; you know everything exactly as it is. (52)
Nevertheless, O Lord, I tell you that my suffering is equal to death;
[I count] the kalās, the kāṣṭhās, the muhūrtas, the dhaṭikās, the days, and the years. (53)
All fortnights, months, and yugas rejoice when presided over by a master;
my origin is from that which has been left overnight, from the remnants of remnants, and from the refuse of the refuse. (54)
Stain, the state of being of the nature of impurity, untouchability, disrespect, lack of ownership, humiliation, and inauspiciousness shall always belong to me. (55)
"I have no agency, no fruitfulness, and no authority anywhere, even by the sages, gods, and presiding deities who have come to the Badarī hermitage. (56)
He was reviled with insults such as "month" and the like; he was rendered untouchable, cast out, deprived of his ritual duties, threatened, and tormented in every way. (57)
Therefore, I prefer death to a wretched life;
you, however, who cannot bear the suffering of others, are a benefactor and the best of men. (58)
"O Lord, bring about my welfare; otherwise, I am a base person devoid of virtue.
I shall die, I shall die, I shall die—of this there is no doubt. (59)
Having spoken thus, he fell at the feet of Śrī Nārāyaṇa, crying:
"Protect me, protect me, O Lord of the World! Protect me, O Kṛṣṇa, O Consort of Ramā! (60)
"O Lord of Lakṣmī, O Protector, protect me who have come to you for refuge"—to him who had spoken thus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Hari whose abode is Vaikuṇṭha, [replied]. (6.1)
He said, "Arise! May it be well with you; do not grieve, look upon me.
Come together with me to the Lord, the Sovereign of Goloka. (62)
[He meditated on] Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama) situated among the multitude of gopīs, sounding his flute, two-armed, and darkly beautiful. 6.3.63.
Lotus-eyed, with a face like the full moon, he is the abode of Kandarpa;
clad in yellow garments, adorned with a forest garland and the jewel Kaustubha. 64.
His chest was anointed with sandalwood paste and adorned with a tilaka of musk; he was endowed with excellent jewel-encrusted bangles, a staff, a crown, and earrings. (65)
The ancient Supreme Person, whose chest is adorned with the Śrīvatsa mark, seated upon a lion-throne, and surrounded by hosts of cowherds and cowherdesses.
"Let us go; that Hari Kṛṣṇa will dispel your sorrow.
Having said this and taking him by the hand, Hari went to Goloka. (67)
The glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa was present along with the requisites for worship;
there were also various articles for the sake of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Rādhikā. (68)
Jewels, ornaments, garments, and household articles; delightful fragrant liquids, as well as drinks and foods. (69)
The Lord indeed brought fruits, mouth-fresheners, divine gold and other such items, and countless articles worthy of a king. (70)
Having taken him with them, they reached Goloka and Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa;
they both bathed in the Virajā river and went to Śataśṛṅga. || 71 ||
Here, the impurities of the intercalary month are destroyed by immersion in the Virajā;
indeed, for one who bathes on the second lunar day of the intercalary month, all impurities are truly removed. (72)
The merits acquired over many lifetimes will perish from their very root, yet those people who observe the vow shall attain the merit of bathing in the Virajā. ||73||

By merely bathing there, one shall attain Goloka; of this there is no doubt. Furthermore, by beholding the site of the Rāsa-maṇḍala, Vṛndāvana, and other such places, [the same result is attained]. ||74||
Having placed dust upon his head and beheld the excellent Akṣaya-bhāṇḍīra and the great Vaṭa tree, as well as the principal fortress, he entered the place inhabited by the cowherd women.
They went to the dwelling situated within the sixteen gate-towers, into the interior of the palace near Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. ||76||
Beholding that divine pair, the two of them prostrated themselves like a staff; having been honored by the two gracious ones, they bowed at their feet with both knees. ||77||
Having been duly honored, the two of them sat down on appropriate seats;
then Kṛṣṇa, out of joy, took Nārāyaṇa by the hand.
He closed his eyes, clasping his arms around his chest and pressing his chest against them, repeatedly placing Nārāyaṇa upon the lion-throne of his banner. ||79||
Endowed with laughter and serenity, the Lord made an inquiry;
then Nārāyaṇa explained the reason for his arrival. (80)
Then the Blessed Lord himself was worshipped by Nārāyaṇa; the Master, together with Rādhā, was bathed with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta). ||8 1 ||
Afterwards, the Lord was bathed with milk and then bathed with water;
he was then wrapped in a cloth and worshipped with sandalwood paste and other offerings. || 8.2 ||
Adorned with ornaments and decorated with divine garments and the like, [he is honored] with incense, lamps, *ārārtika*, circumambulations, hymns of praise, and so forth. ||83||
The Lord was honored with offerings of vessels made of gold, gems, and precious stones, and was gratified by various fruits, juices, and foods. (84)
Then Rādhikā and the other wives of Kṛṣṇa were honored with suitable turbans, and Śrī Kṛṣṇa himself was also worshipped with the power of the intercalary month (malamāsa). ||85||
Having attained grace, Māsa and Mala also received a true blessing; Śrī Kṛṣṇa, accompanied by Rādhā, spoke with favor. (86)
Just as I have been worshipped here by you on this second day, so shall I be worshipped in the world on your lunar day—the second—both at dawn and at night. (87)
Those people who worship Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa according to their ability, I shall then accept them all together with Rādhā. 88.
On the second day, the Lord, represented by a golden image, should especially be bathed with cow’s milk, or else with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) or with water. ||89||
He, together with his consort, should be adorned with gold, garments, and ornaments, as well as with substances such as sandalwood paste;
he should be embellished with the various requisites for personal adornment. (90)

He is to be worshipped with incense, lamps, and the like, as well as with bracelets, crowns, and other ornaments; he is to be gratified with sweet foods and likewise with jewel-encrusted decorations and so forth. //91//
I am to be worshipped exceedingly; I shall be satisfied in every way.
I will bestow upon them various and countless riches as my recompense, just as they exist in my world; of this there is no doubt.
And at the end, I shall grant Goloka, which is opulent and possesses eternal happiness.
Having received this blessing, even the intercalary month (malamāsa) became fortunate;
indeed, in the presence of Nārāyaṇa, it was born possessed of exceeding majesty.
Then she said to Kṛṣṇa: "O Lord, prospered by your grace, act for me in such a way that I may once again possess a master. (95)
O dispeller of the blinding darkness of ignorance, illuminator of the path of knowledge, [you who have explained] the manner of the arising and destruction of innumerable globes! 96.
O Lord of divine form, visible to those who are worthy and devoted to You;
You are worshipped with four arms bearing the conch, discus, mace, and lotus as weapons. 97.
Served by the consorts of countless Lakṣmīs, you are dark as the petal of a blue lotus, with eyes as red as a lotus. ||98||
O you whose face outshines the splendor of ten million autumnal full moons;
O you who are enchanting as the abode of the playful beauty of ten million gods of love. 99.
His chest was radiant with the Śrīvatsa mark and adorned with the shining Kaustubha gem and necklaces; he was resplendent with a crown and bracelets set with millions of excellent jewels. 100.
O Viṣṇu, O Lord Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, who brings auspiciousness to Your devotees!
Casting aside all inauspiciousness, bestow auspiciousness upon me. 101.
Thus praised, Kṛṣṇa then became pleased and spoke:
"By the recitation of this hymn, a person shall obtain a true fruit. (10.2)
Devotion to Kṛṣṇa will arise, which shall increase sons and grandsons;
there will be the destruction of ill-repute, and fame shall prevail. (103)
Whatever objects have been offered in worship, I declare that I shall bestow them upon my devotee multiplied a hundred thousandfold. 104.
On the second day of the intercalary month, I am to be worshipped by infinite beings; I shall grant whatever is desired to that seeker of the vow, even if it be infinite. (105)
Water should be given to a banyan tree, food to a virtuous brāhmaṇa,
and a garment to an excellent maiden for the sake of attaining fruits. Raw grains should also be given to a virtuous devotee of Viṣṇu.
A gift of gold should be given to one seeking knowledge and to a woman.
On the second lunar day, all auspicious gifts should indeed be given double;
one shall obtain a fruit ten million times greater both in this world and in the next.
Speaking thus, Kṛṣṇa addressed Nārāyaṇa again and again:
"O Nārāyaṇa! O Hari! O Lord of Lakṣmī! O Sun of Vaikuṇṭha! (109)
O Lord, I know the entire account of the intercalary month (malamāsa), which was explained in detail by you, the Lord of Śrī. || 110 ||
But this is an intercalary month, devoid of the sun's transit; it is impure, unfit, and excluded from auspicious rites. (111)
Thinking thus, although he was rejected by the gods of creation, he has indeed come to my house;
therefore, he is no longer impure from this day forward.
It is divine, it is perfectly pure, and it is worthy of worship in every respect;
however, let it now be considered who shall be its master here today. (113)
I am the lord of the other months as well, O Kṛṣṇa;
likewise, you too are the lord—let this be reflected upon. (1.14)
Therefore, in the thirteenth month, you have no claim of ownership over us.
For that reason, let us surely go to where Śrī Puruṣottama resides. ||115||
The Emperor of Emperors shines in the supreme, imperishable abode, from whom innumerable incarnations such as myself arise. (11.6)
Since the abodes such as Goloka are indeed portions of His own abode,
He, having reflected upon this, will conceive of Himself as its Lord.
The incarnator, however, is the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama;
whomever He shall unite with this [work], he will become its master. (118)
Having reflected thus, Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa is superior;
the three of them went to the imperishable abode where Śrī Puruṣottama resides.

Thus, in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the first section concerning the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga, in the *Puruṣottama-māsa-māhātmya* (The Greatness of the Month of Puruṣottama), regarding the arrival of sages, munis, mountains, rivers, trees, creepers, gods, years, months, and so forth at Badarikāśrama for the purpose of beholding Nara and Nārāyaṇa, when the intercalary month (*malamāsa*) was rejected due to its impurity, [the text describes] the departure of that intercalary month to Vaikuṇṭha, its journey from there to Goloka along with Nārāyaṇa, and its attainment of great fortune following the worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Rādhikā by those residing there.

Chapter Two Hundred and Ninety-Four, titled "The Departure for the World of the Imperishable Brahman (Akṣarabrahmaloka) after Receiving Blessings and Collecting [the Remains] for the Purpose of Establishing Ownership": 1.294.
← Chapter 294: Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā – Section 1 (The Lineage of the Kṛta Yuga) Chapter 295 [Author: Chapter 296 →
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, Lakṣmī! Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, and Adhimā went from Goloka by way of the divine sky in an instant. || 1 ||

Having bathed in the heart-lake of Brahman—which is the imperishable abode endowed with the mass of being, consciousness, and bliss—the three [gods], who possess the form of Puruṣottama, [emerged]. 2.
Having become so, they beheld circles of liberated souls,
each possessing two arms, being sixteen years of age, and having forms perfectly corresponding to their beauty.
Equal to ten million Nārāyaṇas in beauty, splendor, and perfect accomplishments,
they were indeed ten million times more beautiful even than Goloka.
Upon seeing those who possessed the form of the Supreme Person, their minds were drawn [toward him], and the three became filled with wonder. (5)
Having beheld the gardens and palaces made of pearls,
and having seen the celestial chariots and their furnishings, they were filled with wonder.

Having perceived the imperishable reality within his own abodes, he became dispassionate toward them; for when compared with the realities of the imperishable realm, those born of his own abodes [appeared inferior]. (7)
At that time, however, those [beings] perceived only a vast expanse appearing as if devoid of joy;
it was the very substance which had been brought from Vaikuṇṭha for the worship of Puruṣottama. || 8 ||
Or rather, all that from Goloka appeared devoid of bliss;
it was seen by them as if lacking luster, though it was the very substance of their own abode. (9)
Then, their hearts indeed broken regarding the matter of the gift, they looked about there for the lake of Brahmā. || 10 ||
Extending for infinite yojanas and consisting of divine water of exquisite taste, by bathing in which an object attains the state of being fit for enjoyment by the glorious Puruṣottama. || 11 ||
Those three, having bathed in the Brahma-lake with joy, received the offerings consecrated by him; thus, at that time, they became worthy recipients.
Then, having asked the guards and being granted entrance, they beheld a vast palace three *lakṣas* of *yojanas* in extent. || 13 ||
They entered where the king of kings, the Supreme Person, the Lord, was shining, attended by countless liberated divine beings. 1.4.
Seeing Kṛṣṇa and Nārāyaṇa arrived, the Lord Puruṣottama rejoiced exceedingly as they bowed down to him again and again. || 15 ||
He inquired after their welfare and their eternal well-being in their respective abodes.
By the grace of the Blessed One, everything is well, secure, and abundant. || 16 ||
Having spoken thus, those two, Nara and Nārāyaṇa, shone resplendently upon their seats;
even the intercalary month, having performed itself like a prostration of five staffs (pañcadaṇḍavat), [remained] indeed. || 17 ||
That supreme man stood by their side like a servant;
then the Lord of Letters questioned him in return.
"Who is this youth who has come here to my abode with you?
I think he has come for the sake of great gain, having sought refuge in one who is a protector. (19)
When the Lord of All asked thus, both Kṛṣṇa and Nārāyaṇa honored him with infinite divine gifts.
First, there was the thorough washing of the feet with the waters of the Brahma-lake;
thereafter, followed the immersion in the five nectars of divine essence.

Having consecrated the Lord of the Imperishable with waters consisting of the essence of rasa, and having properly worshipped both of them with liquid substances such as sandalwood paste, [he performed the rites]. ||22||
With joy, they presented garments, ornaments, necklaces, and the like;
as well as an umbrella, chowries, jewels, sandals, a staff, and other such items. ||23||
Finger-rings, armlets, crowns, chains, and neck-ornaments;
golden flower-earrings, garlands, girdles, bracelets, and so forth. (24)
Eatables, foods, things to be licked, and things to be sucked, mixed with sugar and honey;
food fit for eating, delicious drinks, and various items for chewing and so forth. ||25||
Then, let them offer whatever was appropriate to be presented: gold, garments, seats, vessels, divine fruits, juices, and so forth. (26)

Having performed the *ārārtrika* rite and offered hymns of praise, they sat down comfortably; having received the hospitality and honors of guests, they spoke concerning the intercalary month (*adhimāsika*).
This month is an intercalary month, a *malamāsa*, which is censured; it is forbidden by all months and by the sages for auspicious rites. (28)
Therefore, this good fortune of his was indeed bestowed by me, Kṛṣṇa;
however, without his presiding deity, he does not deserve to be counted among them. ||29||
This great suffering of his cannot be warded off except by you;
therefore, out of compassion, please make him free from fear and full of joy. (30)
"And for our sake, his suffering must be removed.
Upon hearing this, the illustrious Puruṣottama, who transcends the syllables, spoke. (3.1)
"O Kṛṣṇa, what you have done by coming here is excellent;
that Nārāyaṇa has also come here today is likewise auspicious. (32)
"By performing [this] during the intercalary month, you two shall attain fame in the world. That which was held in your hands has been taken by me into my own hand. (33)
Therefore, I shall make him equal to me, standing above all;
indeed, I shall fashion him so that he is endowed with qualities just like my own. (34)
By means of my powers, by my state of being worshipful, and likewise by my excellent valor, I make myself equal to him; what else is required beyond that? (35)
The destruction of all sins, the granting of the power of true resolve, the bestowing of the fruits of one's desires, and the conferring of similarity in form with Me. 36.
May the intercalary month be endowed with these powers: the capacity to lead one to heaven and other realms, and the quality of bestowing the state of liberation. 37.
All my other virtues have been surrendered to the intercalary month;
likewise, even my designation as "Puruṣottama" has been offered for the sake of its satisfaction. (38)
I shall indeed become its master, Brahmā, Īśa, and Puruṣottama;
by my name the entire world [shall be known], and it too shall take that name. (39)
Having shaken off his own sins, he shall become a purifier;
indeed, having become my very self, he shall be worshiped by the world.
Worthy of universal veneration, this month shall become the most excellent of all months;
for by resorting to it, people shall indeed become observers of vows, reciters of mantras, and worshippers.
By my power, they shall be givers, performers of ritual ablutions, providers of food, and even doers of some meritorious deed. (42)

And having shaken off the afflictions of suffering, poverty, heat, mental anguish, disease, and pain, [they are endowed] with happiness, prosperity, wealth, wives, offspring, and the abundance of health. ||43||
The royal palaces will become magnificent and filled with festivities, adorned with ornaments of love and provided with vessels for wine and various articles of luxury. (44)
With male and female servants, friends, attendants, and well-adorned grounds, and with security, prosperity, strength, and freedom from wretchedness, there shall be great festivals. (45)
They will be endowed with food, drink, and objects of enjoyment, with the manifestation of existence and ignorance, and with gardens, vehicles, mounts, and the like. (46)
They shall be ever resplendent with juices, tree fruits, flowers, herds of cattle, gold and silver, and with gems, jewels, diamonds, and the like. ||47||
For those who observe the vow of the month of Puruṣottama have indeed gone to me;
from me they shall obtain everything, just as people obtain [everything] from a wish-fulfilling gem. ||48||
Whether it be the celestial realm, that of Brahmā, Vairāja, or Vaiṣṇava; or that of Rudra, or the earthly realm—whatever state they deem fit, they shall attain. (49)
By observing the intercalary month, they shall obtain wives, husbands, homes, palatial mansions, virtuous sons, and the splendor of beauty—all imperishable and inexhaustible. (50)

Whether possessing desires or free from them, they shall indeed obtain their most cherished goal from this; for whether one has desires or is desireless, one becomes like me, the Supreme Person. ||5 1||
Thus, this [work] has been made a fulfiller of the desires of the people and a bestower of liberation;
just as I am complete, so too has this been made imperishable. //52//
Thus, those who possess this aspiration, or even those who are free from aspiration, shall worship their own desired deity; having attained that which they seek, they will achieve liberation. //93//
Having worshipped this [Self], the actions of those who perform rituals are reduced to ashes;
the divine, supremely pure Self shall surely attain Me, the Imperishable. (54)
Indeed, for my sake, ascetics, celibate students, the virtuous, great-souled ones, yogis, and likewise practitioners of austerity have exerted great effort. (95)
The Yoginīs, the Sāṃkhya-yoginīs, the virtuous women, the truthful ones, and likewise the widows; those free from passion and the passionate women, all of whom paid devoted homage to Nirvāṇa. ||56||
Free from delusion, likewise expounders of Brahman, and devoted to the practice of renunciation,
they strive for a thousand years, up to a thousand times a thousand.
Nevertheless, these do not go at all to my supreme, most transcendent abode;
but those devoted to Puruṣottama go to my abode within a month. ||58||
Other ascetics were peaceful, abstaining from food and free from desire; they subsisted on leaves, flowers, and fruits, or consumed nothing but water. ||59||
Subsisting on mere air, feeding on vapors, inhaling smoke, dwelling in water, and likewise enduring cold and heat; || 60 ||
With withered bodies and broken channels of the penis, they enter the apertures of the *brahma-randhra*;
though endowed with firmness in their vows, they are fit for entering the bodies of others. (61)
Indeed, without devotion to me, they do not go to my abode;
but those who observe the vow of the month of Puruṣottama are truly mine.
Those devotees of mine who observe vows shall, by my grace, reach my eternal and immortal state within a mere month. (63)
O Kṛṣṇa! O Nārāyaṇa! Therefore, this month has been placed by me at the very head for your sake, as it accomplishes all desires and goals. (64)
Those people who shall serve Śrī Puruṣottama for a month will attain the perfection of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa.
Therefore, let this month, which is the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), be served by all; it is like a most excellent field, superior for the sprouting of seeds. (66)
The Supreme Person bestows merit a crore-fold in reward;
those who perform the Cāturmāsya sacrifice, having enjoyed its fruits in heaven, return once more [to this world]. (67)
Those who sacrifice for the Supreme Person go to the imperishable and eternal state;
he rescues seven hundred and seven generations of his lineage. (68)
One who observes vows in other months certainly does not transcend rebirth;
however, one who observes vows in my month indeed does not undergo rebirth again. //69//
In this month, I myself dwell here as the presiding deity;
therefore, its name was made after mine, for I am indeed identical with it.
I shall fulfill the desires of all those who take refuge in him;
I shall never count their offenses, for they are his devotees in every respect. (71)
In comparison with my own devotion, my devotion is dear to me;
there shall be no delay in fulfilling the desires of those who are devoted to me for even a single month. (72)
Excluding my devotee alone, I fulfill the desires of all others;
indeed, I grant everything to them because they sacrifice for me month after month.
They indeed are very dear to me, even more so than millions of liberated souls;
for having reached my month, they are freed from the need for recitation, charity, and other such rites. (74)

Those who are devoid of ritual bathing and worship, who obstruct virtuous deeds, and who have abandoned the construction of wells, tanks, ponds, and other works of public utility (pūrta), as well as sacrifices (yajña). ||75||
Those who hate deities, sacred fords, the twice-born, holy men, virtuous women, and temples, and who are revilers, shall become eaters of crow-dung. (76)
Those who revile the unfortunate shall become lepers like dogs and jackals, left without any refuge; for such revilers, there shall be no happiness by day or by night. (77)
Those lowest of men who cause suffering to those observing vows during my month shall become fierce donkeys, bound by the nooses of others' beatings. (78)
Those who revile my month, those who are defilers of the Dharma, and those envious ones who create obstacles on this path of devotion—[may they be destroyed]. (79)
But those who, having reached Puruṣottama in every third year, will become tree-juice-drinkers and gluttons. (80)
Those who do not perform what is for their own spiritual welfare shall go to my abode;
having become intensely miserable here, pervaded by the fire of the bonds of suffering. (8.1)
The giver of fortune (Śrīda) is the bestower of prosperity; therefore, he is the granter of victory over death.
This month of mine, Puruṣottama, must not be spent in vain. || 82 ||
Maidens and young women, both married and unmarried, co-wives, elderly women, those who are fortunate as well as those who are unfortunate—(all these should be honored). || 83 ||

Those who, for the sake of attaining their own desired goals, shall perform vows, give gifts, and worship me during my month—whether they are currently unhappy or even very happy—[shall attain their desires]. (84)
I am the Lord Puruṣottama, the bestower of all things—bathing, garlands, service to the gods, and whatever other meritorious deeds there may be. (85)
I bestow righteousness, desire, as well as wealth, happiness, and liberation;
I grant food, the power of digestion, the capacity for sexual pleasure, and an excellent husband.
I grant sons, grandsons, male and female servants, and whatever else is desired;
I become the bestower of happiness upon one's brothers, fathers, and kinsmen. ||87||
O Supreme among Men, for those women by whom my month has been made empty, may all their [good fortune] become empty and their true prosperity pass into voidness. 88.
Those wealthy householders who spend their month in vain without performing acts such as giving charity to me—by that, my treasury shall fall into emptiness. (89)
If those who follow the path of renunciation—namely, the celibate students, forest-dwellers, and ascetics—should spend even a single month without devotion, [they fall from their state]. || 90 ||
Indeed, even all those ascetics become devoid of liberation;
likewise, Śūdras, women, and the classes of servants [attain it] by [worshipping] Śrī Puruṣottama. (91)
If they pass their time without serving the Guru and the God, they too shall be bereft of prosperity and afflicted by suffering and poverty. (92)
The guru is to be served, Hari is to be served, and parents and other elders are to be served;
the cow is to be served, the husband is to be served, and the devoted wife is to be served, just as I am. 93.
"Wherever I may abide, I shall grant the fruit in every way;
therefore, Śrī Puruṣottama is to be served by all with their whole being. (94)
One should strive for one's own spiritual welfare through righteousness and devotion, which lead to liberation;
however, widowhood and the state of being a widower do not bring about the arrival of the intercalary month (malamāsa). 95.
"O months of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, listen certainly to my words! By my command, those worlds that indeed exist within the cosmic egg—wherever this month exists, there also [is] mine. (96)
They will worship me, the very essence of the sacred seat, in every way. (97)
Those devotees of mine shall attain my eternal abode, the imperishable Goloka, Vaikuṇṭha, or even the immortal realm of Īśvara. ||98||
By my power, through the influence of this month, those various devotees shall go to that supreme abode according to their respective desires, by means of your compassion. (99)
On the third lunar day of my month, I have been worshipped by you both;
likewise, for those who shall worship me [on that day], their desires will be fulfilled. (100)
By means of bathing, giving gifts, recitation of mantras, and other such acts, everything will certainly come to pass;
O Lakṣmīśa, O Rādhikeśvara, do not harbor any anxiety. 101.
"Having taken Puruṣottama, go each to your own respective world. Having received this command and bowed down, those three departed. (102)
Listen, Lakṣmī! Those who bathe in abundant waters on the third lunar day obtain the same merit as bathing in the Brahmahrada and the Brahmasarovara. (10.3)
Indeed, the merit that would result from performing a ritual bath shall accrue to them,
as well as the merit of my worship performed by those two and whatever was offered there.
Likewise, those people who shall perform worship for me during this month and shall also bestow gifts, their merit shall become eternal. (105)
Since worship was performed by those two for me on the third lunar day, human beings also ought to perform a great worship on the third lunar day. (106)
A grand worship of Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, and Puruṣottama should be performed, which bestows happiness, liberation, and other blessings. (107)
Just as I am in the abode of Brahman, so too am I another, consisting of the month;
I exist in every way within the cosmic egg, and likewise I am situated within the heart.
I am Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, served by Rādhā, Lakṣmī, and others;
I know everything, whereas others do not know me in such a way. (109)
I sport with the radiance of Pārvatī as if with a ruby;
know, O lady of my body, that though I am manifold in form, I am truly one. (11.0)

Thus, in the first section on the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga within the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā, concerning the majesty of the month of Puruṣottama, [this describes] the departure of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa and the intercalary months to the imperishable abode; following the bath in the Brahma-hrada and Brahma-sarovara lakes, the approach to the presence of Śrī Puruṣottama, His worship, and the offering of one's own self; the subsequent attainment by the intercalary month of the sovereignty and the name "Puruṣottama"; and the description of the fruits of worship, charity, and other rites performed on the third lunar day, regarding the months of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
Chapter Two Hundred and Ninety-Five: The Description of the Return to Their Respective Abodes, etc.
