Chapter 297 → Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, Lakṣmī! Then all three of them, having gone to Goloka, rested for a moment; thereafter, Kṛṣṇa was worshipped by the two of them. (1)
The greatness of Puruṣottama manifested in many ways in Goloka;
having bowed to Kṛṣṇa, Nara and Nārāyaṇa departed for Adhomāsa.
Then, even there in Vaikuṇṭha, Hari established the greatness of the month and caused the month of Puruṣottama to dwell there as well. (3)
Having attained his residence, even for a month he delights with Viṣṇu;
having become the lord of the months, he remains established in dignity.
Then, having been honored here with great respect by Mahālakṣmī,
he was likewise quickly honored by Nārāyaṇa throughout every single universe.
And on the afternoon of the third day, having dispatched his own attendants, he proclaimed:
"This most excellent intercalary month has indeed been announced."
He is named Puruṣottama, having Puruṣottama as his presiding deity;
by Puruṣottamanātha, he was made the bestower of heaven and the bestower of liberation.

Indeed, his own virtues have been offered to him, for he is not inferior to the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama) in worship, salutation, recitation, giving, bathing, or even in the observance of vows. (8)
This bestower of the yoga of Puruṣottama is equal to Puruṣottama himself;
whether they be men or women, gods or goddesses, or even those that are stationary or moving. (9)
By my will, they shall perform the vow and the worship of the intercalary month with all its constituent parts, both in spirit and at the same time.
They shall obtain everything they desire; this I, Nārāyaṇa, declare.
What then need be said regarding this vow when performed throughout the three periods of time? || 11 ||
"Regarding the monthly vow, however, nothing at all remains to be told by me.
Therefore, one should worship [the deity] once, twice, or three times a day. (12)
A woman shall obtain her desire, and a man likewise shall attain his wish;
whether for a moment, half a moment, or an hour, in the evening, at dawn, or at midday. || 13 ||
This Supreme Person, Nārāyaṇa, is to be worshipped according to one's ability and according to the available materials; I speak this here with the Supreme Person as my witness. (14)
And in this month named Puruṣottama, they shall worship me with devotion for even a single moment, with Śrī Kṛṣṇa as their witness. (15)
They shall attain heaven, the realm of Śiva, and whatever else they desire;
they shall reach me, the ocean of bliss, the Supreme Brahman, higher than the highest. (16)
Those who here, by the will of Nārāyaṇa, shall worship with devotion, will indeed attain me, Nārāyaṇa, who resides in Vaikuṇṭha. (17)
Those who, by the will of the illustrious Kṛṣṇa, worship me here with devotion, shall indeed attain me, Mādhava, who resides in Goloka. 1.8.
Those people who, desiring the Supreme Person, shall worship me when I have gone to the abode of Brahmā, will surely attain me, the Supreme Person. (19)
Whatever form of me embodied beings here worship, they shall obtain that very form of me in each respective case. (20)
Thus, O Lakṣmī, it was proclaimed again and again throughout the cosmic eggs by the messengers and attendants of divine form with great kettledrums. ||21||
On the night of the third lunar day of the intercalary month, he was indeed honored, worshipped, and properly fed by many millions [of beings], yet he experienced great exhaustion. ||22||
On the fourth day, however, at dawn, he was exceedingly gratified by the inhabitants of the two worlds of the seven [sages] through ritual bathing, vows, worship, charity, and other such acts. (23)
Many immobile beings as well as sentient ones who observed vows gathered at the abode of Hari by the hundreds of thousands and tens of millions.
On the morning of the fourth day,
however, Goddess Ramā, accompanied by ten million maidservants and traveling in a celestial chariot, arrived from the ocean of nectar at Vaikuṇṭha.
Having assumed the form of a young bride and adorned with a bridegroom’s garland, she was equal to Lakṣmī in every limb, lacking not even in the slightest degree. ||26||
By the command of Nārāyaṇa, she was duly honored by Lakṣmī and the others; then, having been welcomed by Nārāyaṇa himself, she was seated upon his lap. (27)
Upon seeing that, Lakṣmī and the others were indeed struck with wonder:
"How is it that she, in the form of a wife, was so quickly accepted by her husbands? (28)
Then Lakṣmī was questioned by Ramā to learn the details of those events:
"How and from where have you come, and how did Nārāyaṇa become your husband? (29)
Whose daughter is she, how was she obtained, and having done what did you bring this Narayana?
O fair-browed sister, tell me everything; it must be related for the sake of ultimate happiness. (30)
Having been fed and honored by Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa as well,
she indeed began to relate her own story exactly as it had happened.
Having offered the garland of choice upon the neck of Hari, she stood before him;
having drunk the water from the big toe of Nārāyaṇa and performed a circumambulation. ||36||

Having fashioned a beautiful crescent moon on her forehead with saffron and rice grains, and having placed half of the bridegroom’s garland around her own neck, she then [offered] milk-rice (pāyasa). ||33||
Having fed Hari and given him betel-leaf as his gracious gift, he himself took a handful of flowers upon the lap of Nārāyaṇa. ||34||
Having offered fresh rice and parched grain while standing upon her seat, she, having become his wife, spoke these words: "Listen, Lakṣmī! To this joyous declaration. (35)
While all the male devotees and female devotees were listening, Ramā said:
"O Mahālakṣmī, who are worthy of my worship! During the movement of the third night... (36)
O Dundubhi, you who are well-known by all as Nārāyaṇa, I shall fulfill the desires of the worshipper during the intercalary month. (37)
Even I, as a maiden in the home of the Ocean of Milk, heard of him; and I desired Nārāyaṇa, the Lord and husband of Lakṣmī, as my husband. (38)
On the third day of the intercalary month, having observed the vow without food and without water in the evening, and having bathed, I worshipped Lord Hari. ||36||
Having consulted my father and the Ocean of Milk, and by his command,
he constructed a pavilion adorned with plantain pillars and leafy archways.
And having had a beautiful and most splendid swing constructed in the middle of that [courtyard], he should place there a golden image of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, resplendent with jewels. (41)
Having bathed [the deity] with all the oceanic waters, having worshipped with devotion using jewels,
and having adorned [him] with divine garments, ornaments, and unguents, etc., ||42||
Having worshipped with incense, lamps, foods, and drinks, and having saluted with the waving of lights, hymns of praise, and circumambulations; ||43||
Having offered a handful of flowers and again made a mental resolve:
"O Soul of the Universe, O Nārāyaṇa, become my husband for the sake of Ramā! (44)
Having thus offered praise and drunk the nectar of his feet, Śrī Hari was lovingly laid to sleep by me upon a very soft couch. (45)
Having meditated upon Him while asleep, I then serve Hari; thus I am observed [by Him], thinking, "I am massaging His feet. (46)
For a moment in my dream, Hari was seen by me upon my own bed; smiling, he seemed to draw me toward him with his side-long glance out of affection. (47)
"O Ramā! Having heard your words, I accept you as my beloved by means of this vow.
O dear one, I shall return again in the morning to lead you to my world. (48)
Having thus quickly made himself heard, he vanished from sight;
this very Lord Nārāyaṇa, the husband of Lakṣmī, now shines forth. (49)
When Nārāyaṇa had departed during the muhūrta known as Brāhma, on the fourth day of the intercalary month, I meditated upon this Puruṣottama. ||50||
Having bathed and having bathed the Lord who is upon the bed with great devotion using milk and other substances as well as water, and having rubbed him with sandalwood paste and the like; ||51||
Having presented him with auspicious ornaments, he was honored like a bridegroom;
and a highly valuable yellow garment and a yellow body-protector were bestowed upon him. ||52||
A cloak richly adorned with golden stars, as well as an excellent upper garment;
a golden crown upon his head, a necklace on his chest, and earrings in his ears. (53)
A *tilaka* mark and a crescent moon on the forehead, collyrium on the eyes and the eyebrows, sandalwood paste as dots on the cheeks, and a tiny crescent moon on the chin; ||54||
A covering of flowers upon the forehead, an excellent garland around the neck, golden necklaces upon the chest, and auspicious bracelets on the hands. (55)
There are rings on the fingers, bracelets on both arms, garlands of *tulasī* flowers, and a golden sword in his hand. (56)
In her hand she held a coconut fruit, and around her waist was a girdle;
on her feet were golden anklets and auspicious sandals. ||57||
The fruit of desire is indeed in the forearm; auspicious milk-rice is in the food;
betel-leaf, drinking water, and the juicy grape are the fruits. ॥58॥
Then follows the gift of betel nut, the sacrificial fee consisting of an excellent garland, and one hundred and eight oblations with clarified butter into the circle of fire. (59)
Perform the nightly lamp-offering with five wicks and four circumambulations.
You are the most excellent, the granter of boons; be my chosen one, O you of truthful speech. (60)

An offering of handfuls of flowers, as well as the arghya water, prostration, the request for forgiveness, the dismissal [of the deity], the drinking of the water from the feet, and the consumption of the remnants. ||61||
Meditation upon what was seen in the dream, the anticipation of when [he] would arrive, and the most joyful worship with the name Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. 62.
He gave food to the young girls and also to the maidens;
his meditation was fixed upon Nārāyaṇa, and his body resided in the house that is the Ocean of Milk. ||63||
"The eyes are in the sky, on the supreme path; the Self resides in the dweller of Vaikuṇṭha.
When Hari is thus worshipped, enriched with his retinue, during the intercalary month (adhimāsa), [the fruit is obtained]. ||64||
Having bowed to my father and partaken of a small amount of milk as a meal,
while I remained in his abode, this very Nārāyaṇa appeared.
He appeared before me, resplendent with a form corresponding to his nature;
gracious and exceedingly radiant, he indeed touched me with his hand.
Drawing me close to him, he said to me, "Come here;
for on the third lunar day of the intercalary month, you have worshipped me at this very time. (67)
"O venerable lady, having been well-served by you at night and highly honored on the fourth day, I have indeed been won over by your vow this very morning. (68)
O fair-browed one, since I have been worshipped by you today through your meditation, I have attained [my goal], O auspicious one! You are my fortunate beloved! (69)
Come together with me; you have become my eternal bride. By virtue of your vow, all these maidservants of yours shall also come to my house. (70)
"Let my handmaidens come; I shall delight in them in every way.
Having thought thus, the excellent one revealed his own form as Garuḍa. (71)
Whatever vehicles and conveyances there are here by the thousands, all of that has been reported by me to my father after approaching him. (72)
He too, having arrived there, placed me in the hand of Hari;
having fulfilled her duty by the command of her father, she mounted the bird.
Sent forth by her father with an army and preceded by honors,
she returned to the city of Hari, having taken along her dowry.
This very Nārāyaṇa has been seen here in this palace; behold, O beautiful lady, he is present right here with me! (75)
By the fruit of this worship performed at night and at dawn during an intercalary month, I have indeed obtained a virtuous husband, Nārāyaṇa, and have come here to meet him. ||76||
She was led by that very Kṛṣṇa and brought into his embrace;
she was made a new bride and a wife, a resident of Vaikuṇṭha. ||77||
"I am Ramā, your friend and servant, always desiring your grace;
thus, O sinless one, have I obtained the fruit of this intercalary month. (78)
Just as I have performed the worship of Nārāyaṇa, so shall she do;
whether she be a maiden or a young woman, she shall obtain this very Nārāyaṇa. (79)
Having worshipped Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa in every way during an intercalary month (adhimāsa), [one should do so] specifically on the fourth lunar day, either in the morning, at midday, or at midnight. ||80||
In whatever manner they shall worship him, he will fulfill their desires accordingly:
wealth, sons, happiness, a wife, a husband, grain, and a noble home.
Vehicles, mounts, splendor, beauty, and supreme sovereignty; a kingdom, status, a beloved wife, male servants, female servants, and all forms of wealth. ||82||

Objects of enjoyment connected with pleasure, foods to be eaten and drinks to be drunk in infinite variety, divine substances situated in their true essence, and delights according to one's desire—[these he experienced]. (83)
The worlds of heaven devoted to truth, the abodes of Parameṣṭhin, as well as the Vairāja realms, the grounds of Vaikuṇṭha, and the grounds of Dhenubhūmi; ||84||
Those who worship Nārāyaṇa indeed conceive of Goloka, the imperishable, and whatever is divine as well as non-divine, during the intercalary month. (85)
Men, women, and the gods and goddesses dwelling on the fourteen levels shall all obtain their desired objects through the longing for Puruṣottama. (86)
O Lakṣmī! Just as I have become eternal through very little effort, so too shall another woman become possessed of great good fortune. (87)
Even if a woman who is a widow should worship Kṛṣṇa like me during the intercalary month, she will certainly attain Vaikuṇṭha. (88)
Having obtained Nārāyaṇa as her husband, she shall always be possessed of good fortune, even if she is old, diseased, or despised by her kinsmen. (89)
She who has fallen away from her duty through her own actions, who is possessed by remorse,
who is helpless, alone, destitute, a widow, and an unchaste woman— (90)
Whether she be a wanton woman or a lustful one who has consorted with anyone at all—
deprived of kinsmen, devoid of vows, and engaging in union with beasts— (9.1).
Always greedy for the pleasure of the tongue, consuming liquor, meat, and the like—how much more so?
She is a locus of defects such as menstruation and the like, and is established in the defect of caste-confusion. ||92||
Whether she be a woman who has taken refuge with outcasts and the like and is devoid of proper refinement, or one who possesses the application of auspicious refinements; (93)

Having heard this narrative and performed the vow during the intercalary month according to one's capacity, with the desire for the attainment of Hari, one should observe eating once a day, eating only at night, or eating food unasked. (94)
Even after consuming fruits and drinking milk by the power of Śrī Hari, she, being exceedingly purifying, wiped away all sins and even the most heinous crimes. (95)
Whether she be a courtesan, a female entertainer, a dancer, a jester, a procuress, or a beautician, she becomes a purifier of the assembly. (96)
Whoever she may be in this world, having become one whose form is pure, she becomes like gold, being both the field of Viṣṇu and the object of his compassion. (97)
Divine, pure, free from sin, and endowed with a mass of merit, she was rendered exceedingly purified by the grace of Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, and Viṣṇu. || 98 ||
Having purified his own kin as well as others through his association,
he shall go to that eternal, supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
"I, Lakṣmī, am ever established on the lap of Nārāyaṇa;
O Lakṣmī, I tell you the truth once more: she shall attain the abode of Hari. (100)
One who is a eunuch or like a eunuch, or a woman who is a eunuch or resembles a eunuch; one who is without menses, or mentally deranged, or like a female monkey, having fallen from her vows. 101.
Whoever she may be, by performing this vow during the month at Śrī Puruṣottama, she shall attain the boon of Nārāyaṇa. (10.2)
Whether one is free from desire or has attained liberation through freedom from desire, one will certainly reach the divine abode of Hari’s imperishable syllable; of this there is no doubt. (103)
What more need I say? Even illusion itself would become non-illusory through its union with him; so what then to speak of women attaining liberation? 104.
Therefore, the vow of the intercalary month must be performed by all means;
for by its power, one may attain everything—enjoyment, liberation, and likewise heaven. (106)
"And I am staying here, O eldest sister! Look upon me with favor. Having spoken thus, she prostrated before Lakṣmī, who increases affection. (106)
Nārāyaṇa also led her to his palaces;
he delighted her with her cherished desires and fulfilled her aspirations.
"In this way, O beloved! how did Ramā become the beloved of Nārāyaṇa?
This story of her being the daughter of the Ocean of Milk has been told to you. (108)
By merely hearing, reciting, and worshipping this, a person shall obtain the fruit arising from the vow of the intercalary month. || 109 ||

Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Residence in Vaikuṇṭha for Nārāyaṇa and the Adhimāsa, the Proclamation by Drumbeat in the Cosmic Eggs for the Purpose of the Vow of the Adhika-māsa, and how, upon hearing that, Rāmā, the daughter of the Ocean of Milk, attained the status of Nārāyaṇa’s consort in Vaikuṇṭha by performing the vow, worship, and other rites on the evening of the third lunar day and the morning of the fourth," in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the first section, the *Kṛta-yuga-santāna*, concerning the majesty of the month of Puruṣottama.

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī! To the auspicious story of Śāradā;
having performed the vow and worship on the fifth day of the intercalary month (adhimāsa). || 1 ||
She attained incomparable sovereignty and eternal maidenhood,
as well as freedom from menstruation and the ability to extend her mouth at will.
Thus Śāradā attained the divine and imperishable status of wife to the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, and she received worship in the world just as the lotus-born goddess did.
While she possesses the state of being a wife, she maintains her maidenhood; while she is a virgin, she possesses the status of a bride.
This coexistence of two contradictory attributes in her arises from pleasing Śrī Hari.
O Lakṣmī, listen to this greatly meritorious story concerning the month of Puruṣottama, which is filled with wonders and endowed with the power of the intercalary month. 5.
Abiding in the abode of Brahman, the beautiful Śāradā, known as Brahmavidyā, manifested from the body of the beginningless Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (6)
Having come to the world of Vairāja by the command of Nārāyaṇa, she attained absorption into Vairāja along with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara. || 7 ||
That maiden, born together [with him], was Vairājī, the daughter of Śarada;
for a long time, the young girl resided in her father’s house. (8)
Consisting of the knowledge of Brahman, she eternally investigates the body—that purpose for which I, as a deity, was manifested by Brahmā. (9)
Indeed, in the creation of the Creator, [my] verbal form stands face-to-face with him;
therefore, if I were to go among the creations having become a creation of the Creator, [I would be lost]. 10.
If I, as a maiden, were to dwell here—impure and unconsecrated—I would indeed become untouchable and forever excluded by all. (11)
At that time, death alone shall be my refuge there;
for the body of a young girl, being in the womb, is indeed sinful.
It is indeed suitable for a certain kind of karma, but not for all;
this [being], born from the urinary organ and generative faculty, has grown within the bladder and the womb. (13)
Immersed in the water consisting of urine, he emerged through the urinary passage;
even in childhood, his nature was composed of filth and urine, covered by impure and untouchable waste. (14)
A body devoid of the purificatory rite of the sacred thread (yajñopavīta) is always impure;
it consists of a foul mass of transformations such as impure phlegm and fat. (15)
While a girl remains unmarried, how could her female body be auspicious? Purity is attained through marriage; otherwise, it never occurs. (16)
Even marriage brings great suffering, as does subjection to a man;
there is the performance of impure acts while dependent upon the organ of excretion. (17)
Residence in the womb occurs within the urinary bladder; there is birth from the womb and being smeared with impurities.
In all cases of distress, there is the discharge of blood accompanied by filth. (18)
The production of excrement and urine, the movement of the downward-voiding wind, and impurity in every respect arise in the state of wifehood during the act of sexual intercourse. (19)
Therefore, the state of being dependent on another as a wife causes excessive suffering.
What should be done? Where should one go? For a woman has been made dependent on another. (20)
The female body is dependent on others, to be enjoyed by others, and exists for the sake of others;
he who has committed such a sin attains the state of womanhood. (21)
Therefore, I must not become dependent on another woman;
for such is the nature of a woman in her courses: it brings about impurity and causes sin. (22)
I shall not be subject to that dependence by which even that [which is desired] is not obtained;
if what is desired by me does not come to pass, I shall die, without a doubt. (23)
Freedom from impurity, purity, and the absence of menstruation, as well as being devoid of the duties of a wife, just as in my own maidenhood. (24)
"Since effort must be made so that it may become eternal, one should act accordingly from now on.
Thinking thus constantly, she sought the means for its attainment. (25)
He heard the drum of Viṣṇu for the sake of the vow of the intercalary month;
indeed, the desires of those observing the vow of Puruṣottama-māsa [were fulfilled]. (26)
The illustrious Puruṣottama said: "They shall become perfected;
people will worship me once a day or twice a day. (27)
Whether he be a man, a woman, or a eunuch, by a mere fragment of my compassion, he shall indeed obtain that which is difficult to attain; I shall grant him everything he desires. (28)
Having heard the proclamation, the maiden Śāradā, daughter of Vairāja, was filled with great joy and set her mind upon the performance of the vow. (29)
On that fifth lunar day, having risen very early in the morning upon hearing the sound of the drum,
she bathed and likewise meditated upon the form of Hari.
Having gathered divine articles of worship in his own abode, he worshipped the god Viṣṇu, Nārāyaṇa, with devotion. || 3.1 ||
Having invoked Lakṣmī, Nārāyaṇa, Śrī Hari, Puruṣottama, and gold,
and having spread out a seat, [he offers] water for the feet, the arghya offering, and water for sipping.
Having offered these and bathed Kṛṣṇa with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), with water, with the essence of nectar, and with fragrant liquid substances; ||33||
Then, having massaged his body in many ways, he prepared himself for adornment; having put on his ornaments and decorations, as well as his garments. (34)
Having worshipped with musk, sandalwood, unbroken rice grains, and saffron, and having fully honored [the deity] with *tulasī* flowers, *mandāra*, and *campaka* blossoms; ||35||
Having gratified [the deity] with incense, lamps, excellent food offerings, fruits, drinks, and chewables, as well as with betel leaves, he then performed the *ārārtika* ceremony.
Having performed circumambulation and praise, she prostrated like a staff;
that young maiden asked for forgiveness for her offense and prayed for her desired wish. (37)
O Lord Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, worthy of being proclaimed by the celestial drum;
O Śrī Puruṣottama, dweller in Brahmaloka, Goloka, and Vaikuṇṭha! 38.
"You grant whatever is desired to your devotee who performs vows;
therefore, grant it to me likewise, so that I may choose it. (39)
May my maidenhood be eternal, and may I never experience menstruation;
likewise, even though [these things exist], may there be no impurity for me. (40)
May husbandhood, which is most auspicious and brings good fortune, be mine forever;
and may I never experience pregnancy, even while remaining a wife. (41)
I beg this which is indeed difficult to obtain, even though it is entirely contrary to your body;
for you are a speaker of truth, having undertaken a vow for a single lifetime. (42)
"If you give when the intercalary month has been honored, then give it to me likewise;
otherwise, O Lord, do not sound the drum with falsehood. (43)
O Lord, I give you a parasol; I also give you two chowries.
I present you with sandals and I give you a soft bed. (44)
I offer myself, surrendered for the purpose of massaging Your feet;
O protector of those who seek refuge, You who fulfill the desires of Your devotees! 45.
Accept this handful of flowers, or take my hand—or do not;
O Lord, grant me that which I have requested, for it is indeed eternal and bestows happiness. (46)
A maiden shall not be a wife, nor shall a wife be a maiden;
lest many faults regarding the state of being a wife should touch me. (47)
O Lord of Compassion, if the drum is indeed true to its purpose, grant that no faults whatsoever may touch me even in my maidenhood. (48)
O Lord, for you who have the power to do, not do, or even do otherwise, there is nothing whatsoever that is impossible; otherwise, your drum would be in vain. (49)
Having thus offered praise and presented an *arghya* accompanied by fruits to Viṣṇu,
the maiden Śāradā then caused him to prosper with unbroken grains (*akṣata*).
Having offered the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) consisting of her own self-offering into the heart of the God, she dismissed him while meditating upon Nārāyaṇa. ||5.1||
Then Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Lakṣmī, the illustrious Puruṣottama, the husband of Ramā, appeared before them, smiling gently. (52)
With his right hand granting fearlessness and touching [her] on the head with his left, he said, "O Śāradā, what is in your mind? Make it known. (53)
I am pleased with your worship, O lady who observes the vow of trust. O fair-browed one, I am forever bound by you with the noose of confidence. (54)
I am capable of giving you everything; nevertheless, listen to my words:
the state of being a maiden and the state of being a wife are never seen together in one person anywhere. (55)
Therefore, choose one of these two; I shall grant it to you:
either maidenhood for Kalaka in this world, lasting as long as life endures, ||56||
Therefore, choose here the status of being my wife, which bestows good fortune; I shall grant it to you.
Furthermore, O maiden, choose whatever else you desire, and I shall give it to you as well. ||57||
"I shall grant you either a kingdom ruled by women, a great kingdom, or a kingdom of illusion. Do not choose anything contrary [to my intent], O maiden; speak after due reflection, do not delay. (58)
Having heard these words of Hari, Śāradā said to Keśava:
"O Lord, fulfiller of the desires of your devotees, I have requested this because of your renown. (59)
For the sake of protecting your own truth, do as you wish;
for there should be no insistence toward a devotee, and one who possesses devotion is not one to insist.
I have sought refuge in you; O Lord, remove the anxiety of your devotee.
I am yours, I am your devotee, fallen at your feet. (6.1)
"May women not suffer miseries; grant the desires of your devotees.
Thus entreated, seen, touched, bowed to, and honored with reverence— ||62||
Honored there, fed, and gazed upon with exceeding love, the Lord, the remover of the distress of his devotees, reflected for the sake of his own devotee: 63.
"How might her heart's desire be granted?
And by what means could her wish also be fulfilled? (64)
I grant her this great accomplishment (siddhi), which takes the form of both the pervaded and the pervader; indeed, I grant her this divine accomplishment that manifests in manifold forms.
Having thus resolved, the Blessed One placed the water from the conch in her mouth;
at that moment, she indeed became the embodiment of all powers.
Then the Blessed One said: "O Śāradā, my wife is of the nature of Śāradā; she possesses a divine form and always dwells in Vaikuṇṭha. (67)
Contemplate that you are free from defects such as those of the womb;
the state of being my wife has been bestowed upon you, devoid of any impurity of birth. (68)
May your divine form, untouched by excrement, urine, and the like, be yours forever.
Now, O beloved, accept your second form, which consists of speech. (69)
I grant you such a form as that of Sarasvatī herself, endowed with the state of maidenhood and delicate; thus become.
Go, in that very form, through the gateway of the Vedas among living beings;
let your pervasive form exist in the form of speech in every mouth. (71)
O Śāradā, may maidenhood always abide in you there within your own nature;
and may you remain free from menstruation while your activity is directed inward.
May your virtuous nature and maidenhood always remain so for you;
now, indeed, by some pretext in a third form— || 73 ||
O Sarasvatī, you who flow within the waters in the form of a river, free from dust and ever youthful, may you remain forever present in this autumn season. (74)
May there be no restlessness, nor outwardness, nor the nature of passion (rājasva) in you; may you always possess purity and be free from the seasonal flow of bodily functions. ||75||
O Āśārada! Your menstruation has dissolved, devoid of the state of impurity;
may no impurity whatsoever ever exist in you. (76)
Possessing all sovereignty, worthy of worship, and pervasive throughout the worlds, may you be so; O Sarasvatī, may there be no Rajasic sin among people in you! 77.
If, while you exist externally, menstruation and the like were seen to be produced by the world, then that defect would belong to the worlds, but not to you. (78)
May the sin committed during menstruation belong to those who speak [of it], and may there be perpetual purity for you; may you possess divine riches. (79)
May you possess both maidenhood and the state of being a wife, pure and as desired;
you are my wife Śāradā, a maiden and a daughter of Brahmā.
"Everything has been given by me to you; tell me, what else do you desire?
Thus addressed, that goddess said: "As for those who perform my worship... (8.1)
May those who worship Sarasvatī—the goddess Śāradā, the river, and speech—attain Vaikuṇṭha through the majesty of their Lord. (82)
Having worshipped Nārāyaṇa in due order on the morning of the fifth day of the intercalary month, I have attained my heart’s desire in its entirety. (83)
Likewise, let those who worship you and those who worship the intercalary month—men and women alike—come to your feet in Vaikuṇṭha. ||84||
It is free from birth, death, old age, disease, suffering, and poverty; it is eternal, adorned with the embodiment of the mass of existence, consciousness, and bliss. 85.
"So be it," he said, making the sound of a celestial drum resonate, [thereby] making the intercalary month meaningful, yielding the fruit of truth, and bestowing prosperity. (86)
Adhimāsa also said to her: "Those who are devoted to me and to you—I, indeed, am Puruṣottama, the deliverer of both those men and those women. (87)
I shall indeed become the remover of defects, the bestower of happiness, the granter of the heart's desires, the purifier, and the giver of perfection; of this there is no doubt. (88)
Those who, having made this prayer to Śāradā, shall hear what is difficult to obtain, or shall read it, for them that which is difficult to obtain shall become easy to attain. (89)
That which is inconceivable becomes well-conceived; that which is unattainable comes to be attained;
that which is impossible becomes possible; and even the undesirable turns into the desired. (90)
On earth, in heaven, or elsewhere, that which is difficult to attain becomes easily obtained;
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is directly attainable—what need is there to speak of anything else? 9.1.
Nārāyaṇa indeed bestows much upon him through his own grace;
for he grants the merit of that which was performed during an intercalary month here as an incalculable fruit. ||92||
O you who have attained fortune! Just as [the temple] of the goddess Śāradā is wonderful, so too does the worshipper obtain wonderful worldly enjoyment and liberation. (93)
Recitation, fire-offerings, vows, charity, meditation, rosaries, austerity, and sacred learning—whatever is performed on the fifth lunar day shall become multiplied a thousandfold and more. (94)
Having spoken thus and led Śāradā away, Hari returned to Vaikuṇṭha;
he dispatched her, who was the very embodiment of Sarasvatī, back to the progeny of Brahmā.
Freedom from impurity, purity, and the absence of menstruation, as well as non-subjugation to the duties of a wife and remaining in maidenhood—these are what is meant by "protected. (96)

Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Attainment of Being the Consort of Nārāyaṇa, Purity, Freedom from Menstruation, Virginity, Childlessness, and the State of being Sarasvatī, through the Performance of Vows and Worship on the Fifth Day of the Extra Month by Śāradā, Daughter of Vairāja," within the *Puruṣottama-māsa-māhātmya* of the first section, the *Kṛtayuga-santāna*, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*. 1.297.

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī! To this divine narrative which bestows happiness and prosperity, which fulfills all desires, which is celestial, and which is united with Puruṣottama. 1.
At the beginning of creation, the ancestors had daughters endowed with excellent qualities;
they were three by name: Svadhā’s daughters Menā, Dhanyā, and Kalāvatī. || 2 ||
The yoginīs, endowed with all excellent qualities and capable of assuming any form at will,
while sporting in their father’s house, heard the drum of Hari.
This month of Puruṣottama has been honored by me under my own name; for those established in its vow, I fulfill their desires at one or two times [of the day]. (4)
"I shall fulfill it; Nārāyaṇa himself indeed declares this.
Having heard this proclamation in the morning on the sixth lunar day while in his father's house, [he resolved]. (5)
Today, indeed, a vow to Hari must be undertaken by all three of us,
so that Nārāyaṇa himself will grant our own desired object.
The ancestors shall have eternal contentment and indeed perpetual satisfaction;
having sought the cause of this, one should pray here to the illustrious Puruṣottama. (7)
However, Viṣṇu must never be requested for the sake of becoming a husband, because he possesses a great many wives. (8)
Rivalry with a co-wife is always suffering, for it is indeed a cutter of happiness; one must certainly not seek [such a relationship] even as a father or as a brother. (9)
At that time, what indeed was the use of happiness for us girls who were ignorant?
For our residence in her house would continue until the time of our marriage. (10)
Separation from kinsmen and even from one's father—that is indeed suffering.
Even as a son, Viṣṇu must never be entreated for anything at all.

In cases of beating, instruction, verbal abuse, and so forth, there may be culpability; however, regarding the nature of one's father-in-law and others, such transgression would result in suffering. (12)
Excessive proximity leads to offense, while excessive distance results in neglect; likewise, exceeding the proper limit and falling short of it both cause suffering. (13)
"Viṣṇu must therefore be entreated; in what form indeed should he be? Having thus reached a mutual agreement, those three [goddesses] alone... (14)
They maintained a moment of silence, meditating upon Nārāyaṇa;
at that time, a voice from the sky spoke to them again and again.
O women, choose Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa as your son-in-law;
by giving your daughter to him, there shall be eternal happiness for all. 1.6.
A mother is always spoken of by her daughter as being the daughter herself;
she considers herself happy, for the giving away of a daughter should be regarded as the giving away of oneself. (17)
A son-in-law should be treated like a son and is considered a supreme recipient of gifts;
he is to be honored and gratified with various forms of service. (18)
Whatever service was performed by the daughter, may its fruit also belong to the mother;
for the daughter, being entreated by her mother, performs that very service. (19)
Just as a portion belongs to the preceptor on account of the disciple, so too is a share obtained by the mother;
the attainment of happiness in this world, as well as fame and renown, shall be certain.
"Having resolved that many kinds of blessings indeed arise in this world through the power of a son-in-law, you should seek out such a son-in-law. (21)
The parents of that daughter of the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, in whose abode she always dwells, are considered meritorious and are regarded as having gone to Vaikuṇṭha themselves. (22)
Likewise, there shall be the deliverance of seven hundred and nine families;
and likewise, the mother, maternal grandfathers, and others shall attain liberation.
The ancestors always reside in the house of their daughter's husband;
therefore, you all should constantly entreat Hari, your son-in-law. (24)
"Furthermore, let there certainly be no rivalry among co-wives there;
therefore, let them request this by performing the vow and worship of the intercalary month. (25)
Then, having addressed them with the words "Cease," a voice from the sky spoke;
and they, both startled and exceedingly delighted, concluded that it was indeed so. || 26 ||
"May Brahmā become your son-in-law; may Hari become your son-in-law;
may Kṛṣṇa become the son-in-law"—having spoken thus, they indeed undertook a vow. (27)
On the morning of the sixth day, having bathed, all three of them—Menā, Dhanyā, and Kalāvatī—performed worship using three images made of gold. (28)
Having performed [the rites], they worshipped the deities in due order with the rituals beginning with invocation (āvāhana);
and with devotion, they bathed the three gods with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta). || 29 ||
Having massaged him with sandalwood and other substances, they bathed him with excellent waters; having wiped him dry, they adorned him with garments, ornaments, and unguents.
With saffron, unbroken rice, musk, fragrant substances, and flowers;
likewise with necklaces, garlands, crowns, and so forth, as well as incense, lamps, and the like.
Having worshipped the three with various kinds of sweet food offerings, drinks, betel leaves, and powders, as well as with umbrellas, beds, chowries, sandals, and other such items. || 32 ||
Having honored the three deities with fruits and sugar,
one should offer an *arghya* consisting of gems and other substances, together with plantain fruit.
Having paid homage to them, they gave handfuls of flowers; then, having begged for forgiveness, they entreated: "O Keśava, become our son-in-law! (34)
O Lord, through the resonance of your drum, you have been held within our hearts;
by means of your daughter, may you grant us happiness in every way. (35)
"This sixth day of the month of Puruṣottama has been observed according to the vow; we shall perform the worship again by taking our meal at night. (3.6)
Then, at the very break of dawn, they dismissed those gods;
by means of the brahmins, they had performed their daytime vow with clarified butter poured into the fire. (37)
Having performed the oblation at midday,
they honored with devotion the ancestors, the sages, the gods, and the munis established in the austerity of the people.
They gratified the lords with milk-rice, the essence of milk, cakes, leafy vegetables, and various kinds of sweet juices.
The daughters of the Tṛṣṇikā, being pleased, joined him with auspicious blessings:
"May Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa, and Kṛṣṇa bestow upon you the fruit of your vow. (40)
"And may they bring about whatever happiness you desire.
Then, in the evening, they once again displayed a garland of lamps. ||41||
Having caused a pavilion to be constructed, adorned with plantain pillars and gateways of leaves, and beautified by the inlay of golden vessels and mirrors; ||42||
Having caused it to be made variegated with garments and lightning, beautiful with the brilliance of various paintings, and in its center fashioned of gold inlaid with excellent jewels; ||43||
Having caused a large, beautiful throne to be fashioned, covered with skins of the makha, mallaka, śipra, and other animals, [he seated] Brahmā, Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa. ||44||
Having installed the three forms (mūrtis) accompanied by song and instrumental music, they performed an excellent worship there with gold, unbroken grains of rice, and saffron.
With excellent substances dyed with turmeric and with objects worthy of auspiciousness, they performed dancing and singing accompanied by the tinkling sound of small bells. 46.

Having performed the nightly lamp-offering, the incense and lamps, and the water for the guest-offering (arghya), one should partake of fried cakes, milk-drink, and vegetables grown from mustard leaves. ||47||
Having fed them and offered them three drinks of water and excellent fruit, and having granted them a moment's rest, they remained absorbed in meditation. ||48||
There, Brahmā, Kṛṣṇa, and Narāyaṇa had arrived for meditation;
among these, Menā beheld one wearing a loincloth who was exceedingly well-nourished. (49)
White as frost, wearing a tiger skin, with the moon upon his crest, he has matted locks and is intensely radiant with the splendor of Brahman pervading all around. (50)
He who was a youth of enchanting form, that very same one who is indeed the qualityless Brahman, has attained a state of possessing qualities and exists in human form. 5.1.
Śaṅkara, who fulfills all states of being, is accessible through internal mental activity that is free from impurity;
he proclaims his graciousness by raining down a shower of smiles and laughter. ||52||
Meanwhile, not seeing his own auspicious daughter seated on his lap, who was calling out to him repeatedly, "O Mother! O Mother! he indeed looked for her. ||53||
This Lord Śaṅkara, in the form of Brahmā, said to Menakā:
"O Menakā, you shall be born from Himavat, who is a portion of myself. (54)
And there, this maiden shall become your wife, Pārvatī;
you shall indeed give her to me, and from me you will obtain happiness. (55)
By observing the vow for even a single day of the month of Puruṣottama, your desired fruit, which bestows all happiness, shall come to pass. (56)
Having spoken thus, the god Śaṅkara, who is the supreme Brahman, vanished;
then indeed, Hari himself was seen by Dhanyā, bearing his bow.
Richly adorned with matted locks and bark garments, yet bearing the marks of a true kingdom, the youthful and enchanting Lord Vāsudeva transcends all qualities. ||58||
The Lord is endowed with a face encompassed by a halo of radiance and accompanied by a smile;
he is both four-armed and two-armed, and he shines resplendent upon a lion-throne. ||59||
Beside him, she saw her own beautiful daughter Sītā, repeatedly calling out "O Mother! with a sweet voice. (60)
The blessed Lord Śrī Rāma, being pleased, said to Dhanyakā:
"O Dhanyā, you shall indeed become the future wife of Janaka."
This daughter of yours, Sītā, shall become Mahālakṣmī;
you will surely give her to me, and from me you will obtain happiness.
O affectionate one, by performing this vow for even a single day of the month of Puruṣottama, you will surely obtain the desired fruit, which is of the nature of happiness.
Having spoken thus, the Lord Vāsudeva Nārāyaṇa vanished;
then Kṛṣṇa, accompanied by Sudarśana, was seen by Kalāvatī. (64)
Wearing a crown of peacock feathers, with yellow garments and a flute at his lips,
he was later that very same boy cowherd who became the lord of kings.
The Blessed One, the sovereign of kings, was most beautiful in every splendor;
he was a youth with the lovely luster of a fresh rain-cloud, adorned with ornaments.
Seated upon the most excellent divine lion-throne, the king of kings, with two arms, displays his great serenity through a gentle smile. (67)
Standing by his side was his daughter Rādhā, a future goddess who was a treasure-house of beauty corresponding to her form; Kalāvatī beheld her. (68)
Placing her own hand upon Kṛṣṇa’s neck, overwhelmed with love, she repeatedly called out to him with sweet words, "O Mother! O Mother! (6.9)
Śrī Kṛṣṇa, being well-pleased, touched Kalāvatī Rādhā and said: "In your state as a Vaiśya, this girl shall indeed become Rādhā. (70)
"You shall indeed give her to me in the vicinity of the Bhāṇḍīra fig tree;
she shall always be my chief wife, for she shall be eternal. (71)
Through me, O daughter, you shall obtain all happiness by means of the vow performed on a single day of the month of Puruṣottama. ||72||
"And the fruit you desire shall be of the nature of happiness. Having spoken thus, Kṛṣṇa vanished from that spot. (73)
Then, after a short time, those three emerged from that meditation;
with serene faces and having accomplished their purpose, they bowed repeatedly to Nārāyaṇa. (74)
Then, having offered handfuls of beautiful flowers during that night,
those maidens broke their fast by feeding one another.
They performed the gift of the forms of Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa, and Kṛṣṇa;
then, indeed, in the first age, they were received by the ancestors in due order. ||76||
Menā was married by the prescribed rites to Haimaja, Janaka, Gopa, Dhanya, and Kalāvatī;
and they became their daughters. ||77||

In sequence, however, Pārvatī, Sītā, and Rādhā are the embodiments of Brahman and the Supreme Self; at the beginning of creation, they appear in the form of the primary incarnations for the sake of the qualified [devotees]. (78)
And they were indeed offered to Śiva in the form of Rāma and to Kṛṣṇa;
having approached those sons-in-law, who are indeed incarnations of the Supreme Brahman. ||79||
Menā, Dhanyā, and Kalāvatī obtained all their desires;
thus, O Lakṣmī, is the vow of eating only at night and performing worship during the intercalary month. ||80||

By performing [the vow] on the sixth lunar day throughout the three periods of time, the fruit of the vow was obtained from the Ancient Supreme Person; as sons-in-law they were obtained, and Hari himself was obtained. || 8.1 ||
These daughters were given by Śambhu, Rāma, and Kṛṣṇa to the eternal [Lakṣmī];
indeed, they take delight on Kailāsa, in Vaikuṇṭha, and in Goloka. 82.
Therefore, his parents also become eternally liberated, having attained his supreme happiness as well as fame according to their desire. ||83||
And what more shall I tell you, O Lakṣmī, regarding this world and the next?
A mother truly desires to make her own daughter happy. (84)
Then she should perform the vow pertaining to the intercalary month, as well as the vow and worship on the sixth lunar day, just as it was performed by Menā and the others. (85)
Then she will indeed obtain Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa as her son-in-law;
thereafter, they shall all effortlessly attain worldly enjoyment, liberation, and everything else. ||86||
If Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is the worthy recipient for the gift of a daughter, then the four goals of human existence reach their highest perfection therein. (87)
There remains no worldly duty nor any other-worldly one to be performed, where Hari, the absorber of all, delights together with his daughter. (88)
The Lord is pleased with his son; when He is thus pleased, what indeed could be difficult to obtain or unattainable in the presence of Kṛṣṇa? (89)
Thus has that compassion of Nārāyaṇa been described to you, O Lakṣmī! During the intercalary month, the Unborn One fulfills the mental desires of those who observe vows. (90)
If one should desire that a son-in-law be equal to Kṛṣṇa in the power of his virtues, as well as in beauty, learning, and so forth, then it shall be so. (91)
If he desires, "May my son-in-law become world-renowned and an upholder of royal power," then indeed it shall be so. 92.
If a devotee of the Blessed One should desire, "May my son-in-law be long-lived and possessed of an abundance of wealth and grain," so shall it be. (93)
If one desires that my son-in-law should possess the qualities of a Brahmin, or else be endowed with the dharma of a Kṣatriya, it shall be so for the performer of the vow. (94)
If one desires that the son-in-law born in the household be a bringer of happiness, and that he possess sons, grandsons, and so forth, it shall be so for the woman who performs the vow. 95.
However, by the grace of Lord Hari, the mother-in-law obtains exactly such a son-in-law as she desires. (96)

Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-eighth chapter, titled "The Attainment of the Fruit in the Form of Establishing Relationships with Śaṅkara, Rāma, and Kṛṣṇa as Sons-in-Law," occurring within the *Puruṣottama-māsa-māhātmya* (The Greatness of the Month of Puruṣottama) in the first section, the *Kṛtayuga-santāna*, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*. It describes how Menā, Dhanyā, and Kalāvatī—the daughters of Pitṛmānasa—upon hearing the drum announcing the *adhikamāsa* (intercalary month), sequentially obtained daughters named Pārvatī, Sītā, and Rādhā through the performance of the *trikāla-vrata* on the sixth lunar day, thereby securing the aforementioned result.

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, Lakṣmī! The vow was performed by the two daughters of Viśvakarman who resided in Satyaloka, accompanied by the sounding of a drum. || 1 ||
Of the truthful [beings] in the heavenly and other worlds, of kings, of those dwelling in the netherworld (pātāla),
of cities, of palaces, of assembly halls, and of those performing sacrificial rites.
He who was the architect of the pavilions was indeed a portion of Nārāyaṇa;
his daughter named Siddhi was the elder, and Buddhi was the younger. (3)

O you who possess accomplishment and wisdom, who are beautiful in form and virtuous in conduct, and who worship the gods—having constantly remembered Nārāyaṇa, one should bathe every morning and thereafter [perform the following]. || 4 ||
Having bowed at the feet of his parents during the auspicious moment known as Brāhma,
he then lit lamps in his home and in the temple.
Having offered fragrant incense, they perform hymns of praise;
and having bowed to the God, they offer flowers, water, and food with sugar. || 6 ||
Then, having entrusted the household duties to one another,
both of them quickly fetch water from the middle of that lake for the sake of their success.
Having cleansed the house, she sets fire to the hearth and places a water vessel on the stove for the purpose of heating it.
Having established the ancestors, the devout one bathes them; meanwhile, having gathered the household bed and other items, he prepares the bed in the sleeping chamber. || 9 ||
Then, having protected the couches, swept them, and moved them to a clean place,
he prepares the cleansing of the night-vessels.
Meanwhile, Buddhi washed the damp garments of her parents who had bathed,
hung them on a rope, and went to a garden adjacent to the house.
She quickly brought flowers for the purpose of worshipping the gods and other rites, before her mother and father could reach the temple of Hari. (1-2)
Having first spread out a seat, he offers water for the sake of the twilight prayers and other rites, as well as garlands made of *tulasī* leaves, lotuses, *kunda*, and *campaka* flowers. (1.3)
With supreme devotion, he offers for the sake of worshipping the deity and his parents sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, saffron, the five nectars, and water. (14)
Vessels worthy of worship, vessels filled with ghee, sugar, seeds of grapes and pomegranates, and various kinds of fruits. (15)
She also brings cardamom, cloves, betel, and food offerings for her mother who is engaged in worship, and likewise for her father who is engaged in worship at that time. (16)
Having performed ten circumambulations and having offered ten prostrations, he indeed took up the water that had been used for washing the feet of his mother and father. (17)
While he stands by his side for the sake of service and offers his vision, Siddhi likewise arrives there at that very moment. 18.
Having performed circumambulations, prostrations, and other such acts born of devotion, and having drunk water, he goes once again to the vicinity of the hearth in the house. (19)
Then, having thoroughly cleansed the entire collection of materials in the kitchen for the purpose of cooking and having set them aside, he summoned that intelligent woman. ||20||
She prepares various kinds of foods, both solid and soft, as well as drinks;
moreover, she quickly effects the attainment of milk for her parents. (21)

Then, having scrubbed all the vessels used for worship with clay and purified them, one should perform whatever rites are prescribed for the morning; having done all that, both [the day and night] are then [rendered pure]. ||22||
Then he performs the study of the Vedas until the conclusion of the Vaiśvadeva rite;
having performed those two and fed [the guests], he again observes the midday ritual.
Having set aside portions for guests, cows, and living beings, and having given food to their dependents, they then respectfully partook of their own excellent meal. (24)
In the afternoon, he should perform the cleaning of the kitchen, the purification of the alms-bowl, sweeping, the fetching of water, and the preparation of the food and other provisions. (25)
Having relieved the fatigue of the body, they take a moment's rest;
then, having performed the viewing [of the deity] and other rites solely through the discourse on the sacred ford (tīrtha), || 26 ||
In the evening, having performed the complete worship of Kṛṣṇa with the sixteen types of offerings, and having fed him cooked food and desired delicacies with great devotion; || 27 ||
Then, having spread out a bed and other such items for both his parents, he performed the massaging of their feet as well as general service to them. (28)
Whatever one's own daily service to the cows and glorification of the Lord may be deficient, having made both of these complete and exhaustive, [one attains perfection]. (29)
Having performed a small amount of study, they should take a brief sleep;
then, rising at the hour sacred to Brahmā, they should reflect upon the knowledge they have practiced.
Furthermore, both maidens performed their daily duties;
thus, through such service and with great devotion, they delighted their parents exceedingly. (31)
They joined them with auspicious blessings: "May you both be happy, for you are endowed with love for the Lord Nārāyaṇa-Hari. (3.2)
"In time, that most auspicious and worthy of service shall be attained by you both.
Thus, they were the recipients of blessings, for Hari was ever present in their hearts again and again. (33)
While I was thus desiring Śrī Hari, Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord,
I heard the sound of a drum from those two in Satyaloka during that vow.
On the seventh day of the intercalary month, at dawn, the awakener of vows indeed awakens the people to the observances of the intercalary month. (35)
To all those people residing within the universe—whether men, women, or others—who shall perform [this] according to their ability, he is the bestower of their desired objects. (3.6)
For I am Śrī Puruṣottama, the giver of what cannot be obtained;
whether it be monthly, fortnightly, weekly, or even daily.
Whether it be the fast of the night, that of the forenoon, or that of the afternoon, or the intermediate one;
or fasting, subsisting on fruits, drinking milk, or consuming only water. (38)
Eating only bulbs, eating nivāra rice and the like, eating only at night, eating during the day, eating only one meal a day, eating only sesame seeds, or eating only what is unasked for; || 39 ||
Having performed [the rite] according to one's ability, one should worship Puruṣottama with flowers, or else with water, fruits, roots, or saffron. ||40||
Having worshipped Puruṣottama with unbroken grains and sandalwood paste, [he should offer] a garment, or well-matured milk, or sweet food. || 41 ||
With sugar, drinks of water, betel-leaf and the like, or even with a mere leaf, worship me, Puruṣottama, with excessive devotion and love. ||42||
Being satisfied, may you obtain from me that which is difficult to attain even during an intercalary month;
now, out of compassion, I shall grant it even when the spiritual practice performed is slight. (43)
Whatever is difficult to accomplish during other months, I shall indeed grant that very thing today multiplied ten millionfold, even if it be but a small amount. ||44||
Therefore, I shall certainly not give it later; so, O people, take even this fruit of the betel nut, which is superior to the station of Brahmā. (45)
Even by the vow of drinking only water, one attains the state of reclining upon the Ocean of Milk;
even by the vow of eating but once a day, one gains the right to Goloka. ||46||
Even by the mere vow of fasting at night, one attains equality with Nārāyaṇa;
even by the offering of leaves and flowers, one attains the status of Mahendra.
Even by the mere offering of a lamp, whether it be a man or a woman, a boy or a girl, they attain embodied existence as the sun, the moon, and so forth. (48)
If she desires my splendor as well as me, the Supreme Person—whether as a wife or a husband, or even as a son—I shall grant her Lakṣmī and myself as well. (49)
May they accept these boons from us and perform the accumulation [of merit], which arises from the power of virtue and is obtainable through the great rain of supreme compassion. (50)
"Truth, truth—never falsehood indeed—is what the drum proclaims.
Having observed the vow for the intercalary month, let the subjects receive whatever they desire. (51)
Having heard this, both maidens, on the morning of the seventh day, bowed down to my drum and offered salutations with the water of their folded palms. ||52||
Having worshipped with beautiful flowers, they both became filled with joy;
then once more, the auspicious words of compassion from the drum were heard.
"If these two maidens desire me, the Supreme Person, as their husband, then even by the vow of eating but one meal a day, I shall become the husband of them both. (54)
Having performed the midday worship with whatever offerings are available and having fed me with sweet food, you two shall attain Puruṣottama. (55)
Perceiving him speaking thus for their own welfare, Siddhi and Buddhi recognized that their own good fortune had arrived. (56)
Having worshipped his own parents and fed them according to the prescribed rite, and having completed the household duties with flowers, sandalwood, and water; ||57||
Having worshipped the golden image with unbroken grains, sweet foods, incense, lamps, and excellent offerings—whatever things were available in his own home—he honored it. (58)
O auspicious lady, with the desire to obtain a husband, they both performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) for the divine Lord Nārāyaṇa Hari, who is the auspicious fulfiller of all desires. 59.
Having given [these], they both prayed: "May you be our husband.
Having spoken thus, they respectfully offered handfuls of unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*). ||60||
At that moment, the illustrious Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa himself appeared, a youth who gazed with a sidelong glance like a shaft from his eye. ||61||
Hari himself, grasping the forearms of the two with his own hands,
placed their hands upon his head, drew them both toward his chest, and held them there.
Having addressed her as "Beloved" and gazed upon her again and again, I have united with you, O beloved; now that we are joined, I am truly born according to the sacred rite. (63)
Having spoken thus, Kṛṣṇa vanished; for those two always beheld that Hari, who is enchanting, both while awake and likewise in their dreams. (64)
In one place they beheld Kṛṣṇa seated on the lap of Pārvatī with a single trunk, and in another, he was without a trunk and holding a flute, situated in Goloka. ||65||
Then, in another moment, they both beheld that Gaṇeśa, the son of Śaṅkara, who was worthy of being chosen as a bridegroom, possessing a trunk and of beautiful form. (66)
Seeing him white-complexioned, with beautiful eyes and a handsome brow, endowed with youth, and yet essentially black, they fainted again and again. (67)
And once, while you two girls were making many sweetmeats in a dream, Gaṇeśa was seen by you arriving there and sitting upon a wooden bench. (68)
While she sat there requesting for sweetmeats, others also gave them at that time;
standing on both sides, the two of them repeatedly gave her *laḍḍūkās*. (69)
Gaṇeśa, having repeatedly received the excellent *sulaḍḍuka* sweets offered by his two sides with his short trunk, placed them into his own mouth. (70)
He places exceedingly sweet [foods] [before them], and with affection, he quickly eats;
then, placing his hands on the backs of the two girls, he praises them. (71)
Giving a single *laḍḍuka* to each of them, he feeds them both, laughing, making them laugh, delighting, and gladdening them with joy. (72)
Having thus revealed himself, he vanished;
yet the two maidens remained awake and repeatedly called him to mind. (73)
Thus, when Gaṇapati had been born in the heart and the time had arrived,
Viśvakarman learned of his previous history.
Having invoked Gaṇeśa according to the prescribed rite for the auspicious moment, the two daughters, Siddhi and Buddhi, were offered to him. (75)
Listen now to a great wonder that occurred here after the wedding:
at that time, two forms were manifested by Gaṇeśa within the house. (76)
One form was that of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and the second was the self of Gaṇeśa;
two forms were also created for each of the two maidens, both exceedingly beautiful.
Then Śrī Kṛṣṇa, taking those two forms equal to Rādhā upon Garuḍa, went to His own eternal abode, Goloka. (78)
There he indeed delights through his accomplishment and his divine form of intellect;
thus, by those two, the fruit consisting of liberation has been granted for the sake of the vow. (79)
Then, with his other form known as Gaṇeśa, he placed both of them upon his own lap and gazed at them repeatedly with affection. (80)
When she has been kissed on the cheeks, gratified, and has gone within the house, the fruit of fresh youthfulness is indeed attained through sexual union. ||81||
Thus, O Lakṣmī! by those two, the fruit consisting of Kṛṣṇa and Dhava was obtained;
each pair attained a divine form that became renowned even in the world. (82)

When the state of being worthy of worship and firm establishment have been attained through honoring the intercalary month (*adhimāsa*), or by the vow of eating once a day (*ekabhukta-vrata*), or by worshipping with acquired objects; || 82 ||
In this manner, whatever maiden performs the worship of Puruṣottama on the seventh lunar day, observing a single meal out of her desire for the true Lord Kṛṣṇa, [attains her goal]. ||84||
She will certainly obtain her own divine husband, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, who has manifested as a human being somewhere or other. 85.
Having enjoyed worldly pleasures in many worlds and experienced eternal realms, he will thereafter certainly attain Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s Goloka or Vaikuṇṭha. (86)
Therefore, one should perform the vow arising from the intercalary month;
through this, liberation will be attained without effort, and rebirth shall no longer remain. //87//

Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-ninth chapter, titled "The Description of Viśvakarman’s Attainment of Two Forms through the Vision of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and His Residence in Goloka, along with his Marriage to Kṛṣṇa in the form of Gaṇapati, following the Hearing of the Drum that Proclaims the Vow of the Extra Month and the Performance of the Ekabhukta-vrata on the Seventh Day by Means of Serving His Parents after Receiving Their Blessings," within the section on the Greatness of the Month of Puruṣottama in the first part, the Continuation of the Kṛtayuga, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*. 1.299.
