Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, Lakṣmī! Hear what occurred in the past at the beginning of the Yuga, at the start of creation;
six offspring were born to Brahmā from his mind during the night.
From the forehead of him who was emaciated by austerity, a great Rudra emerged;
he too, by the command of the Unborn (Aja), filled the world with Rudras.
Those [Rudras] were terrifying, cruel, and causes of the world’s destruction.
Seeing this, Brahmā did not find satisfaction and once again issued a command.
For the sake of the destruction of the Rudras, he then indeed created [them] by means of his son;
however, they were all destroyed by Rudra, and consequently the world became empty.
Beholding his own home, Satyaloka, to be empty,
the Creator of the universe fell into a state of profound indifference, save for the sound of children’s play.
In that house there was indeed no child, nor was there any weeping of children.
Neither play nor quarrels, nor even the chatter of children, were heard there.
That house was indeed like the abode of the King of Jackals belonging to the Night of Doom;
without a son and without a daughter, it became like hell, though it was heaven.
The palaces of impoverished lords resound like hollow pits;
a mansion occupied solely by a circle of old men resembles a withered tree;
and a family without offspring is like the peak of a parched mountain. (8)

A childless father is like a ground scorched by the flames of a funeral pyre. (9) Without the sweet, high-pitched chirping of children, even the flavors in the palace become tasteless, as if during the great dissolution of the world. (10)
Even foods that are only lukewarm become unsatisfying;
without him, festivals never truly become fresh and new again. Even those who exert themselves to achieve greatness perish without him. (11)
In summer, their moon-like faces wither like lumps of mud;
in the heat, their minds become parched like *barbura* wood;
and in the month of Jyeṣṭha, even drinks turn bitter like the juice of the *nimba* tree.
Children who bring happiness are born to those endowed with merit;
those who bring suffering are born to the impoverished who have performed evil deeds.
In this matter, the sole cause is the debt incurred from previous expenditure.
"A new penance must also be performed that will grant me offspring.
Having thus resolved, Brahmā restrained the entire circle of his senses and practiced austerity for the duration of a single *ghaṭikā*, remaining established in meditative absorption (*samādhi*).
Desiring offspring, he indeed meditated upon them within his heart;
then, born from his mind, there appeared Dundubhi, Ghaṇṭaka, and Kambu.
These were three sons and three daughters: Ghaṇṭā and likewise Nīrājanā.

And the *jhallarī*—these are the mental [manifestations]. Furthermore, the triad born later consists of the bronze vessel (*kāṃsya*), the five-vessel set (*pañcapātra*), and the incense-holder (*dhūpadhra*). These are the mental [forms].
Of Prajāpati, there were three daughters, three sons, and a third of neuter gender.
Nine offspring were born from his mental resolves; for whatever kind of intention one has during the act of impregnation or at the time of conception,
such is the offspring that is born— so it was with those born of the Lotus-born One.
In that place, indeed, six noisy things that caused reproachful cries—
namely, the conch, the bell, the drum, the small bell, the jhallarī cymbal, and the bronze vessel— made a tumultuous clamor in the house as soon as they were born. || 21-22 ||
Because he had attained a state of equanimity, even the Creator’s decree became void;
his home became filled with festive joy along with his playing children.
Brahmā was pleased by him, as he remained devoted to the nurturing and protection [of his family].

You considered the home with its children to be the abode of auspiciousness. At that moment, those six— Nīrājanā, Pañcapātra, Dhūpadhra, and the others, along with Maunavṛtti— delighted in dancing and other such performances.
Always, both morning and evening, those nine indeed gather together;
they perform kīrtana and worship for the sake of their respective duties.
They became truly devoted to Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa alone. (26)
Brahmā indeed rejoiced exceedingly at the acquisition of his own offspring.
As time passed in this manner, on the morning of the eighth day of the intercalary month,
a great drum was heard by them on the bank of the Viṣṇupadī.
While those performing their morning ablutions there heard that which brings auspiciousness, let all who possess consciousness hear it, as well as the immobile and the insentient;
indeed, both the embodied and the formless, and likewise boys and girls. (29)
Let even the children listen to this, which yields the highest fruit with little effort.
I, who am a proponent of Puruṣottama, speak according to the truth:
this month is Puruṣottama, and he himself is Puruṣottama.
He who has honored Śrī Puruṣottama, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, with his mind, his actions, and his speech, transcends all months and attains Śrī Puruṣottama himself.
(35) By him through whom he is honored, that Śrī Puruṣottama becomes truly honored.
Today, silence should be observed and food should be taken only once a day.
Worship should be performed in the morning, at midday, and likewise at night.
Today, the divine form of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa should be meditated upon.
Having bathed in the morning and bowed to Hari, one should bring the materials for worship.
One should place a golden image of Viṣṇu within the maṇḍala and upon the water-pot (ghaṭa).
[One should bathe it] with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), milk, curd, honey, and clarified butter.
One should bathe Puruṣottama with sugar and pure water.
Having wiped him with cloths, one should dress Puruṣottama in washed garments and the like,
and adorn him with ornaments such as bracelets, crowns, and so forth.
One should worship with sandalwood, agarwood, musk, saffron, and other such substances;
one should feed [the deity] milk-preparations and the like, and offer betel-leaf and other items.
One should cause the rite to flourish with incense, lamps, prostrations, and the waving of lights (ārārtika), and so forth. (38)
One should circumambulate [the deity] while prostrating like a staff and pray for one's heart's desire.
Likewise, one should offer water for drinking, as well as arghya, fruit, and a handful of flowers;
and one should pray: "O Lord of Compassion, Supreme Person, Keśava! (39–40).
O Lord, for your sake today the monthly vow of Puruṣottama has been observed by me day and night after performing a fast,
or else a single meal has been taken according to my capacity. (41)
"Whether it is being performed or will be performed, may it be completed without obstacles.
And grant the fruit as desired, O Janārdana, ocean of compassion!
Having thus prayed to the Lord of Gods, may they obtain what their hearts desire. (42–43)
Upon hearing the great drum in this manner, Vedhobālā and the others immediately bathed and, filled with wonder, joyfully approached him at that very moment.
The small drum, eager, questioned the great drum.
"Who are you? From where have you come? What will you say? What will you give?
Where is your dwelling? What is your purpose? And who is your master?
Thus questioned by Dundubhi, Mahādundubhi spoke to him.
I am the son of Vaikuṇṭha, and I have come from Vaikuṇṭha;
my eternal residence is in Vaikuṇṭha, in the abode of Nārāyaṇa. My duty is to play [the flute] at the time of the *nīrājana* ceremony for Nārāyaṇa.
My Lord is Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the illustrious Puruṣottama. By His command, my father, having assumed the form of the abode of Vaikuṇṭha, remains eternally engaged in service as a servant. || 48-49 ||
By the command of my father and likewise by the command of Nārāyaṇa,
I always wander through the three worlds, performing the duties of a servant. Whatever command arises from that Nārāyaṇa, that I carry out.
I proclaim, I cause it to be heard, and I go there once again.
Indeed, I have two forms; one has four arms and is my attendant.
I am always engaged in service, while the second is Sudundubhi.
Struck by my staff, I joyfully proclaim the command of Hari:
"By His grace, I am capable of assuming many forms.
The Blessed Lord Himself is satisfied by my service and by His own mercy. (53)
He gives me the finest food, all of which is pleasing to the senses; he gives me gardens, celestial palaces, and furnishings—
just as Nārāyaṇa possesses them, so too do I possess them.
Everything is equal to Nārāyaṇa; there is nothing whatsoever inferior to Me.
The Ānaka, Paṭaha, Bherī, and Ḍhakkā drums are My forms.
Indeed, I dwell in temples in service according to the requirements of the occasion.
Having heard that from Dundubhi, his mind drawn by that happiness,
he asked the excellent Dundubhi: "How indeed can Vaikuṇṭha, or Hari’s prosperous abode, be attained by those such as I?"
The great drum challenged this small drum, which desired to know its measure:
"Whether on the new moon day, or once a month, twice a month, or thrice a month;
on whatever day the worship of Kṛṣṇa is performed, that [small drum] shall attain [the greatness of the great one]. (59)
By means of vows such as fasting or eating only what is unasked for, by eating but a single meal,
or by the vow of eating only at night or subsisting on milk alone—
by performing even a small portion of these, people indeed obtain that great fruit. (60–61)
Even that [fruit] is obtained by Hari through the mere offering of water;
it is obtained even by one who possesses nothing before him, provided he does so with devotion.
One should perform dancing before the Lord and singing accompanied by beautiful melodies.

Pleased by that as well, the Blessed One indeed bestows Vaikuṇṭha; and he also bestows Goloka, the abode of Brahmā known as Akṣara. Whichever of these he desires—each being progressively more excellent than the last—he grants it.
Having heard this, Svalpadaundubhi said to Dundubhīśvara:
"Is there indeed another place higher than Vaikuṇṭha, namely Goloka?
Is there any other realm superior to Goloka, such as the abode of Brahmā?"
"Who dwells there as the Lord? Shall we reach him or not?
Mahādundubhi replied: "The glorious Lord Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa is the master of the world of Vaikuṇṭha; if you desire him, he shall indeed be attained."
The Lord of the abode of Goloka, Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, the Great Master,
is indeed attained by one who has observed the vow during the intercalary month (adhimāsa).
And the Lord of the world of Brahmā, Puruṣottama, the Sovereign of the Imperishable (Akṣara).
Because there is indeed no one superior to him, nor even anyone equal to him—
He is the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord.
Carrying His command upon my head, I proclaim this vow and worship.
The lord of that intercalary month bestows it upon the observer of the vow;
for if the observer of the vow desires anything divine, he grants it all through his grace. But whoever has a desire for you, their worship of my form [is required].
In the abode of Goloka, there is happiness a crore times greater than in Vaikuṇṭha.
In the supreme imperishable abode (Akṣara-dhāma), the happiness is even beyond numbering compared to that of Goloka.
Thus, there is infinity of blisses and an incalculable number of divine lordships.
Understand that there is indeed nothing else so excellent;
the worlds of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa are comparable to hell.
If you must go there, then worship Puruṣottama.
Today, on the eighth day, let him be worshipped according to one's ability and according to one's disposition.
Let dancing be performed, and let singing also be performed. Hari will grant every desired fruit in accordance with one's inner state.
Whenever he is desired for the purpose of dwelling in all abodes, in the spheres (*golaka*), and even in the planets beginning with Acyuta, he grants that as well;
having heard [this], one should indeed exclaim "Aho! Aho! and perform most wonderful deeds.
There, the Vedhas and their offspring performed dance and song;
they honored the supreme drum and earnestly entreated it:
"We shall go to that place where Śrī Puruṣottama resides. || 78-79 ||
"You must tell him about our vow and worship:
'Today, on the eighth day, we are observing a fast along with the performance of the vow.
We shall indeed perform the worship of Akṣareśa and Golokeśa. (80)
"Indeed, we shall perform the consecration of the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, by which we may have access everywhere.
Having honored Dundubhīśa, they led Vedha into the interior of the house;
just as Nārāyaṇa is to be worshipped, so was he worshipped by all of them.
He was adorned, served, and decorated with ornaments;
he was fed, massaged, and honored with sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā).
His feet were rubbed and his body massaged until he was made to rest.
Having been put to sleep for a moment, he was later awakened and dismissed.
Being exceedingly pleased by his service, he turned back again and again and said to Dundubhi and the others: "Perform the vow with devotion. (84–85)
"Having made a proclamation throughout the universe and returning here this evening,
I shall meet with you and then indeed depart for Vaikuṇṭha.
Having spoken thus, the best of drums went forth to awaken the worlds.
And Dundubhi and the others,

having performed their ablutions at dawn, midday, and night— thus bathing three times a day— at that triple juncture, likewise worshipped Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa and Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa with ritual offerings. (87–88)
Then, having joyfully fed the gods with divine, supreme sixteen-fold milk-preparations and other delicacies,
they made their formal decision in the presence of the Blessed One’s image. (89)
May Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, Brahmā, and Īśvara hear this decision:
we must certainly remain forever in the abode of the Blessed Lord, engaged in worship and service before Hari throughout the entire creation. (90–91)
May he protect us in his presence according to our own desires;
we must always accept service and nothing else.
Indeed, servitude is the best of all; why then should we not find it pleasing? 92.
"May Hari, our Lord, grant us employment and exchange [of duties].
Having thus offered their prayer, they performed ninefold dances accompanied by musical instruments and singing, imbued with various gestures, emotions, and melodies. (9.3–9.4)
Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, Brahmā, and Īśvara—the compassionate lords—were pleased;
even the month of Puruṣottama perceived their devotion there.
At that moment, Dundubhīśa arrived there at night to meet Hari.
Having seen and heard [this],
all those supreme lords were filled with grace and extreme satisfaction toward the nine sons of the Creator, who were united in a devotion that transcends all else. (96–97)
They appeared visibly before him in divine and beautiful forms;
all of them wore celestial crowns and were adorned with divine garlands and other ornaments.
Their splendor was equal to ten million streaks of lightning, and they were endowed with the radiance of Rādhā.
Wearing celestial garments, they are well-served by those bearing parasols and chowries;
endowed with the beauty, loveliness, and gentleness of ten million Cupids, their forms are filled with divine sovereignty, great heroism, and bliss. (99–100)
With serene faces, they said: "What offspring do you desire?
We are exceedingly pleased by your devotion, by your worship of Dundubhi and Īśa, and by your service;
therefore, tell us whatever you wish for."
Then, seeing and hearing that the offspring of the Creator were exceedingly joyful, they said:
"O Supreme Lords of Fortune, lead us to your homes;
employ us in service at your feet in your close presence."
In every house, in every world, and wherever your abode may be, we nine shall always perform service there;
for we are all born together as sisters and brothers.
Therefore, may there never be a separation between us anywhere.
Wherever you may be, may the Supreme Lords protect us day and night while we serve you; there, may they protect us together as a united group.

"By attaining supreme liberation through service to you, may we become abodes of happiness. Please accept that which we have requested; whatever is your will, let it be done. As for us, we are servants and slaves; we are satisfied with servitude and do not seek anything else."
"A servant must indeed do whatever is necessary so that his master may be pleased.
Having heard these words of theirs, which were filled with devotion, those supreme lords asked Dundubhiśa: "Tell us by our command, what should be given to these men?"
The great drum resounds here: "Indeed, heirs are easily obtained;
but servants and groups of slaves are difficult to find everywhere in the world.
To the group of slaves, everything certainly belongs to the master.
For such servants as these, what is there that cannot be given?
Indeed, the world of Akṣara is to be given, Goloka is to be given, Vaikuṇṭha itself is to be given, as well as whatever other abodes there may be. (111–112)
Likewise, there are other temples throughout the universes where your forms,
such as the forms of your incarnations and so forth, reside;
let your dwelling be granted in all those places.
Indeed, they must dwell with me as well, for these devotees are like me.
May you possess innumerable forms,
so that you may remain together with them through songs of victory and dances.

During the nightly watch, during worship, during processions, and during festivals— by means of proclamations, by the offering of *arghya*, and by the presentation of fragrant substances and the like—
at each and every temple of yours, there shall be worship in the evening and in the morning.
Let the lustration rite with fire perform the dance and the circumambulation.
Let this drum, whose nature is that of a kettledrum, indeed raise a cry of victory.
And let the bell bring forth his subsequent victory within the temple.
Let the bell produce a most enchanting proclamation of liberation;
at the time of the lustration ceremony and other rites, let embodied beings worship Hari.
May those who do not worship Him, the revilers, the atheists, and the antagonists [also be moved].
Let the bell proclaim, "They shall be punished by Yama; let him do so!
(120). And let the sweet-sounding hand-drum perform song and dance in the hand;
let the small drum call out to the people within the temple. (121)
Let him perform the circumambulation in front [of the deity] with the water from Kambustīrtha;
let him preserve the water for the feet in five vessels and also offer the *arghya*;
and let him indeed offer fragrant incense in the temple.
"By means of this drum, I shall indeed summon all those who are far away:
'O highly fortunate ones, let men and women who desire liberation come here for the sake of beholding Hari; but let the wicked go far away.'"
"In this way, all of us, being disciplined, shall perform the service;
O glorious Supreme Lords, grant the fruit of this vow to them.
Moreover, just as with me, let these two have two hands for the sake of the imperishable Brahman."
May there be two arms in Goloka and four hands in Vaikuṇṭha;
may there be equality with the forms of their respective lords and divine splendor; and may the capacity to assume innumerable forms exist in every house. (1.26–1.27)
May purity such as yours, may the practice of performing good deeds such as yours, and likewise honor and protection such as yours, always endure.
May those who commit slander against these [virtues] go to hell. (128)

"May those people who shall cause the destruction, theft, abuse, breaking, and so forth of these [images], fall into hell. And may they [fall] for those who perform the dismemberment or the rejoining of their limbs. (129–130)
May those who serve these makers of images, givers of images, as well as those who nourish images and those who perform restoration of dilapidated ones,
attain the world of Puruṣottama. (131)
"I indeed choose that embodied beings who produce the sounds of these musical instruments and so forth may attain the abode of the Blessed One;
thus was it requested by Dundubhi with the great drum. (132–133)
And there, the Blessed Ones granted their consent, saying, "So be it.
Then those Supreme Lords drew near their nine children,
embraced them, and bestowed upon them divine forms with four or two arms.
Having seated him upon his own vehicle, they led him to their respective abodes.
There, she who was devoted to the service of Hari became like Lakṣmī herself, accompanied by the lustration rite (nīrājanā), bells, and the divine-formed jhallarī drum. || 135-136 ||
Elsewhere, however, those [attendants] shone, fashioned according to their respective roles:
the conch, the bell, the drum, the bronze vessel, the five-fold bowl, and the incense-bearer—these six gentle ones, assuming divine forms for the Lord. (137)
And having assumed their liberated forms, they entered into the abodes for service;
elsewhere, however, they shone according to their respective requirements.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, those divine children of the Creator were truly born.
Indeed, by means of the vow on the eighth day of the month of Puruṣottama,
those who perform such a vow shall likewise go to that abode.
Thus, even a small act performed here during the intercalary month (malamāsa) will bear great fruit.
That compassion which consists in not grasping even the slightest gain is the supreme lordship of the Lord.
(141) As long as Brahmā shall live and as long as the earth shall endure, so long shall the drums, bells, and other instruments remain in the abode of Acyuta. (142)
But upon liberation, they shall forever remain divine in the abode of Keśava.
Therefore, this vow must be performed; otherwise, there would not be such a downpour [of rain].
Brahmā then reflected: "My sons have attained liberation."
"Then, if I were to produce others, my home would not be empty.
Indeed, the masters of yoga, Sanaka and the others, as well as the mental sons of Brahmā, were produced by Brahmā; therefore, they are truly exponents of Brahman. (144–145)
In this way, other creators of the world were also manifested.
Seeing the progeny, he became tranquil, and the flow likewise came to rest.
Those humans and others who indeed hear this narrative—
And those who shall recite it on the eighth day will certainly obtain its fruit. 147.

Thus, in the first section, the *Kṛtayuga-santāna*, within the *Puruṣottama-māsa-māhātmya* of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, [is described] the vision of Akṣareśa, Golokeśa, and Vaikuṇṭheśa by the mind-born sons of Brahmā named Dundubhi, Ghaṇṭa, and Kambu, as well as their daughters named Ghaṇṭā, Nīrājanā, and Jhallarī, and their offspring named Kāṃsyapātra, Pañcapātra, and Dhūpadhrā, following the hearing of the great sound of the drum (*mahādundubhi*), through the performance of the vow on the eighth day (*aṣṭamī*) during the intercalary month (*adhikamāsa*), and their subsequent creation in those respective abodes and worlds.
And Chapter Three Hundred, titled "The Description of the Installation in Various Forms in Every Temple, Liberation, Benedictions, and so forth," [ends].
Chapter 300 of the *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā*, Section 1 (The Lineage of the Kṛta Yuga).
Chapter 301.
[The Author: Chapter 302.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī! [to the account of] Puruṣottama-yoginī.
The divine narrative of the month of Puruṣottama destroys all sins. 1.
From the presence of the Supreme Brahman, Vāsudeva was born;
from Vāsudeva arose the foremost Puruṣa known as Bhūman. (2)
From the Abundant One (Bhūman) arose Virāj; from his mouth Agni was born.
Among the three worlds, gold is renowned as the offspring of Agni. (3)
At the beginning of creation, indeed no one performed any honor for Agni,
because of his extreme heat, his burning nature, and likewise his black-pathed course.
Seeing such a fire—one that reduces the body of the one who enters it to ashes—even kinsmen such as Brahmā and the others [would be terrified]. (5)
Having fallen into fear, they do not even associate with those who offer honor; at meals, festivals, and drinking parties, they keep them far away as if from fire. (6)
Having received insults from all embodied beings in every direction, he found no rest anywhere in the three worlds for his food and other necessities. (7)
From certain places, however, he received beatings and other such treatment;
therefore, having concealed his tongue, [he endured] the heat and other qualities of the flames. || 8 ||
Unobserved by others, the fire went to the Lokāloka mountain;
hungry, it devoured the peak of the Lokāloka mountain. (9)
That which was being cooked in her womb was born in the form of a son;
it became gold, and that ground became golden. (10)
On the side of the Lokāloka mountain, it became illuminated.
Thus, indeed, he proceeds while performing a circumambulation of that mountain. || 11 ||
Wherever he becomes hungry, there he eats the mountain peak;
then, in the form of his son, he is born as that which is cooked. (12)
Thus sons were born everywhere from all sides; indeed, the ground was golden everywhere along the Lokāloka mountain. (13)
Having become round in shape, it subsequently grew into a massive horn resembling the cosmic egg, devouring everything within the earth. (14)
The divine fire went to the Middle Country (Madhyadeśa) and rested there for a moment;
while being cooked, it was born as a great peacock in the form of a son. || 15 ||
That [gold] pervaded the great Meru on all sides;
therefore, Meru attained its renown as "Suvarṇa" (the Golden One). || 16 ||
Inert, devoid of fragrance, consisting of mine-ore and stone, and heavy;
wherever it falls, there it remains fixed. (17)

Just as people do not place a fixed measure upon fire, they likewise do not place a limit on gold; for embodied beings sustain themselves through things such as the products of the wish-fulfilling tree. (18)
Indeed, no such thought occurred to him as "What is gold? or "What is fire? nor did he consider "What is the purpose of gold? or "What is the purpose of fire? (19)
Even so, at that time, wisdom did not arise through the power of the wish-fulfilling tree;
both gold and fire shone forth, devoid of value. (20)
Now, in this matter, indeed, there is no arbiter for us;
for without a purpose, the value of anything whatsoever does not arise. (21)
Even when it is time for mere grass, it becomes equal to ten million pieces of gold;
indeed, fire proves highly valuable in a dispute over cold. //22//
The peacock feather discarded by me was held by Kṛṣṇa in Goloka;
by placing it upon his own crown, it attained both worshipfulness and value. (23)
In ancient times, the water of the Gaṅgā was held by Brahmā in his water-pot;
when it was released, it became as precious as a great being, for that which is great is indeed precious. ||24||
Indeed, Kaṅkara was held upon Kṛṣṇa’s chest as something of great value;
Kardama, however, was not held by anyone at all, nor did he attain even the slightest value. (25)
Therefore, I am Mahānagni and my son is Suvarṇaka;
whether it be for some purpose or without one, [this was done] by the great ones, even without formal agreement. ||26||
We would certainly not be of value; that indeed would be the greatest sorrow, if our finger were not included at the start of the counting of the virtuous. (27)
In this case, death for him is indeed better than a life lived in vain that brings only suffering—whether it be learning, royal power, spiritual accomplishment, or even sovereignty. (28)
Fame, wealth, or even devotion is better than life;
one devoid of these must die. Therefore, we shall indeed die this very day. (29)
Having reflected thus, Vahni and his son went up high to the peak of Mount Meru, seeking death by falling from it. (30)
At that time, the drum of Hari resounded there in Satyaloka;
it was heard by those two [Nārada and Parvata] who said, "Let people not grieve during this additional month."
Those people who, having recollected Nārāyaṇa, shall perform the vow and worship on this ninth day, their desire will be fulfilled. (32)
By eating once a day, by eating only at night, or likewise by eating only what is unasked for;
or today [let it be] with fruit or milk, twice a day or even once a day. ||33||
Having observed the vow and performed the worship, they have taken refuge in Kṛṣṇa;
even if they are devoid of honor, impoverished, and without purpose. ||34||
Even those beyond counting shall go to the supreme state;
I, indeed, Dundubhi, proclaim the teaching of the Supreme Person. (35)
Whether it be painful, or bound up with afflictions, or utterly disregarded; whether it be out of place, or of little value, or dull, or even extremely intense. (36)
Whoever, having sought refuge, observes a vow during an intercalary month—for such a person I shall always dispel all miseries and provide protection. (37)
In the month of Puruṣottama, one who observes the vow is indeed honored by me;
in the month of Puruṣottama, a performer of meritorious deeds shall attain purification. ||38||
One who performs my worship here shall attain the state of being worshipped by all;
whereas for one who has no protector whatsoever anywhere, it is indeed never so. (39)
If he protects me, the Supreme Person, as he protects the intercalary month, then I, the Supreme Person, shall protect him; so I declare.
Let them worship me with devotion and feed me excellent milk-rice;
let them pray for whatever they desire and receive their heart's wish from me. (41)
Out of grace, I shall grant even that which has not been performed, bestowing what is desired;
though it be small, I shall give much—let them receive from Puruṣottama. ||42||
Those who today shall neither perform the vow nor the formal acceptance [of marriage], for them there will be loss and failure; nothing greater than this exists. (43)
Therefore, let them come, let them accept the boons, and let them perform the worship;
let them observe this most excellent vow on the ninth day during the intercalary month. ||44||
"I am the giver, I am prosperous, I am sublime in every way;
here I sound the drum, having Nārāyaṇa as my inner self. (45)
I am the very nature of Nārāyaṇa, the teacher of Puruṣottama;
I make my devoted servant gracious and [thus] the supreme person (Puruṣottama). 46.
Whoever shall offer me a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water, I shall in turn bestow upon him the most excellent [gift], such as jewels and the like. (47)
Whoever shall offer me food to be eaten, chewed, licked, or sucked, to him I shall likewise return that gift multiplied ten millionfold. (48)
For him who has no one at all as a witness, a provider of refuge, a nourisher, an honor-giver, or a protector—I am indeed his creator and his protector. 49.
Let those of great fortune come, whether they have been honored or not;
let them be boys or girls, young women, or married or unmarried. (50)
Whether they be young or fortunate, or unfortunate and impoverished; whether they be old with grey hair and wrinkled limbs, or possessed of a virtuous mind, or even devoid of mind. ||51||
Pervaded by the third nature (tamas), devoid of names and designations—whether stationary or moving, insentient or appearing like the insentient—[they all exist]. (5.2)

Even animals—those dwelling in crevices, those dwelling in pits, those born from digging or burrowing, those born from the mouth, those born from the back, those born from filth, and those born from what is not filth. (5.3)
Having taken recourse to the intercalary month and having gratified the Supreme Person, may they attain the station of Brahmā or that imperishable abode. ||54||
May they go to the supreme happiness in heaven; may they go to the Illustrious Puruṣottama; may the son go to his father, the husband go to his wife, and the lotus-like woman go to her spouse. ||55||
May they attain a home, fame, and wealth; may they attain eternal worship;
and by my grace, may they occupy the most excellent station of supreme preeminence. 56.
Having heard this noble proclamation, Agni and Suvarṇaka attained great fortitude and thereafter abandoned their grief. (57)
On the peak of Meru in Satyaloka, they both went to Dundubhi for refuge;
having bowed to Dundubhi, they performed his worship with great reverence. ||58||
Vahni then caused the son of Dundubhi to bow at his feet with gold;
seeing that his son possessed such exceedingly beautiful form, he [honored him]. ||59||
Having lifted it up with the Dundubhi mudrā and grasped it with the hands born from the palms, the golden [image] was held for a moment upon the head and likewise upon the shoulder. (60)
After he had been offered into the fire, the Fire-god spoke with a faltering voice:
"There is no protector for us two, nor is there anyone who would treat us with honor. (6.1)
"O Dundubhi, having experienced great suffering, we two have come for the sake of death;
yet, if by your word we perform the *nakta* vow today," (62)
"We shall perform the worship of Hari, provided that Hari becomes our protector.
As they were speaking thus, tears fell from their eyes onto the ground. (63)
Seeing that silver produced there, shining brilliantly upon the dry land, the great fire felt compassion for him whose heart was thus broken. (64)
And Dundubhi consoled him along with his son with kind words:
"Observe the vow of eating only at night on the ninth day of the intercalary month."
Perform worship today indeed to Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, having had a golden image of Nārāyaṇa fashioned. (66)
Having bathed [the deity] with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), worshipped with unbroken rice grains and sandalwood paste, and adorned with golden ornaments, necklaces, and garlands as well; 67.
With excellent jewels, garments, various articles, foods, and fruits;
with water, betel for drinking, incense, lamps, and circumambulations. ||68||

Having gratified the Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person (Śrī Puruṣottama), one should make a request of Him—He who is beyond worldly treatment, self-supported, beyond honor, and without external refuge. (69)
Rescue me, who am hungry, thirsty, hateful, and burning;
I am indeed dull-witted, scentless, heavy, and as harsh as a stone. (70)
O Ocean of Compassion, O Lord, rescue even that which is devoid of qualities, lacking consciousness, or seemingly ineffective; bring it to a state of reckoning. (7.1)
Thus one should offer praise and present the *arghya* with a bilva fruit;
having offered a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*) and bowed to the Lord, one should perform the ritual dismissal (*visarjana*). ||72||
One should act likewise at midday and likewise at midnight;
one should perform the lustration ceremony with musical instruments, dancing, and songs, and then dismiss [the deity].
"O Kṛśānu, act thus; O Hāṭaka, you likewise act thus.
Nārāyaṇa, being pleased, will deliver both of you. (74)
Having heard these words spoken by Nārāyaṇa from the great drum, Vahni fashioned a golden image of Nārāyaṇa indeed. (75)
Then the father and son fashioned an image of Lakṣmī and worshipped it; they both duly observed the vow of eating only at night. ||76||
As he was praying to Hari Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa during the night, [the Lord],
accompanied by Lakṣmī, appeared before him.
Beholding that Supreme Person, whose face was completely encircled by a halo of radiance, who was attended by Lakṣmī, and who was smiling very gently; ||78||
O Lord of Compassion, Agni and Suvarṇa entreat you: deliver me, who am possessed of a hot nature and am a consumer, from this place! (79)
"O Lord, there is no such thing anywhere; give me food likewise.
There is indeed no price for a foolish son, nor for gold. (80)
No honor is seen for the sacrificial grass; therefore, manifest that glory.
O Blessed One, O All-pervading Lord, grant us your service forever. ||8 1 ||
"I have fallen for refuge at your feet; deliver me along with my sons.
Thus entreated, Hari-Kṛṣṇa, who is Nārāyaṇa, spoke to the fire.
"O Kṛśānu, abandon your grief; I am indeed pleased with your vow.
Born from my mouth, may you always remain my mouth. (8.3)

"I grant you this boon, my son: those who, at the beginning of a sacrifice and other rites, shall offer oblations into the fire situated within the sacrificial pit, they shall provide you with food. (84)
Those people who entrust the offering of the Agnihotra to you—through you, all of that must be consumed by me as being identical with me, and not otherwise. (85)
"Except for Vahni, I shall not accept food or other offerings from those who give them to me; this is entirely due to my favor toward you. (86)
"From this day forward, I shall become renowned in the world as the Blessed One 'Agnimukha' (Fire-mouthed); therefore, people will provide me with food and other necessities. (87)
They shall cast all that upon you, and I will devour it from your mouth;
for your dwelling shall especially be among the śamī trees in an invisible form.
And likewise, may your abode be everywhere, even in diamonds and the like;
so that there may be no burning of objects, yet you remain their dwelling. (89)
O Agni, may you be present everywhere; may you be happy among all people.
May you receive honor in every way, and may you be treated with respect in every manner. (90)
At the time of the destruction of the wish-fulfilling trees, for the purpose of cooking on hearth-stoves and the like, may the kindling of fire belong to you alone in every single household. (9.1)
But when the wish-fulfilling gem and such are lost, you will be honored in every way in house after house; therefore, maintain your fortitude. (92)
And with my second divine form as an attendant, O Agni, perform service eternally in my abode; you are liberated by me, O sinless one. (93)
When the first cycle of the yuga has passed, then indeed no task whatsoever will be possible for anyone without fire. (94)
Your price, honor, hospitality, respect, and worship shall all reach their highest peak; of this there is no doubt. (95)
Moreover, this son of yours, Suvarṇa, is indeed very dear to me;
from this day forward, he must be borne by me upon my own head. (96)
"Let this crown indeed be mine, and let these earrings be yours; let the chain, the bracelets, and the rings be the very form of my ornaments. (97)
Let the girdle, the food, and the vessels be made of gold for all things;
I have placed your son upon my head as a crown. (98)
Then, as time passes, he will receive honor everywhere;
he will become highly valued, well-concealed, and worthy of protection. (99)
When the wish-fulfilling trees and others perish, he shall become that very Kalpadru tree;
furthermore, I indeed grant you a divine form of pure gold.
In his fundamental form, he shall always serve me in my abode;
my attendant named Hāṭaka shall dwell in my imperishable realm.
Then, at another time, when a task was necessary, he, who is of the nature of fire and composed of great splendor, became known by the name Hāṭakeśvara. || 10.2 ||
In the netherworld and upon the earth, Mahādeva shall exist;
my incarnation will receive worship everywhere through my power. (10.3)
Maheśvara shall be the bestower of liberation upon his devotees, and in the creation of the entire universe, he will attain fame just like you. (104)
Just as I, O Blessed One, am all-pervading, so shall the fire pervade gold;
it shall attain pervasion within my creation and shall receive my honor. (1.05)
"Furthermore, their protection and their entire establishment shall be certain.
Having spoken thus, Hari himself assumed divine forms for the two of them. (106)
Others led her to their own abodes when her form was infused into objects; and having fully understood this form and the account [of it], the gods and others [acted accordingly]. (107)
By means of fire they consume food and are satisfied by that meal;
and at various places they wear ornaments of gold. (108)
Thus, having performed the vow of the worship of the ninth lunar day, Vahni and Svarṇa both became liberated, highly esteemed, and wealthy. (10.9)
Indeed, wherever those two go, they always attain purity;
likewise, they always attain growth as well as eternal happiness. (110)
Those people, whether men or women, who shall read or hear this narration of the vow on the ninth day, will attain both worldly enjoyment and liberation.

Thus, in the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā, in the first section concerning the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga, within the *Māhātmya* of the month of Puruṣottama: when the people residing on the Kalpa-vṛkṣa showed disregard for Vahni—the son of Virāṭ—and his son Suvarṇa—who was possessed of defects such as combustibility and dullness—and when [Suvarṇa] was on the verge of death on Mount Meru upon hearing the sound of a drum, he performed the worship of the vow on the ninth day of the intercalary month (*adhimāsa*); consequently, he attained universal honor at sacrifices and other rites, the state of being the mouth of the Lord, and the form of the Lord’s own ornament.
The three hundred and first chapter, titled "The Description of Attaining the Abode and Becoming a Divine Attendant," etc. 1.301.
← Chapter 301: Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā – Section 1 (The Lineage of the Kṛta Yuga) Chapter 302 [[Author:
Chapter 303 →
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Furthermore, O Lakṣmī, I shall relate to you a story that brings delight to the gods;
in the month of Adhimāsa, there is truly no end to the grace of Hari. 1.
On the night of the ninth day, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow questioned Dundubhi: "Is this being proclaimed everywhere, or only in certain places? (2)
The drum spoke: "O Lord, facing whichever direction it may be, I shall proclaim [the message] everywhere from the time of dawn until the time of evening. (3)
Indeed, many embodied beings here perform vows;
they obtain compassion and, from even a slight performance [of the vow], they attain both worldly enjoyment and liberation. (4)
At that moment, the Earth herself arrived there to offer her earnest prayer:
"O Blessed One, Lord of the gods of gods, Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, Mādhava! (5)"
"By you, through your great compassion, the liberation of countless living beings is now being effected during this intercalary month; therefore, I am exceedingly happy. (6)
I too, as the God of gods, must with great reverence perform my vow:
the liberation of those who observe vows during the month of Puruṣottama. (7)
Union with heaven, yoga, wealth, grain, and other riches, as well as sons, grandsons, fame, and whatever else may be desired—may all that come to pass for you. (8)
Out of compassion, let everything be given; it has attained a state equal to Vaikuṇṭha.
Indeed, I am one of blessed fortune, since your drum [has been placed] within me.
With a free voice, he proclaims his magnanimity to all:
"The compassion that was shown by you, the merciful one, during the intercalary month—[how great it was! (10)
Upon me has arisen that very same compassion, so that living beings who partake in my merit shall always become free from sin and pure in me. (11)
O Blessed One, due to the abundance of those devoted to you, I shall be endowed with merit and will never again be oppressed by the burden of evil. (12)
Even during an intercalary month occurring within two and a half years, those people who shall observe your one-day vow—all of them will have their sins cleansed. (1.3)
"And they shall always be capable of uplifting others in me;
thus I am greatly pleased by the attainment of this future well-being. (14)
O Lord, I am oppressed by the burden of the wicked;
for in the future time, wicked people will come to prevail. (15)
O Lord, those Brahmins who are devoid of the Vedas, deprived of the Mother of the Vedas, and lacking in Vedic rites, are merely a burden upon me. (16)
Devoid of purity and contentment, likewise lacking in austerities, and bereft of self-study and devotion to the Lord, they are merely a burden upon me. (17)
Those who are devoid of the vow of non-violence, who are slanderers, who are bereft of truthfulness, who lack the vow of non-stealing, and likewise those who are addicted to sexual misconduct; 18.
Shrouded by craving, they seize the property of others; they are burdensome to me, devoid of compassion, lacking in virtue, and intent on disrespecting others. (1.9)
Those who speak false accusations, those who revile, those who are full of hatred, and those who cannot endure excellence or loftiness—they are always a burden to me. (20)
Those Brahmins who cause suffering to others and themselves, who proclaim faults where there are virtues, and who are intent solely on their own self-interest, remain as a burden upon me. (2.1)

Those who are devoid of ritual bathing and the twilight prayers (saṃdhyā), deprived of the worship of the deities and other rites, lacking steadfastness in the Self and so forth—such dull-witted ones are merely a burden upon me. (22)
Those Brahmins who create obstacles to sacrifices, who destroy the Vaiśvadeva offerings, and who are devoid of the cultivation of purificatory rites, are a burden upon me. (23)
Those who disregard the rules for birth and death impurity, those who propound causation as nihilists, and Brahmins devoid of the worship of Brahman—they are a burden upon me. (24)
Those Brahmins who are devoid of the spirit of devotion, empty of spiritual knowledge (adhyātmavidyā), and lacking in the libations to their ancestors, are merely a burden to me. (25)
Devoid of assistance to others and bereft of the merit of giving, these brahmins have committed unrighteousness through their tongues and genitals; they are merely a burden upon me. (26)
Brahmins who inflict suffering upon others, who obstruct the affairs of others, and who commit offenses against others are a burden to me. (27)
O Brahmins, those who sow seeds in unsuitable ground, farmers who till barren fields, and those who strike at dharma through deceit—these are a burden upon me. (28)
Violent and cruel, they are the cause of others' lamentation; moving with deceptive guile, they conceal their venom while speaking sweet words to deceive. (29)
Those who sprinkle poison through rumors, those who are a burden to me at all times, those who are betrayers of trust, the ungrateful, and those who kill children; || 30 ||
Those who kill the ignorant, those who kill those who have sought refuge, those who destroy their families, and those who kill their mothers, fathers, or wives; ||31||
O Lord, those who destroy the Dharma and destroy liberation are a burden upon me;
they are eaters of forbidden food, those who cause the loss of caste, and those who create social confusion.

Those who cause the destruction of wives and children, those who seize one's livelihood, wealth, or life, those who are wicked in their conduct as assassins, as well as arsonists and poisoners; ||33||

Those who perform acts of killing, exorcism, and sorcery, those who cause abortions and the like, those who strike out of place, and those burdened with cruel deeds—such oppressors have been directed toward me. (34)
Those who are not brahmins yet claim the status of brahmins, who are devoid of their own duties, and who always destroy the happiness of others, are a burden upon me. (35)
Those who lack exertion, who are ever lazy, who subsist on the fortune of others, and who are arrogant even in unauthorized matters, are always a burden upon me. (36)
Those who follow wrong paths, who by their own strength cause distress to the weak, and who inflict punishment upon those who deserve no punishment—these are always a burden to me. (37)
Those who do not protect those who ought to be protected, nor honor those worthy of honor, nor show respect to those deserving of respect—they are a burden upon me. (38)
Those who cause suffering to their cattle, those who fail to protect their dependents, and those who inflict pain upon their servants are always a burden to me. (39)
Teachers who deceive their disciples, and disciples who turn away;
wealthy men who deceive their servants, and laborers who ruin the wealthy. (40)
Both disciples and teachers have abandoned their respective duties;
they deceive one another, and all of them are a burden upon me. (41)
Servants who kill their masters, masters who torment their servants, and slaves who have abandoned their state of servitude—all these burdens are upon me. (42)
Where the king is not a protector and the subjects do not perform meritorious deeds,

those who are deceitful among the subjects, O Queen, all become a burden upon me. In this world, the Kṣatriya is one who does not protect, the Vaiśya is one who does not give, and even the Śūdra is one who does not serve.
O Lord, all those who abandon their respective duties are a burden upon me. 44.
A daughter or even a daughter-in-law who does not carry out her mother's commands is not such [a daughter or daughter-in-law];
and a mother who does not act for one's welfare is not such [a mother], nor is she a mother-in-law. (45)
Where there is no unity between the couple and constant quarreling between the two, the husband is indifferent to his wife's service, and the husband is a source of misery for the wife. 46.
Sons who do not follow their father’s instructions, and a father who reviles his sons—those who lack the relationship of master and servant; all such people are a burden upon me. (47)
A celibate student who does not abide in the practice of celibacy due to passion, yet acts by prioritizing the duties of renunciation while remaining a householder, [is likewise]. (48)
Even a forest-dweller who still possesses craving, or one who has renounced yet lacks true renunciation, or those who adopt other doctrines—all such people are merely a burden. (49)
They cause the mixing of curd, milk, ghee, oil, and meat;
they cause the mixing of food, leaves, grains, vegetables, and flowers. ||50||
Those physicians who cause a confusion of foods, drinks, and medicinal preparations that ought to be carefully maintained, and who bring about the destruction of life—all of them are a burden. //51//
Mortals who consume liquor and meat, who subsist on the food of others, and who cause confusion by appropriating clothing, ornaments, and other such things, are indeed a burden. 52.

Those who deal in counterfeit goods, those with false measures, those who use deceptive scales and weights, those who employ fraudulent counting, and even those who claim to be astrologers, are all embodiments of sin. (53)
Wicked men who deceive through their business dealings—whether in matters of what is to be taken or given—and mortals who forcibly plunder, are always a burden upon me. (54)
On this earth, those who are incompetent, addicted to vices, like the planet Saturn;
those like the eclipse of Rāhu, and likewise those like the bite of a serpent; ||55||
Those who are like flat-nosed monkeys and those who resemble the thorns of the *badarī* tree;
those who are like fish and hawks, and those whose actions are like cranes and cats. (56)
Externally white, red within the heart, and black as collyrium within the self—whether mortals, gods, or dānavas, whether inhabitants of heaven or dwellers of the netherworld. ||57||
All of them are indeed burdensome and are merely performers of evil deeds;
they would afflict me at the time when their own greatness is absent. (58)

Those for whom there is no vow of the intercalary month, nor for whom there is the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), and who possess neither devotion nor a sense of faith—they shall be a burden upon this earth. 5.9.
Therefore, O Hari Kṛṣṇa, from time to time, for the sake of removing the burden of such future beings, the Supreme Lord is entreated by me. (60)
"O Keśava, what should be done by me for the destruction of their burden?
Out of a desire for my own future welfare, tell me that which is most beneficial. (61)
While the Earth was thus entreating her, Dundubhi said to the Medinī:
"O Pṛthvī, have you not heard what I have proclaimed, which grants all desires? (62)
In the intercalary month, a vow should be performed; it shall indeed become eternal merit.
And the Blessed One, Puruṣottama, will grant you protection.
Now, the glorious Lord Hari Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Supreme Master, remains gracious and ready to bestow the fruit; therefore, perform the vow of the tenth day. 64.
At the conclusion of your vow, the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa will himself grant you his vision;
and that descendant of Bharata will provide protection for you at all times. (65)
Go now, O Queen of the Gods, and take up your residence in Satyaloka;
there, observe the vow of the tenth day and pass the intercalary month. ||66||
If that god does not grant you his vision at the conclusion of your vow,
you must certainly come here tomorrow evening to make a request.
Having been addressed thus by Dundubhi himself, she bowed to the Lord, the Master, as well as to Dundubhi, and then departed for Satyaloka. ||68||
In his own abode, on the earth, and on the tenth day, he performed the vow;
having bathed in the morning and meditated upon Hari, he fashioned a golden image. ||69||
Having worshipped Hari with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) and bathed him with auspicious waters, one should smear him with fragrant sandalwood paste and other substances with great devotion. ||70||
With garments, gold, ornaments, saffron, unbroken grains of rice, and excellent leaves;
with sprouts of *tulasī*, lotuses, incense, and lamps. (71)
Having performed worship with excellent offerings, he gave sweet food to Hari;
thereafter, he offered water, betel, desired delicacies, fruit, and the arghya oblation. ||72||

Having performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana), offered a handful of flowers, and likewise performed praise and obeisance, one should then offer circumambulation and a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) upon the ground. ||73||
He paid homage to the Supreme Self, having indeed observed the vow undertaken on the tenth day; "May my night-vow be completed during this intercalary month. (74)
Having thus worshipped in the morning, he worshipped for two watches;
then, having fed [the guests] as desired, he offered [the remains] to the wielder of the Śārṅga bow.
In this manner, he worshipped [him] at evening with these sixteen subordinate articles of offering.
The nightly lamp-offering, the food offering, water, betel-leaf, and fruit. ॥76॥
She offered a handful of flowers to Kṛṣṇa and gave him excellent milk-rice;
then she made him drink it and paid homage to the Compassionate One. ||77||
He performed dancing and singing with vigil until midnight;
then, at the hour of midnight, Lord Hari himself, Śrī Puruṣottama, appeared in person. ||78||
"Speak, O Earth! What is desired by you? I am pleased with your vow; choose a boon.
For one who observes a vow during an intercalary month, I shall indeed grant every desire. (79)
"This is my vow; therefore, whether it be easy or difficult to obtain, whatever it may be, I shall fulfill it in every way. Speak to me here. (80)
Thus addressed, the Earth spoke there to the Supreme Lord:
"O Blessed One, if you are pleased, and if you are one who makes his word true," (8.1)
If you give everything to me, then Puruṣottama is entirely mine;
I desire nothing else but Puruṣottama as my protector. 82.
"O Lord, I indeed always dwell in your service;
O Master, who brings protection to beings, grant me such a divine form. (83)
Moreover, O Great Lord! For the destruction of those who are burdensome, for the eradication of unrighteousness and vices, sport in my world, O Lord!
[Do this] during the other months, excluding the intercalary month, as performed by the people. (84)
You incite me to take up residence [with you] in order to set my own evil ablaze. (85)
O Lord Janārdana, by what means may I always have protection from you, O God?
Come, O Master, either in your divine form or in a physical one. (86)
If your physical body should ever be properly formed and well-developed, then I shall become your mother and I will protect my own son. (87)
I shall cherish you, O Govinda, and I shall feed you with devotion;
I shall perform service for you as you desire, so grant me my request. (88)
Having spoken thus, she ceased and bowed to Puruṣottama;
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, having heard that which had arisen from the heart of the Earth, [acted accordingly]. (89)
And he bestowed upon her a divine form fit for service in Vaikuṇṭha;
she became divine, beautiful, four-armed, and equal to Ramā. ||90||
Then Mādhava, having become the earth, the vast Vasumatī, shone forth;
he led that Vasumatī to Vaikuṇṭha above the waters. (91)
There she remains eternally, having become an exceedingly devoted Vaiṣṇava servant. Now, her second form is in the layer of the earth-enclosure (pṛthivyāvaraṇa).
She is always worthy of dwelling eternally in the abode of the earth;
that goddess is considered to be the presiding deity of all beings. (93)
Commanded by Nārāyaṇa to remain there as a covering for the earth, that [shell] stays eternally above Satyaloka, fixed in place.
As for the third form, which is of the nature of action and consists of earthly materials such as stone and the like—
This entire cosmic egg, consisting of solid matter, was created by Brahmā. ||95||
In that regard, regarding the earth’s burden to be borne as required, Hari indeed promised repeatedly to come to her aid. Hari said: "Listen, O Earth! At the transition of the first age,"
When [the age] has passed, the people will indeed repeatedly become like a burden. 97.
Even in the first age, for the sake of the gods' work, I shall now come to you repeatedly through my granting of boons and because of your devotion. 98.
I shall take incarnations and I shall protect you; do not grieve.
I have been gratified by your vow on the tenth day of the intercalary month.
Therefore, indeed, throughout the four ages, for the sake of those respective tasks,
I shall assume ten principal incarnations and even more than that.
I shall indeed assume many secondary and non-different divine forms according to necessity, and in each of those respective forms, I will provide protection for you.
I shall withdraw the gods and destroy the Dānavas;
I shall crush the Daityas and bring you happiness.
"In this way I shall carry the burden; go, O Goddess, as you please. Having addressed her thus, Hari vanished there in an instant. (103)
The Earth became pleased and again offered a handful of flowers;
having completed the vow, that goddess then bowed to Dundubhi. (104)
She went to her own residence, her palace within the covering of the earth. Thus, O Lakṣmī, having performed the Adhimāsika vow of the tenth day, she departed. (10.5)
By name Vasumatī, she became a maidservant residing in Vaikuṇṭha;
in age after age, day after day, she is ever present at my manifestation. || 106 ||
By my vow, I have made it so that [this] leads to the attainment of all gains;
never has such a gain been bestowed by me upon anyone else unjustly. (107)
Whatever anyone desires, even with a very small vow of mine, I grant that very thing to them; indeed, there is no "no" in that regard. (108)
Whoever shall hear this narrative of Vasumatī and whoever shall read it, will obtain the merit of the vow of the tenth day; of this there is no doubt. (109)

Thus ends the three hundred and second chapter, titled "The Description of the Earth’s Prayer to the Lord in Vaikuṇṭha, the Introduction to the Embodiments of the Burden, the Earth Becoming Vasumatī and Dwelling in Vaikuṇṭha through the Daśamī Vow, and the Lord’s Promise for the Manifestation of His Incarnations in Every Age," in the section on the Greatness of the Month of Puruṣottama within the first book, the *Kṛtayuga-santāna*, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*. 1.302.
