Chapter 304 →

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: O Lakṣmī, listen to the divine narrative of the Ekādaśī of the intercalary month (adhimāsa), which bestows [the grace of] Hari; it was born at the beginning of creation, consisting entirely of austerity.
Born from the chest of Brahmā, the god Dharma exists in embodied form; his consort, the goddess Mūrti, having become invisible, eternally resides within the body of Dharma. (2)
And she, though arising simultaneously with Dharma, appeared according to worldly convention in the form of the daughter of Dakṣa. (3)
Furthermore, according to worldly custom, she was born as the wife of Dharma;
for while Dharma was a god, she remained invisible and unmarried. (4)
Then, O Lakṣmī! that maiden, endowed with celibacy, always serves her husband, who is likewise a celibate, with devotion. (5)
Residing in Satyaloka within the abode of Veda, with Dharma as her companion, Brahmā indeed knows everything regarding her who remains there; others do not know her so situated.
From the very moment they first attain the nature of a child, the ignorant should constantly perform bathing, worship, recitation, fire-offerings, meditation, and service to their master.
He indeed performs bowing and salutation toward the elders; likewise, he practices compassion, tranquility, contentment, straightforwardness, beneficence, and so forth. (8)
Indeed, the qualities of truthfulness, extreme gentleness, and endurance of hardship reside within her form; for that very form, having become perfected through asceticism, abides in austerities. (9)
They remain in the rain during the monsoon, in the cold amidst freezing water and the like,
in the heat of the five fires, and they remain without food during their religious observances.
Constantly wearing wet garments, she would come from the celestial river to her own home, bow to her husband, and perform the worship of Kṛṣṇa. || 11 ||
Having first bathed her husband with water and other substances and having worshipped him,
she gives him food, water, solid food, fruits, and so forth.
She herself, with divine knowledge and supreme devotion, constantly worships her husband with tulasī leaves, lotuses, and pārijātaka flowers. (13)

Thus, having caused her to perform the morning bath every day, the worship of the gods, the honoring of the husband, and the service to the husband, as well as the taking of food and so forth, and having performed these herself; || 14 ||
She is always merged within the body of her husband;
thus, through this constant devotion, she is the most excellent among the best recipients of love. (15)
To Dharmadeva, a daughter was indeed born who bestowed happiness; and Dharmadeva, in turn, was greatly pleased by her devoted service and obedience. (16)
Day by day she receives and bestows upon her auspicious blessings:
"O Mūrtikā, may you always be devoted to serving your husband and remain happy. (17)
According to worldly custom, marry one who has obtained a body and become his servant;
thereafter, be endowed with good fortune, virtuous sons, prosperity, and so forth. (18)
Keśava, who is the form of the fruit of constant devotion, shall be your goal;
he is Hari, Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Brahman, the Lord of Śrī, and the Highest Person. (19)
Thus, that ground of benediction, which is the locus for the accumulation of great merit, [should be performed] every morning like a daily rite on the eleventh day of the intercalary month. (20)
Having gone there to bathe in the celestial river, she heard the sound of a drum:
"O goddesses, today is the Ekādaśī that falls within the month of Puruṣottama."
Satisfied by her vow, the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa will bestow upon her whatever happiness she desires, both of this world and the next. (22)
Whatever merit I bestow for the vows observed on other days of the intercalary month,
I shall grant ten million times that fruit for the vow of Ekādaśī.
Whatever fruit may arise from the observance of other Ekādaśīs, the merit of this one’s vow shall indeed be a hundred million times greater than that. (24)
I am Brahmeshvara, the presiding deity of the intercalary month;
therein also, I am the Lord of the eleventh lunar day, the illustrious Purushottama.
This month is meritorious and this day is meritorious; I am the God and the vow of the Compassionate One is meritorious.
To those who follow my command with devotion, I bestow everything they desire. (26)

In whatever manner the threefold desire may arise in the mind of the performer of the vow, day by day, I grant him a fruit equal to a hundred million times that, as well as prosperity, myself, and my own abode. (27)
I give him my lion-throne; I grant him supernatural powers and wondrous miracles.
Furthermore, I give him the entirety of my sovereignty, my prosperity, my crown adorned with the Kaustubha gem, and my ornaments. ||28||

Just as I have compassionately caused rain to fall during an intercalary month to fulfill the requests of people, so shall I never cause it to rain anywhere else by my own desire, except for the sake of the intercalary month. (29)
Let men, women, children, and the elderly perform this vow for my complete satisfaction;
I shall indeed grant them the fruit of my eternal state, which is most divine and higher than the highest. (30)
Whether it be Goloka, Vaikuṇṭha, or even the unmanifest abode (avyākṛta-dhāma), or Śvetadvīpa, or that which belongs to Sūrya, or others such as the earthly realm (bhauma) and so forth; || 3.1 ||
"Whatever vow one may desire, I shall grant it out of compassion once the vow has been performed;
let my practitioners receive infinite fruit with little effort. (32)
No separate sacrifices need be performed here; no separate austerity need be practiced here;
no separate pilgrimage site need be visited here, for all that is contained within the fruit of a single day. (33)
The milk-vow (payovrata) and the performance of the Putreṣṭi sacrifice are not intended here as separate acts;
for it is said: "By means of the vow of Ekādaśī, I shall grant a son. (34)
Performing the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice is not desired as a separate means of attainment;
I grant heaven to him who observes the vow of Ekādaśī. (35)
Nothing remains for him to achieve through the Rājasūya sacrifice;
by means of the Ekādaśī vow, I grant him sovereignty over the entire earth.
What need has he for the Agnihotra sacrifice to grant him the rank of Vairāja, since on Ekādaśī he offered me fruits, water, and other such gifts? (37)
Whatever satisfaction is sought through various types of ancestral rites (śrāddha) and diverse forms of worship of the gods, that indeed I shall grant through the vow of Ekādaśī. 38.
Whatever liberation, whatever prosperity, whatever accomplishment, or whatever divine yoga one desires— having performed this vow on this day, I shall grant all that here.
Whatever great merit is acquired by those who subsist on fruits for as long as they live—may my people attain that same merit through the Ekādaśī vow. (40)
To him by whom eating once a day has been observed throughout his life, I directly grant the fruit of that merit through the Ekādaśī vow of mine, even more abundantly.
At midnight, that woman who, wrapped in a single moist garment, carries on her head a finger glowing like a burning coal; 42.
Though unaccompanied, the forest-dweller, having gone on foot with his sandals as his only drink, performed the annual vow by worshipping Kālī every day. || 4.3 ||
One should always practice eating only once a day, consuming no more than a single māṣa of food without interruption, during the rainy season, the cold season, and even the hot season. (44)
Having gone and performed worship, he returned to his own home at midnight;
then he should always take the cooked masha-rice and water. (45)
Thus, that great vow which is so very difficult to perform for the sake of obtaining a son should indeed not be performed separately once the Ekādaśī vow has been undertaken. (46)
That which is the Mahākālī vow—whether performed annually or every night—yields a fruit consisting of a son, yet that [fruit] is perishable. (47)
This Ekādaśī vow bestows upon one's sons heaven and liberation;
by means of this single day alone, it grants merit exceeding that of other vows. (48)
The vow of subsisting on air alone for a period of a thousand years need not be performed separately once the Ekādaśī vow has been observed. (49)
Therein is the gift of a thousand maidens, each adorned with ornaments,
along with a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) of one thousand gold coins for each.
For every maiden, however, there were a hundred slave-girls adorned with gold;
and for every slave-girl, there was a hundred elephants accompanied by female calves.
For every elephant there were a hundred horses adorned with gold;
for every horse, a pair of bulls; and for every bull, a chariot. || 52 ||
He who gives a hundred milch cows for every chariot, and a hundred goats for every cow, [attains great merit]. ||53||
Whoever provides for each goat its fodder, its field, and its shelter, that donor obtains at Kurukṣetra during a solar eclipse the same fruit as is obtained there. || 54 ||
Therefore, I grant a hundred-thousandfold merit for the vow of Ekādaśī;
I am Nārāyaṇa, the eternal treasury of merit. (55)
There is no end to my merits; let people receive them like rain.
My resolve is the ground of merit, and my devotion is the ground of liberation. (56)
I, Hari, am the inexhaustible ocean of both resolve and devotion;
free from the fear of emptiness, I surely give, I surely give.
To one who observes the vow on the eleventh day of the month of Puruṣottama,
I give everything— even Kamalā— like one who has renounced madness.
"I myself offer myself; what need is there for anything else?
Therefore, choose as you desire," so spoke the drum of Hari. (59)
"If they do not grant this gain, such a person shall not be taught again.
Having heard this proclamation of the drum, which was the voice of Puruṣottama, [he went]. (60)
That embodied form reflected upon her son Hari, who was born under the auspices of the birth-lagna;
bowing down, she humbly asked Dundubhīśa regarding the ritual procedure for the vow.
Then Dundubhi spoke of the ritual for Ekādaśī:
"Having bathed during the Brāhma-muhūrta and meditated upon Śrī Puruṣottama... (62)
One should worship the Supreme Lord with all ritual offerings without omission;
[one should also worship] the beautiful golden image of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa.

Having placed the offerings along with the ritual services (upacāra) in either five vessels or six vessels, the observer of the vow should then set down a water vessel containing a fine water-pot. 64.
Having consecrated the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) and other substances, one should perform worship upon the image;
first, for the sake of purifying the body, one should arrange three rounds of ceremonial sipping (ācamana). ||65||
Then, having sat down upon an auspicious seat facing the east,
one should invoke Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa into the image accompanied by mantras.
One should ring the bell with auspicious sound at the time of invocation;
one should offer a seat, a cloth, and a golden vessel to the wielder of the Śārṅga bow.
One should offer auspicious water for washing the feet as the *pādya*;
thereafter, one should offer the *tīrtha* water as the *arghya* for the purpose of worship. (68)
Then one should give auspicious water from the sacred site for the purpose of sipping (ācamana);
furthermore, for the sake of complete purification, one should give auspicious water with *darbha* grass.
Then, for the sake of cleansing the teeth, he should indeed provide a tooth-stick;
for the purpose of scraping the tongue, he should provide a golden probe.
Then one should again give pure water for the purpose of rinsing the mouth;
thereafter, one should once more give fresh water for the purpose of washing the face. ||7||
Then, having arranged for purification, one should likewise offer a water-pitcher, or one may also provide earth for the purpose of cleansing the hands and other limbs. (72)
One should indeed offer pure water for the washing of the hands;
thereafter, one should offer pure water for the rinsing of the mouth and so forth. || 73 ||
One should offer a beautiful golden seat made of cloth for the purpose of bathing;
one should then massage the Supreme Lord with fragrant oil. (74)
One should rub the image of Hari with *āmalaka* fruits and sesame powder;
thereafter, one should bathe Puruṣottama with warm water. (75)
Then, having prepared [the image], one should bathe Puruṣottama with milk, curds, ghee, honey, and likewise with water mixed with sugar.
Then one should bathe the Supreme Lord with pure warm water, followed by water mixed with that which produces cleanliness and is slightly warm. ||77||
Having ground the image of Hari with a medicinal pill, one should perform the consecration by bathing it;
then one should apply anointment consisting of musk, sandalwood, the essence of flowers, and other such substances. ||78||
One should wipe Kṛṣṇa with a cloth and put on clean garments;
having applied oil for the grooming of the hair, one should then perform the cleaning of the teeth.
One should apply a moon-shaped tilaka on the forehead with sandalwood and saffron; one should apply collyrium to the eyes and color the lips with rouge. (80)
One should color the palms of the hands, the soles of the feet, and other parts with excellent liquid pigments;
[and likewise adorn the deity] with a golden crown, a garland of fine jewels, earrings, and so forth. 8.1.
Necklaces of gems and pearls, girdles, bracelets, rings, chains, tinkling bells, anklets, and so forth. || 8.2 ||
One should place all the ornaments in their proper positions: one should provide sandals for the feet, and a staff and a garland for the hands. (83)
With the utmost reverence, one should offer beautiful flower garlands, a wreath of tulasī leaves, and clusters and bouquets of flowers around the neck. ||84||
One should offer a sacred thread, a sacrificial cord, and a yoga-band; one should also give a garland of Tulasī beads and an auspicious thread.
One should place the Kaustubha jewel upon it and likewise provide protection for the forearm;
one should place a cloth on the hand and sprinkle sandalwood paste.
One should cause the supreme erotic sentiment (śṛṅgāra) to be depicted as being full of hatred for the King of Kings;
one should likewise provide a parasol, chowries, and a fan that provides a breeze. ||87||
One should provide a mirror for the purpose of viewing the face, as well as a couch, a ball, a bedsheet, a mattress, and a concealed belt. (88)
One should offer a pillow for the cheeks that wards off gadflies and mosquitoes;
having prepared fragrant incense, one should likewise light a lamp. (89)
One should offer white powder, red powder, saffron, and unbroken grains (akṣata).
As an offering (naivedya), one should present sweet laddus, various kinds of food, and excellent milk-porridge (pāyasa). ||90||
One should offer vegetables, green gram soup, curd, milk with sugar, as well as rice with broth, and likewise fried cakes and snacks. 9.1.
One should offer food to be chewed, food to be eaten, food to be licked, food to be sucked, and likewise drink;
one should cause [the deity] to take a mouthful of water and offer betel leaf with lime powder.
One should provide cardamom, cloves, nutmeg, cinnamon, and excellent betel nuts, as well as the fruit of the mango and pieces of rose-apple, jackfruit, and breadfruit. (93)
One should offer grapes, bilva fruits, pomegranates, navaraṅga, and so forth;
one should also offer dried fruits such as badāma, kāju, and khārikā.
Having thus performed the dedication and gratified Hari with devotion, [one should enter] a structure made of plantain trunks and the like, adorned with cloths and other ornaments. ||95||
In the center of the pavilion, which was adorned with arches made of *aśoka* trees, mango leaves, flowers, and fruits, and rendered auspicious by the seven kinds of grain. (96)
There, in the center of that Sarvatobhadra maṇḍala, [one should place] a golden vessel or a copper one filled with water from sacred fords. ||97||
It should be provided with gems, pearls, gold, silver, copper, and so forth;
wrapped in cloth, and furnished with sprouts of mango, Aśoka, and other such trees. (98)
In that well-adorned vessel, worshipped with unbroken grains, sandalwood, and saffron, there is placed a copper or golden bowl. (99)
When that [vessel] has been filled with *khārikā* mangoes, betel nuts, *śrīphala* fruits, sugar, and sesame seeds, one should indeed install Puruṣottama within it. || 100 ||
One should perform the lustration nine times with five wicks soaked in ghee;
thereafter, one should wave a cloth and proceed with water from a conch shell.
One should also wave incense and offer praise that grants one's desires;
one should prostrate like a staff and perform circumambulation five times. (102)
One should ask for forgiveness and offer the arghya again along with fruit;
then, one should indeed present a handful of flowers together with unbroken grains (akṣata) to Śrī Hari. 103.
One should offer a golden seal-ring as a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), and also a silver gift; furthermore, one should present to Hari whatever desired object he wishes for. 104.
One should swing them on a swing and provide them with a bed on a couch; one should massage their feet and give them a vehicle along with its mount. (105)
One should perform dance, as well as song, and likewise play musical instruments;
and there, one should provide the gift of the nectar of the feet to the devotees. || 106 ||
Then, moreover, he should respectfully offer water for drinking;
he should further give betel leaf along with cardamom, cloves, and other such ingredients. (107)
Having embraced Mīla with both arms and pressed Hari joyfully, one should then cause the deity to depart; having gone a certain distance, one should bid him farewell. (108)
One should say, "Please return," and after bowing, he should go back home.
Thus, with one hundred and eight modes of service, [one worships] the Supreme Lord. (109)

On the eleventh day, the observer of the vow should worship with great devotion in the morning; if one possesses abundant wealth, one should cause fire-offerings, sacrifices, and other rites to be performed. (11.0)
On the twelfth day, one should feed the Brahmins, virtuous women, chaste wives, and good people;
thereafter, having fed one's own dependents, one should perform the breaking of the fast.
One should give excellent gifts and joyfully worship Śrī Hari;
in this manner one should act at midday, and likewise in the evening. (11.2)
At night, one should keep a vigil preceded by dance and song;
one should perform the chanting of the glories of Śrī Hari and restrain the senses. 1.13.
Thus, whoever performs the Ekādaśī vow during an intercalary month here has performed everything that ought to be done; nothing remains to be left undone. (114)
The intercalary month is exceedingly meritorious, and the eleventh lunar day (Ekādaśī) is indeed meritorious;
that deity is purifying, and so am I—what could possibly surpass that? || 1.15 ||
The intercalary month is my abode; I dwell there as the Supreme Person. The Ekādaśī was born from me—how could anything surpass it? 1.16.
This triad is of great merit and has attained supremacy over all things;
even therein, my grace has been obtained—what could possibly exceed this? (1.17)
Therefore, having worshipped me with these one hundred and eight articles, may you either reach the further shore of existence or attain equanimity toward existence. (1.18)
O embodied one, perform the vow today according to the prescribed rite, so that Kṛṣṇa, whose self is the drum, will grant you whatever you desire. (1.19)
Then the Mūrti indeed spoke to Dundubhi with humility:
"There is no completeness [of my form] before me, for I dwell in concealment. (120)
"In what manner indeed should the worship prescribed by you be performed by me?
I desire an auspicious birth, a marriage, and a son who is Hari. (121)
"Without him, such worship would be difficult to obtain and not as desired.
Having said this, her heart was broken and she became choked with tears. (1.22)
Having made the formal resolve (saṃkalpa) that "the vow of Ekādaśī must be performed," she grieves; remembering Nārāyaṇa-Kṛṣṇa, the young woman sheds tears. (123)
At that moment, Hari Nārāyaṇa himself, a treasure-house of compassion, having shown mercy, became clearly manifest before Dundubhi. (1.24)
Wiping away the tears of the maiden, he said: "O mother, I bow to you; do not grieve, for you are worthy of honor. I shall grant you whatever you desire. (1.25)
I am always pleased by existence, never by non-existence;
being satisfied by your devotion, I grant [this]; choose that boon. (1.26)
Even if one who is devoid of devotion were to worship with thousands of articles, I am not satisfied here by such a practice that accomplishes the goal while lacking devotion. (127)
Even my worship performed with leaves, flowers, and water, when done with heartfelt devotion, brings me satisfaction; for I am hungry for such devotion. (128)
O Mother, worship me with the one hundred and eight types of internal offerings, even through mere meditation within yourself.
I shall accept this mental worship of yours with great devotion;
indeed, I shall grant you the desired fruit of today’s vow.
Having spoken thus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama,
bowed at the feet of the image with the feeling of a mother, like a son.
Having cast off her grief, the mother became serene within her heart and spoke softly to Kṛṣṇa: "I desire a worldly birth. (13.2)
I desire a Vedic marriage bond with a husband who is righteous;
I wish to cherish a son upon my lap, a child of extraordinary nature. (133)
You alone are transcendent; my mind does not dare to speak further.
I have disclosed what is in my heart; do with it as you wish. (1.34)
Having heard these words of his beloved, the most excellent desire of his heart, from the mouth of the Divine Form, Hari— who was bearing his future birth— rejoiced.
Being exceedingly pleased, he said: "O Mother, everything shall come to pass;
I shall do all that is desired and grant your word. (136)
Go to the house of Dakṣa, O Mūrti, having taken leave of Dharma, your virtuous husband;
become the daughter of Dakṣa, for he will give you to Dharma. (1.37)
"O Mother, tomorrow I shall take birth upon your lap together with my brother in the form of a child; you may go after completing your vow. (138)
"For you, O mother, shall indeed become the daughter of Dakṣa through your mental birth;
then, having married you, Dharma will dwell upon the snowy mountain."
There, I myself shall be born as your mind-born son with fourfold nature; Nara, Nārāyaṇa, Hari, and Kṛṣṇa shall be your sons in your home.
I shall take delight, O Giver of Happiness, always maintaining the vow of Brahman and fulfilling my resolve for the welfare of the world in your presence. (141)
Having spoken thus and bowed once more, Puruṣottama vanished;
and the image, having performed the vow, also offered mental worship there.

Having performed the breaking of the fast on the twelfth day and having performed worship in his heart at dawn, he received the auspicious command of Dharmadeva with a firm and virtuous resolve. (143)
From his mere resolve, he begot a mental daughter, Asiknī, who gave birth to him;
furthermore, twelve other daughters, beginning with Śraddhā and Maitrī, were also born. (144)
Thirteen daughters were also given by Dakṣa to Dharma;
from his form were born Nara, Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, and likewise Hari. (145)
"Performing supreme austerity for the sake of protecting the worlds"—thus has it been told to you, O Lakṣmī, regarding the month of Puruṣottama. (146)

By the mere resolution to undertake a vow, the full fruit of that vow shall be attained; how much more so for the performer who acts according to the complete ritual procedure with all its ancillaries—what fruit could possibly remain unattained? (147)
Therefore, there shall be no other vow equal to Ekādaśī;
it bestows eternal and inexhaustible true merit, as well as liberation. (148)
"Having made a formal resolve for worship in the morning with whatever materials are available, those who shall perform the vow—in their homes I shall always reside. (149)

I shall indeed dwell there, of this there is no doubt; having come under their control through devotion to them, I will bring happiness to the couple who observe their vows by becoming their son and restoring their lineage. (150)

Thus ends the three hundred and third chapter, titled "The Description of the Birth of the Mūrti in the House of Dharma’s Righteous Consort, Her Marriage with Dharma, and the Attainment of the Fruit of Four Sons—Nara, Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, and Hari—in the Himālayas," within the *Puruṣottama-māsa-māhātmya* of the first section, the *Kṛta-yuga-santāna*, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*. In this chapter, it is related how, when the vow of worshipping Nārāyaṇa with one hundred and eight mental offerings (*mānasopacāra*) was performed by Dharmadeva on the Ekādaśī of an intercalary month (*adhimāsa*) through his future wife in the form of a *mūrti*, that *mūrti* was born in the house of Dharma’s right-hand consort. Subsequently, she was married to Dharma, and thereafter, in the Himālayas, she obtained the fruit of four sons named Nara, Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, and Hari. Thus concludes the narrative.

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī! He who has manifested the power of all appearances is the Supreme Brahman;
known as Puruṣottama, he is the Sun, the Lord of the universe. (1)
Kṛṣṇa himself, whose very nature is Kṛṣṇa, brought forth Rādhā from Himself.
Rādhā is the power (śakti) whose essence is Kṛṣṇa; she is the one who empowers the deeds of devotees.
As the creative power of the Sun-like Kṛṣṇa, she brings forth the entire world of moving and non-moving beings.
Indeed, that Rādhā is eternally present in Goloka for the service of Kṛṣṇa.
(3) Desiring to assume another form in order to continuously bring forth the world produced from herself, she then gave birth to a daughter. (4)
That girl, named Sāvitrī, who bestows progeny,
sports with Rādhā in her own palace in Goloka;
she is beautiful, endowed with divine power, and enchanting to the world.
Endowed with the accomplishment of all her desires and possessing hidden sovereignty and other such qualities,
when Rādhā herself engages in the service of Kṛṣṇa,
then the maiden Sāvitrī remains absorbed in meditative concentration.
The Mother, consisting of the bliss of the Self, eternally delights in the Self;
immersed in the supreme happiness of the Self, she meditates indeed upon the Supreme Brahman.
(8) By the power of her practice of yoga and through the perfection of her birth, she desired to behold [the Lord].

What is the nature of Brahmā’s form, and how many such forms are there? (9) Where do they abide, what are their functions, and where do they dwell? What are his sovereign powers, and what indeed are his manifestations? (10)
Having understood all this, the Yoginī, withdrawing her vital breaths into herself, gradually descended into the mūlādhāra-cakra. Remaining there at Gaṇapati, she performed *saṃyama*.
Thereupon, beholding the abodes of countless lords of the Gaṇas who were manifestations of a portion of Śrī Kṛṣṇa within infinite universes,
the beautiful lady abandoned the wheel situated at the root of her secret passage and proceeded to the front.
She held the wheel called Svādhiṣṭhāna for the purpose of *saṃyama*.
Abiding there in Prajāpati, she performed *saṃyama*.
By that [means], [she beheld] the countless Lords of Creatures, whose nature is the Supreme Brahman.
Having beheld the abodes within the infinite cosmic eggs,
that beautiful woman went to the Maṇipura-cakra situated in the root-center (nābhikanda).
Having stayed there and having practiced self-restraint upon the serpent, she remained.
The beautiful [energy] entered upward through the upper-opening [nāḍī] into countless worlds;
from there, innumerable great channels consisting of light also proceed—some toward the netherworlds and some beyond the world-mountains. (17)
Some [paths] lead to the realms beginning with heaven and ending with Satya; some lead to the worlds of Āvaraṇa and the others;
some to the worlds of the Lord (Īśvara); and some even to the abodes of Brahmā.
Whichever beautiful woman goes to whichever place, she does so by whichever path leads there.
Having beheld the divine realms and the splendors of the cosmic egg throughout many worlds, he returned once more to that place; then,
he ascended further upward to the heart-center, the wheel known as Anāhata.
There, having heard the *praṇava*, he practiced self-restraint within Brahman.
When the Self, the Inner Self, and the Self of Brahman are manifested by itself,
then through that practice and restraint, Sāvitrī is brought under one's mastery.
In the abodes of the Vairājas, Bhaumanas, and Vaiṣṇavas,
as well as in the Prākṛta and Sādāśiva coverings—
having beheld those divine grounds within each of those abodes, Sāvitrī [proceeded].
Returning again to that place, she ascended to the throat;
indeed, by her power, she exercised restraint over the wheel of Viśuddha.
[She likewise restrained] Vāsudeva, Aniruddha, Pradyumna, and Saṅkarṣaṇa.
Having observed the construction of those abodes, which were the very manifestations of splendor,
she returned once more to the region of the throat and then to the eyebrows.
Having gone there and reached the *ājñācakra*, she gradually performed *saṃyama*.
There she beheld the Guru in person, whose nature is the Supreme Brahman—
He who was born as the all-pervading Creator of the universe for the sake of guiding the world, and who,
manifesting from the essence of the Supreme Brahman, became the author of the Vedas. (27–28)
Brahmā, the teacher of all the worlds and the grandfather of all creatures,
beheld his own divine Sāvitrī seated upon his lap;
having recognized her as the wife of the Creator, that exceedingly beautiful woman rejoiced greatly.
She reflected for a moment: "I who am a resident of Goloka—how have I come to be here today? Why do I see myself seated upon his lap?
From where has this form of mine, resting upon Aja’s thigh, come?"
"Since I clearly perceive myself here in the form of a bride and my grandmother as well, I shall ask the reason for all this right here.
Having said this, she went forward to inquire, but at that moment she vanished from sight.
Drawn away by her grandmother, the beautiful Sundarī became absorbed [in meditation].
Just then, Sāvitrī emerged from her concentration.
"Where is the maiden residing in Goloka, and where is the grandmother seated upon the lap of Brahmā? || 33-34 ||
Thus, filled with wonder at the certainty of the matter she had seen, the maiden went in haste to where Rādhikā shone, in order to inform her;
Sāvitrī reported to Rādhikā the very object she herself had perceived.
Having heard that, Rādhā said to her: "O maiden, you are my own form;
you exist as the power of Brahman, having assumed a physical body for the sake of Brahman.
You are she who is considered the supreme power of Māyā, whose nature is the progenitor of the universe. (36–37)
I am she, and you are that Sāvitrī, the mother of the world being born;
the consort of Brahmā, the body of Brahmā, created for the sake of Brahmā.
United with the Grandfather, you are eternally the grandmother of the universe.

Because you are beginningless, O Great Illusion (Mahāmāyā), you appear ever anew at every moment; yet from my own nature, you become a maiden. Now, worship that God, and by the power of your asceticism, you shall attain him.
Having heard this, Sāvitrī reflected upon the attainment of Brahman; then,
on that twelfth day, at dawn,
she heard the drum of the God of gods proclaiming words of compassion.
O goddesses, perform the Adhimāsa-vrata which bestows the mind’s fulfillment.
Whether seen within the heart or perceived externally in this world or even in other worlds,
Puruṣottama will grant it by means of a single day's vow alone.
Today is the day of Hari, a merit possessing infinite virtues;
by performing the Trispṛśā vow today, the fruit is a thousandfold. Indeed, by practicing eating once a day (ekabhakta) or eating only at night (nakta), one obtains whatever is desired.
Or subsisting on fruits, or drinking milk, or eating curd;
or subsisting on water, or subsisting on ghee, or eating sesame seeds;
or subsisting on barley, or subsisting on vegetables, or eating tubers.
Or else, having undertaken an auspicious vow, one may subsist on roasted grain, or eat only leaves,
or eat only flowers, or fast entirely, or subsist only on air;
or one may perform the vow by eating only smoke or eating only vapors.
On this twelfth day of the intercalary month, may they attain eternal bliss—
the supreme Brahman, as well as Brahmaloka, Goloka, the immortal station,
the unmanifest Vaikuṇṭha, and the Vaiṣṇava realm of Māyā. ||48-49||

By means of this vow, they shall indeed acquire the abodes within the terrestrial and other coverings— whether it be the station of Sadāśiva, or the empire of Bhūman, or the city of Śrī, or the sovereignty of Vairāja, or that of Hiraṇyagarbha.
Whether it be the abode of Satya, or that of Brahmā, or that of Vahni, or indeed that of Sūrya;
or the abode of Candra, or that of the Nakṣatras, or even that of Grāha;
or the abode of Indra, or of Varuṇa, or of Yama, or even that of Kubera. (5.1–5.2)
Whether it be the realm of Īśāna, or the purifying realm of Vāyu, or the liberating realm of Nairṛta;
or the sovereignty over the earth, or the subterranean realms such as those of the Cātaleyas;
or the divine enclosures and the majestic sovereignties of the gods.
Whether it be the state of a celibate student (kaumāra), the state of a householder (brāhma), or the auspicious state of a forest-dweller (yāuga);
or the realm of Śvetadvīpa and other such places, as well as the oceanic or celestial realms;
or even a universal sovereignty over the earth or a human empire—[he attains these]. 54–55.
The sage’s silence, the ancestral rites, the divine state which bestows many perfections, the kingdom of women, Kailāsa, the eternal kingdom of desire,
or the supreme sovereignty of devotion to her husband consisting of service to her lord.
Possession of a wife, possession of a husband, the excellent fortune of sons and daughters,
health, wealth, grain, and physical elixirs—
whatever one may desire, let the observer of the vow obtain it today on the twelfth day, the day of Hari.
I, the Supreme Person, bestow all of that upon him; I declare:
"Today, having bathed in the morning, he should perform my worship within his home;
remaining there, he should practice meditation on me and perform the invocation and other rites. (59)
Then, one should perform my bath with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) as well as a cleansing immersion in pure water. After that, one should offer garments, ornaments, and sandalwood paste.
Furthermore, according to one's ability, one should perform the offering of incense, lamps, and prostrations.
One should offer fruits, roots, and the like, or various sweet foods, as the *naivedya* (food offering).
Then one should present betel leaf (*jāmbūla*), drinking water, a monetary gift (*dakṣiṇā*), and perform a prostration.
One should also perform circumambulation (*pradakṣiṇa*), recite hymns of praise (*stuti*), perform the waving of lights (*ārātrika*), and offer a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*).
One should offer the arghya with saffron, unbroken rice, tulasī, and fruits.
Having bowed again and meditated once more, one should pray for one's desired object:
"O Keśava, by your worship, may my vow also be fulfilled. (63–64)
One should seek forgiveness by praising the golden image of Hari:
"The proper sequence and its omission were not understood, nor was your desired purpose known.
Whatever has been performed by me with devotion according to my intellect—even if deficient—please grant forgiveness. (65)
O Lord of gods! O Sovereign who brings about the extra rains! You are indeed the intercalary month [that bestows grace].
O Supreme Person! You grant that which is most desired by those who seek your favor.
O Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, Viṣṇu, Lord of Pārvatī, Lord of splendor! || 66–67 ||
O Lord of Lakṣmī, O Lord of Māṇikī, O Lord of Sāvitrī, O Sovereign of the Universe! O Creator of the World, O Beloved of Rādhikā, O Beloved of Kamalā, O Keśava!
By virtue of my vow on this twelfth lunar day, fulfill today that which is desired by my mind.
Having thus entreated Hari and bowed down at dawn, midday, and midnight, one should become entirely absorbed in Him,
dedicating all virtuous actions to Him; then,
one should delight Him with dance and song accompanied by musical instruments, and finally bid Him farewell.
Having thus properly undertaken the vow and performed the worship,
Whether they be inhabitants of the netherworld or such like among the ranks of men—
lords and their consorts, or those who are liberated and their liberated consorts—
if they desire you, they shall obtain you; I promise this, there is no doubt.
According to one's capacity and according to what is required, one should perform my vow and worship;
even in the absence of external materials, there is excellent worship within my heart through a distinct state of being.
I am pleased by that person's disposition and love, and I grant [the fruit] to them as well.
"O Supreme Lord, today, during this intercalary month, I am raining down compassion.
Just as I have rained today, so have I never done before, nor shall I do so in the future.
Therefore, by my grace, let my devotees perform some vow. (75-76)
"May they obtain eternal merit, happiness, and their heart's desire for the world.
Having heard this, the exceedingly beautiful Sāvitrī rejoiced greatly.
Bowing down to Dundubhi, she said: "Listen, O skillful one created by fate!"
While I was in meditative absorption, I beheld Brahmā, the Supreme Lord and Grandfather;
and on his left lap sat Sāvitrī. She was seen by me as having my own form, and at that time I dissolved into her.
Furthermore, O maiden, I have arisen here from my meditative absorption;
this very Creator of the universe, who resides within my mind, is the husband I must attain.
Therefore, on the twelfth day of the intercalary month, my vow is to eat but a single meal.

I shall perform the worship of the God of gods according to my strength. (8.1) Indeed, the attainment of that eternal abode of Goloka is difficult for me to reach with this body; yet, I possess this physical form as a manifestation of His opulence. (8.2)
He possesses a body born of reality, a son of Vairāja, which is well-compacted.
Therefore, tell me how and by means of what body my union with Brahmā may arise;
I shall perform the vow of Dvādaśī accordingly.
Having heard this, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama) spoke to Dundubhi:
"Listen, O auspicious Sāvitrī! Today, have an image fashioned in the form of the son of Agni, Suvarṇa, for Śrī Puruṣottama."
Likewise, have an image of Lakṣmī fashioned in the form of gold;
and likewise, make Brahmā and his Sāvitrī out of gold.
Having worshipped them according to your ability, bestow gifts upon worthy recipients.

"Thus indeed, while you are under this vow, perform worship and also give gifts. By that, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person, will be pleased and will accomplish every purpose for you; do not worry, O maiden. (87-88)
Having heard this from Sāvitrī at the dawn of the twelfth day of her vow,
he gathered a golden portion from the peak of Meru by the power of yoga;
and through his sovereign power, he likewise brought Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa to that very place.
Having fashioned an image of Brahmā and Sāvitrī out of gold,
he invoked them, bathed them, adorned them, and worshipped them; then,
having fed them and given them water to drink, he made his request and performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana).
Having asked for forgiveness, praised them, and disclosed the purpose dwelling in his heart,
Hari himself appeared before Sāvitrī, accompanied by Lakṣmī, just as he was dismissing those gods.
With a serene countenance, enriched with all splendor, and bestowing boons, he said to her:
"Speak, O auspicious lady, what dwells in your mind?
Sāvitrī replied to the Lord of Gods: "Grant me the yoga of Brahmā. (93–94)
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa said: "That which has arisen in your mind is known to me. Close your eyes, Sāvitrī, and meditate upon me for a moment;
then everything you desire shall come into the palm of your hand. (95)
He practiced with devotion exactly as it was taught by Nārāyaṇa.
At that very moment, Nārāyaṇa-Kṛṣṇa vanished.
Then, having worshipped in this manner in the morning, he did likewise at midday.
In the evening as well, she likewise performed worship and kept a vigil;
having placed Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Lakṣmī, the Unborn One (Brahmā),
and Sāvitrī upon the swing, the young girl rocked them back and forth repeatedly.
Then Śrī Puruṣottama, having returned there once more, spoke again:

"O Goddess, having repeatedly offered handfuls of flowers, water for the guest-offering (arghya), fruit, and water, perform the ritual dismissal (visarjana) of me here; I am going to the imperishable abode."
Go this very day to the Vairāja realm from which Brahmā was born;
enter that Vairāja state in its subtle form, and thereafter,
O daughter, become the mental daughter of that [Brahmā] from his navel.

As soon as you are born, Vairāja will give you, a young woman, to Āja. By the very ordinance of the Lord, he shall employ you in his ritual act. O auspicious one, go; may it be well with you, and may your good fortune be eternal.

Having spoken thus, Śrī Hari Nārāyaṇa vanished there. Sāvitrī, having offered a handful of flowers to the form of Śrī Hari, and having presented the *arghya* and the *śrīphala*, performed the ritual dismissal (*visarjana*) of the deity.

He gave a gift of gold in the form of idols for the sake of Vedic splendor to the preceptor named Patnīvra, who dwells in the abode of Goloka. Then, having received his blessing, she said: "May you become a beautiful woman endowed with good fortune. (105–106)
"Be the wife of Brahmā and the progenitor of the worlds! Having thus spoken, she bowed to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa and immediately vanished from sight.
She then entered the Vairāja world, having emerged through the stalk of his navel.
Having reached puberty, that maiden Sāvitrī then became a young woman.
As soon as she was born, the Creator, knowing her purpose for Brahmā,
gave her who had appeared into the assembly of the Lord according to the prescribed rite.

Having attained Brahmā as her husband, the Lord, that Mother of the World also became one whose desires were fulfilled; she [became] the four-faced Brahmā. Thus, O Lakṣmī, I have told you the reason for the Dvādaśī vow.
Sāvitrī’s attainment of the status of Brahman’s consort, exactly as it occurred, bestows the fulfillment of one's desires. (111)

Thus ends the three hundred and fourth chapter, titled "The Description of how Brahmā, while in meditation, beheld the creation of the individual soul, the Lord, and Brahmā himself within the form of Sāvitrī—the other manifestation of Rādhikā—and seeing his own presence there, desired to obtain her as his wife, and upon hearing the sound of a drum, attained Brahmā as his husband through the vow of Dvādaśī," in the section on the Greatness of the Month of Puruṣottama within the lineage of the Kṛta Yuga in the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*. (1.304)

Chapter 306 →
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī! By virtue of the vow on the thirteenth day of the intercalary month, Puruṣottama [was pleased] by the four daughters of Brahmā who had previously observed it. (1)
The Lord himself became their husband and gave them his imperishable abode as a home;
out of compassion, the Master granted them eternal worldly enjoyment and liberation. (2)
O Lakṣmī! In the first Kṛta Yuga, long ago, for the purpose of creation, Brahmā [beheld] the youths named Sanaka, Sananda, Sanātana, and Sanatkumāra. (3)
Four [beings] were created, endowed with sovereignty, power, and splendor;
and for them, four Śaktis were indeed fashioned for the sake of matrimony.
By name they were Jayā, Lalitā, Pārvatī, Prabhā, and Śubhā; they were similar to him, and they were his mental daughters, as he was their mental son. (5)
Having created four pairs, he became exceedingly pleased upon seeing that these [beings], as soon as they were born, were indeed possessed of discernment.
To appoint them to the task of creation, the Creator of the Universe spoke to each one individually:
"O Sanaka, accept this Jayā, who has been fashioned for your sake. (7)
"Sanandana, accept this Lalitā who has been prepared for you;
Sanātana, accept this Pārvatī who has been given to you. (8)
"Accept this radiance given by me; make it your companion.
Having become pairs, indeed four pairs shall you be. (9)
Let them create a mental creation consisting entirely of pairs;
such a tradition of domestic dharma was obtained from Goloka. (10)
Even in Vaikuṇṭha, such a tradition of domestic duties is likewise seen;
by the command of Kṛṣṇa, we respectfully observe these household duties.
Likewise, O sons! You too, having accepted the duties of a householder approved by your father and having fulfilled those household duties, may indeed become happy in this world. (12)
Having appointed you to the task of creation, I too shall once again be freed from the burden of creation and thus become one who has fulfilled his purpose. (13)
In the dharma of the household, O sons, lineages always become saviors;
in the dharma of the household, even women become bestowers of happiness. (14)
In the dharma of the householder, sacrificial rites and offerings arise from devotion:
the honoring of guests, the worship of the gods, and the honoring of the virtuous. (15)
Hospitality toward those in other stages of life arises, as does giving that bestows heavenly rewards; the fulfillment of desires is protected, and wealth is acquired. (16)
The three goals of human life culminate in liberation, which is attained eternally thereafter;
yet, without the dharma of the household, there can indeed be no cessation of the flow of the gunas. (17)
Whether in childhood or in youth, knowledge does not arise that bestows dispassion;
therefore, one should indeed pacify the mind only after providing it with enjoyment. (18)
But for those whose minds are perfectly tranquil, eternal liberation occurs.
Therefore, O sons, perform the duties that ensure the stability of creation! (19)
Having thus heard these words of Brahmā, the four sons of the Creator were already wise and likewise possessed of yoga from the very beginning. (20)
Only these knowers of Brahman are firmly resolved upon the goal of liberation;
liberation does not come through action, O father, for action is indeed bondage. (21)
Even there, the domestic rituals are indeed bonds;
the duty of a woman does not become a cause for liberation. (22)
Furthermore, driven by passion, one continues to perform actions subsequent to previous karma;
indeed, in that state, the pursuits of dharma, artha, and kāma do not exist at all. (23)
Therefore, O Father, without knowledge, the duty of household life is fraught with fear;
the duty of household life is a burden, just as you desire it to be abandoned. (24)
Likewise, we do not desire to carry that burden from this day forward;
for, O sons, those who are called "tārakas" (saviors) are indeed those whose essence is *jñāna* (liberating knowledge). ||25||
That indeed is what is called a "son" for the wise and the yogis;
however, for those who perform ritual actions and whose nature is not free from the desire to act, sons are merely progeny. (26)
May our lineage, O knowers of Brahman, be liberated;
may they be the bestowers of the path to Brahman and dwellers in the world of Brahman. (27)
For the sake of our transient lineage, we shall not engage in domestic life;
association with women is delightful outwardly, but in its ultimate consequence, it is misery within. (28)
What person who knows the truth would resort to that [worldly pleasure], having abandoned his own innate bliss?
The bliss of the Self is declared to be supreme; any other pleasure brings about its end. //29//
O Grandfather, those sacrifices and rituals prescribed for the duties of a householder are not equal, even by a fraction, to the task of propitiating Brahman. (30)
For us who possess knowledge, the propitiation of Brahman alone is considered the sacrifice here;
when the propitiation of Brahman is performed, the honoring of guests is thereby accomplished. (3.1)
The worship of the gods and other rites have been performed, and the honoring of the virtuous has been accomplished;
for when Hari is constantly honored, everything indeed becomes honored. (32)
O Father, the gift of the knowledge of Brahman is eternal;
it is obtained in heaven, and indeed, that alone is the state of liberation. (33)
That which is not intermingled with suffering and the like, and which is not swallowed up at the end, but is produced by the attainment of true resolve—that is the eternal state in heaven. (34)

The law of time (death) befalls one who possesses craving, but never anyone who delights in the Self; nor is there any need for objects such as food, water, and clothing, or for any other objects. //35//
For one who conducts oneself in this way, liberation rests in the palm of the hand;
it is the relinquishing of the flow of qualities through the duties of a householder. //36//
One must awaken from mere hope; indeed, those who abide in the qualities of the gunas are submerged.
For them there is no childhood, nor has youth ever arrived. (37)
And within the Self of all, there indeed exists cessation devoid of enjoyment;
the mind is perfectly colored by Brahman, whose very form is peace. (38)
For them, liberation is not dependent on whether they possess a body or are bodiless;
he is indeed declared to be eternally liberated, he is indeed considered eternally liberated. (39)
Untouched by joy, resentment, fear, or agitation, he is indeed liberated.
Therefore, we are not entitled to creation; we are merely the instruments of Brahmā. (40)
Free from duality, we shall also make others devoid of dualities.
This indeed is the father of his father’s father’s father’s father. (41)
The Dharma consisting of the Upaniṣads belongs to the one known as Puruṣottama;
we shall go before that very Supreme Self. (42)
Whatever indeed ought to be done hereafter, let that be performed this very day;
provided there exists within one's own treasury the means for its execution. (43)
But for us, through the grace of our father, self-restraint arises spontaneously within ourselves; it is a source of happiness and a means to liberation. (44)
Therefore, O father, from childhood onward we shall dwell in liberation, and not otherwise;
for when we are liberated, you too will be liberated—of this there is no doubt. (45)
"Know for certain that we sons are truly named Tārakas;
these maidens, however, are yoginīs, the very embodiments of knowledge and discernment. (46)
"They shall attain Brahman itself in a very short time; do not grieve.
Having spoken thus to his sons, he departed toward the river Viṣṇupadī. ||47||
And the maidens Jayā, Lalitā, Pārvatī, and Prabha, perfected in the yoga of the supreme self, meditated upon Puruṣottama. ||48||
They constantly worshipped Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa with great reverence;
they performed the recitation: "Oṃ, obeisance to You, Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. (49)
Thus, on the thirteenth day, at the very dawn of the Satyaloka, the compassionate proclamation of the drum was heard. (50)
Whosoever is endowed with Brahman, or even one separated from Brahman—whether she be a newborn infant, a young maiden, a woman of noble form, or one free from passion. || 5.1 ||
Whether she be an elder woman, or fortunate, or a married woman, or one who has left her husband; whether she be full of passion, or self-possessed, or even one who strives for liberation. || 5.2 ||

Whether she be without a protector or with a protector, conditioned or even unconditioned; whether she be in a good state or not established in a state, or else possessed of the impulse toward departure. ||53||

Whether she has given her word or not, whether she is worthy of giving or devoid of the act of giving, or even if she was created for the purpose of giving—such a woman should observe the Trayodaśī vow. (54)
I am Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person, the bestower of their desires; for whomever among them anything new and fresh is required during this intercalary month.
Whether it be inaccessible or easily accessible, obtainable or unobtainable—whether obtainable through merit, obtainable through wealth, or obtainable even by means of spiritual practices. (56)
Whether it be inconceivable or conceivable, eternal or transient, enjoyable or indeed non-enjoyable—whatever else she desires in her heart. ||57||
Being pleased, I, Puruṣottama, shall grant all of that to you for having performed this vow of eating but one meal on the thirteenth lunar day. ||58||
One should perform the vow with faith, preceded by my worship, either by eating only at midnight or by subsisting on fruits alone. (59)
I, the Supreme Lord, am her leader, her guide, her protector, and her nourisher; I am the doer of good, the giver of refuge, and likewise her one who brings joy. (60)
Whether they be men, women, or others, whoever worships during the intercalary month on the thirteenth lunar day, I shall grant them their desires with sandalwood and other offerings. (61)
With one hundred and eight, or indeed with fifty-six,
or with thirty-two offerings, and with the sixteen and other such ritual substances.
Or let them worship me with whatever leaves, flowers, water, food, and rice they may obtain, or even through mental offerings and gifts of love. (6.3)
Let people offer me either a handful of flowers or a handful of love;
I shall, in turn, fill their minds with the fulfillment of generosity.
Let them not feel hesitation; let them speak, or retain [the teachings] in their hearts, or form mental resolves within their minds; I shall bestow [these] upon those who have undertaken the vow.
Having heard this on the morning of the thirteenth day regarding Dundubhi, who had taken refuge in Hari,
Jayā, Lalitā, Pārvatī, and Prabhā arrived there.
Then they approached that Dundubhi and asked, "What indeed will you give?
Dundubhi replied, "I shall give either heaven or Puruṣottama. (67)
I give as the price for the Trayodaśī vow my husband Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, along with his riches and even his abode known as Akṣara.
In the intercalary month, I am the giver of what is excessive even when the vow is small;
I am manifest as the very soul of the intercalary month within the circle of creation.
I grant you the eternal Brahman: truth in heaven, the state of Parameṣṭhin, Vairāja, Bhaumana, Dhruva, Goloka, and Vaikuṇṭha as well.
"What do you ladies desire? I shall grant the excellent fruit of your vow.
Hearing this, those four then joyfully spoke to Dundubhi: |||7||1||
"As soon as we were all born, we were indeed unrefined; may we become refined by being united with Kṛṣṇa, united with his abode. (72)
May that Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa come to us;
through this vow, we desire nothing other than to become His maidservants today. (73)
Then the Dundubhī spoke: "O ladies, today indeed with joy, having bathed in the morning, you should worship Puruṣottama made of gold. (74)
With whatever offerings are available, and with mental services imbued with devotion, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, who is the refuge for those hungry for love, will accept them. (79)
"You possess divine forms and are worthy of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa;
having performed the vows and worship today, may you attain the supreme Hari. (76)
Having spoken thus, Dundubhi departed from that place to another;
and Jayā, Lalitā, Pārvatī, Vrata, and Prabhā [performed their rites]. ||77||
Having bathed and returned home, they constructed an excellent pavilion;
on the morning of the thirteenth day, they worshipped Puruṣottama.
Having prepared a lion-throne in the center and placed there a golden image of Hari, they invoked the deity and joyfully offered water and other ritual substances. (79)
Having caused [the deity] to bathe with the waters of the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), [one should offer] garments, all ornaments, and substances such as saffron and sandalwood. 80.
Incense, lamps, excellent food offerings, water, flowers, fruits, and so forth; betel leaf, fans, umbrellas, chowries, and the waving of lights (ārārtika), and so on. || 8.1 ||
They performed circumambulation, offered praise, and presented forgiveness, water for the feet (arghya), and handfuls of flowers, saying:
"O God of gods, Hari, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, Lord of the universe! (82)
"Accept us as your female slaves; we are indeed your slaves.
Having thus resolved, they offered handfuls of flowers with voices choked with emotion. (83)
At midday as well, having worshipped the Lord in this very same manner and fed Hari,
they likewise worshipped Him in the evening and performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) for Hari.
And they gave him sweet food; Hari became satisfied and contented.
Having performed the night vigil before Hari, they kept watch throughout the night. (85)
They danced and sang a sweet song accompanied by rhythmic timing;
at that moment, the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Puruṣottama manifested himself.
The Blessed One, possessing fourfold nature, took up each of those [rosaries] individually;
placing those four rosaries on his left side with his four forms, he held them. (87)
Having bowed his neck, he accepted what was offered by them;
being delighted, he repeatedly touched and joyfully embraced them. (88)
Inaccessible, inconceivable, unreal, and indeed indescribable;
having bestowed happiness upon those two, he quickly placed them upon Garuḍa. (89)
Having bowed to the Creator and received his dowry as well as his blessings, [he departed].
And by Brahmā, according to the prescribed rite, they were offered to Nārāyaṇa. ||90||
Having caused the wedding to be performed, Kṛṣṇakānta departed for his own abode—that which is the imperishable, supreme light, the all-pervading, most excellent Brahman. (91)
Since other abodes had indeed manifested from that [place], Śrī Kṛṣṇa Puruṣottama went to those [abodes] with his wives. 92.
Jayā, Lalitā, Pārvatī, and Prabhā were in the supreme ether;
these others, who had become liberated in the sky, became the wives of Hari. ||93||
Those who have gone to the imperishable abode rejoice like gods, equal to those dear to the divine;
having thus performed the vow on the thirteenth day at Śrī Puruṣottama. ||94||
Having performed the worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa in the month of Māsa, they attained the supreme state;
for even a very small [act] yields a divine and indeed infinite fruit eternally. (95)
Those who, with minds fixed on Kṛṣṇa, shall hear or read this chapter, for them too there will be that same fruit; of this there is no doubt. (96)

Thus ends the three hundred and fifth chapter, titled "The Description of how the Daughters of Brahmā—named Jayā, Lalitā, Pārvatī, and Prabhā—who were created for the sake of the four Sanakas and others, attained the status of wives of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa at the abode of Śrī Puruṣottama through the vow of the thirteenth day of the month of Puruṣottama, while Sanaka and the others remained in a state of detachment," in the section on the Greatness of the Month of Puruṣottama within the first part, the lineage of the Kṛta Yuga, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī! Regarding that which occurred on the fourteenth lunar day in the supreme, primordial, and foremost Vaikuṇṭha—namely, the account of Dundubhi.
Within the boundary of the abode of the imperishable Brahman, however, there exists Vaikuṇṭha, the first and most excellent residence, which resembles Goloka. (2)
There indeed dwell the Kalpa trees of perfect form;
their daughter, Śrī, always resides there as a maiden. (3)
She possesses a divine splendor whose nature is the celestial realm; she is the Goddess presided over by consciousness, whose very form is the support of all. (4)
And the daughter of that goddess Vibhūti is the maiden Māṇikyā;
there in Vaikuṇṭha, the divine milk-ocean of nectar exists. (5)
His daughter is the maiden Lakṣmī, who is of your own nature;
these three goddesses indeed shine resplendent in that abode.
She had three friends of equal age, maidens exceedingly delicate:
Māṇikyā, Śrī, and Lakṣmī; they were always knowers of Brahman. (7)
Those women who are yoginīs of the knowledge of Brahman as the Self and who possess devotion for Hari constantly perform service to Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (8)
They constantly meditate with devotion upon His very image in their home;
these three—the divine opulence, the wish-fulfilling tree, and the ocean of milk—are [His manifestations]. (9)
Seeing the daughters' practice of meditation and other such virtues, they indeed rejoice repeatedly;
becoming embodiments of bliss, they bestow blessings upon them. (10)
In infinite abodes there exist many wives of Kṛṣṇa;
and you yourselves truly are those supreme consorts, beloved of the Supreme Brahman.
"Those who possess the form of supreme sovereigns, and than whom none others are superior anywhere"—having received such blessings from their father, they shine, ever-increasing in prosperity. (12)
In the morning, they bathe while remembering Hari and then meditate upon Hari;
they construct a divine pavilion, radiant with lightning-like archways.
It was adorned with pillars and other features bound with various jewels and gems,
filled with artificial gardens, and decorated with divine garments.
Adorned on all sides by the form of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, in the center was a beautiful lion-throne resplendent with jewels, gold, and other precious materials. (15)
And they place there comfortable mattresses, having installed within them an image of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. (16)
They bathe her with streams of milk and bathe her with water;
they repeatedly rub fragrant sandalwood oil upon her. (17)
Having bathed, they give divine garments in the morning; they wear ornaments and assume a graceful, amorous demeanor. (18)
They worship again and again with leaves, flowers, fruits, and water;
they offer incense, lamps, and fragrances in the presence of Kṛṣṇa. 19.
They massage his feet, they take up the nectar of his feet, and those devoted women smell the fragrance born of Kṛṣṇa’s grace. (20)
They behold that form of Hari, they touch the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, and they taste whatever fruits and other offerings have been given during the worship. ||21||
They listen to one another’s singing of hymns in praise of the Blessed One, and they speak of the virtues and conduct of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (22)
They undertake the work of Hari and circumambulate him;
likewise, they display graceful charms, gestures, and expressions, as well as mental bliss. (23)
They perform reflection, determination, and the exercise of ownership born of union with Kṛṣṇa;
before him are vessels of sweet food and nectar, as well as vessels of water. (24)
They offered golden plates filled with food offerings; they fed Him with full devotion and further delighted Hari. 25.
They cause water to be offered for drinking and they rejoice before Hari;
they play musical instruments and joyfully perform the waving of lights (ārārtika). ||26||
They bow down to Hari and praise his virtues;
they describe his deeds and recount his narratives. (27)
They meditate on Him whose heart is dark (Kṛṣṇa) and offer their hearts to Hari;
they satisfy Nārāyaṇa by presenting handfuls of flowers.
They praise the Supreme Self, they also remember and utter the names of Hari; they constantly perform service, cultivate friendship, and offer self-surrender. (29)
Thus, performing divine acts consisting of devotion, they worship Him even at midday; and Śrī herself offers them fruits. (30)
Even from the wish-fulfilling trees, the celestial maidens carry away that which is most excellent, most sublime, delightful, flavorful, sweet, and free from acidity. || 3.1 ||
The daughter of the tree, Śrī, also offers ever-new fruit;
she gathers from the plantain trees perfectly ripe plantains. (32)
And having gathered the finest mangoes from the mango trees, and having obtained desirable sour fruits from the *karmada* trees, [he gave them]. (33)
And having gathered from the vines ripe and succulent karkaṭikās, as well as well-ripened kaliṅgas which bring about coolness; ||34||
Then, having brought ripe wood-apples from those trees,
and having also gathered sweet dates from the date-palm trees.
Having brought from Kaṭīṅguda the fruits of the Kaṭīṅguda tree— namely,
large iṅguda fruits that were ripe and possessed a succulent, oily essence— 36.
Śrī brings and offers them, and Nārāyaṇa himself eats—delicious dates and most flavorful grapes. (37)
Dates, dates-pods, and the like, palmyra fruits, and bilva fruits; earthy fruits that are very sweet and smooth. (38)
Kṣīrikā fruits, tawny jackfruits, and large ones as well;
various kinds of garlic, and indeed jars of ghee. (39)
There were ripe śiṅgava fruits, as well as jambū and rāvaṇa fruits;
they were like nectar, most sweet, and the ṭiṭīma fruits possessed a delicious flavor.
Pomegranates, sugarcane stalks, fresh jujubes, tamarinds,
madhuka fruits, almonds, and bahubījaka nuts.
And *rāma* fruits, sweet *sītā* fruits, various trees, as well as *jambīra* trees in bloom. ||42||
Having brought cirbhaṭas with their fruits, ṭimṭimas, and other fresh raṅgas, Śrī gave them [to him]. (43)
To Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the embodiment of Śrī Puruṣottama, the Blessed Lord indeed offered these with devotion and with his entire being. (44)
The maiden Māṇikyā, possessing divine splendor, brings jewels for the sake of the Blessed One and personally wears Acyuta himself. ||45||
Likewise, garlands of jewels, strings of pearls, pearl bracelets, diamonds, rubies, and emeralds; ||46||
And also sapphire gems, kaustubhas, and likewise bhīṣmaka stones; cat's-eye gems, topazes, karketakas, and golden [gems]. ||47||
Hārita pearls, pulakas, rudhiras, as well as sphaṭikas, vidrumas, pravālas, māṇikyās, and citrakas; ||48||
Having taken gomedas, mahānīlas, and kūpyas, Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa gave them those jewels consisting of precious gems. 49.
Having donned the ornaments, he became exceedingly pleased;
then indeed Lakṣmī, the daughter of the Ocean of Milk, who is ever disposed toward the virtuous, [appeared]. (50)
He caused them to eat and indeed caused them to drink those very things:
the essence of milk, milk-rice (pāyasa), and milk-prepared rice with grains. || 5.1 ||
The milk-foam, the churned milk, the stirred milk, the milk-oblation, the boiled milk decoction, the lumps of milk, and the auspicious milk-plantain. 52.
She gave curd, clarified butter, buttermilk, fresh butter, and milk-porridge; she also provided rice with milk, milk mixed [with other foods], and drinks of milk and so forth. ||53||
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa indeed ate and drank those various things, and she gave him diverse jewels produced from the milk-ocean. ||54||
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, filled with devotion, accepted those things which Śrī Māṇikyā Lakṣmī had offered with heartfelt sincerity. (55)

He partook of fruits, jewels, and milk-rice, and he wore and ate that which was filled with devotion; seeing his supreme fortune, his excellent gems, and his Lakṣmī ever intent on service, Hari was pleased. (56)

And every evening, those daughters, intent on propitiation, performed worship just as before; with great devotion, they always offered the lustration ceremony (*nīrājana*), food, and other offerings. (57)
On the fourteenth day of the intercalary month, at midday, following the worship, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa was indeed heard by them through the sounding of drums. ||58||
Let them perform worship constantly; let them perform my propitiation;
let them offer something to me and come to my abode. (59)
I am the person known as Puruṣottama, the Lord of the abode of Brahman; I am the presiding deity of the intercalary month. I speak it, and indeed I grant it.
Those who reside in Goloka and those who reside in Vaikuṇṭha—both women and men—who observe this vow on the fourteenth day of the intercalary month; ||| 6.1 ||
I, the Blessed One, shall fulfill their mental desire;
I shall grant them the supreme abode, the dwelling place that transcends the imperishable.
People shall worship me with fruits, jewels, and milk-rice;
they shall attain the supreme abode where I, the Supreme Person, reside. (6.3)
I grant a superior state of existence to others who dwell in my abodes;
let my devoted followers, full of devotion, attain the supreme station. 64.
Neither Vaikuṇṭha nor Goloka exists like this; indeed, there is nothing else whatsoever that is equal to my own abode. 65.
There is no one equal to me, nor indeed anyone superior; there is nothing whatsoever comparable to Brahmā.
There is no other happiness equal to my own happiness; let the noble ones taste it by accepting even a small gift. (66)

May they become my servant-maids, may they become devoted, and may they eternally enjoy the mere measure of bliss obtained from my form; may they take delight in me through the performance of the excellent vow on the fourteenth day. ॥67॥
May human women, having propitiated me, become deities in heaven;
and may goddesses, having propitiated me, likewise become ṛṣis.
May the daughters of the ṛṣis, having propitiated me, become indeed sovereigns; and may the daughters of Īśāna, having propitiated me, likewise become goddesses of power. (69)
May the goddesses, having propitiated me, become Nārāyaṇīs;
and may the Nārāyaṇīs, having propitiated me with joy, become gopīs. (70)
And having propitiated me, the Supreme Person, may all of them become supreme women who are eternally liberated. || 7.1 ||
Having propitiated me, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person, let those who seek my vow attain my supreme, imperishable abode. ||72||
Whoever performs this vow at Śrī Puruṣottama on the fourteenth day of the intercalary month has indeed acquired everything that belongs to me. (73)
I speak, I speak, indeed I speak again: "Come with me!
Dwell indeed within my imperishable abode together with me. (74)
I am pleased by your roar; I tell you again and again:
on the fourteenth day of the intercalary month, come to my abode through the observance of this vow. (75)
Having heard the drum of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa in Vaikuṇṭha, they went there with joy and haste to where the sound originated. ||76||
Śrī, Hṛṣṭā, Māṇikyā, and Lakṣmī, delighted within their hearts, bowed again and again, and spoke to that drum of Hari: ||77||
We dwell here in Vaikuṇṭha, the abode of Nārāyaṇa, in great bliss; therefore, if the Lord so desires, He bestows upon us supreme good fortune. (78)
"We are maidens; we shall always perform the worship of that Hari.
Today, according to the determination regarding the intercalary month, we shall observe the vow of the fourteenth day. (79)
When will Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord of the Imperishable, appear? When will the Supreme, the Ancient, the Puruṣottama, lead us away? (80)
Having heard that, Dundubhi then said to them: "The Lord will indeed come today at night after his worship; you must keep a vigil. (8.1)
Let you praise Janārdana, the Supreme Self dwelling within the heart;
may your desires come to fruition. (82)
Having spoken thus, Dundubhi, honored with unbroken grains and flowers, departed.
At midnight, the maidens worshipped Śrī Kṛṣṇa continuously throughout the night. (83)
While they were keeping watch there, Śrī performed a beautiful dance; Māṇikyā, meanwhile, played musical instruments there in time with the rhythm. (84)
Lakṣmī made the singing, and the three of them sang together with beautiful voices, accompanied by the sounds of small bells, anklets, and bracelets. ||85||

I bow to the Supreme Lord, the manifest Sovereign of Bliss—Truth, Brahman, the imperishable, the supreme and the non-supreme, the Lord of this world and the Lord of the next world; eternal knowledge, infinite and boundless, possessing manifold forms, the Lord of the Lotus; peaceful, lovely as the sun, devoid of sin, the great bliss of Brahman-bliss. (86)

I bow to the Supreme Lord, the embodiment of supreme bliss who manifests as the Lord; whose feet are worshipped by the hosts of liberated attendants of the Imperishable Lord in His abode; whose face shines with the nectar-abode of pure consciousness; who is the sole moon of nectar for the liberated souls; whose soles are bowed to by Śrīvatsa, Brahmā, and Śiva; and who is the joy of His friends. (87)

I bow to the Supreme Lord, the Sovereign of Manifestation, the Supreme Bliss; whose form dwells in the midst of the divine, indivisible, and infinite circle of the lords of sages; who is with-form yet the supreme form, to be known through the chapters of the Vedas and Agamas; who is the divine abode, unborn in nature, beginningless, and the treasury of divine qualities. 88.

I bow to the Supreme Lord, the Sovereign of Manifestations and Supreme Bliss, who possesses a gentle luster, wears a garland of consciousness as earrings and a crown, and is clad in fine yellow garments; who is endowed with all-knowing and immeasurable power, who is Hari and Kṛṣṇa, the bestower of inconceivable bliss; whose fame is praised by the Vedas and Āgamas, and who proclaims the Dharma according to the Vedic doctrine. (89)

I bow to the Supreme Lord, the best of gods, who illuminates the world and its beyond, whose splendor dwells in the unworldly realm, who is ineffable, from whom this universe originates and so forth, the Blessed One who is the refuge for the shelterless, the beloved of the lowly, Kṛṣṇa, whose very form is the essence of compassion, who is merciful toward the distressed, and the supreme bliss of the manifest Lord. (90)

I bow to the Supreme Lord, the Sovereign of Manifestation and Supreme Bliss—He who possesses a luster like that of radiant gold, lightning, jewels, the sun, and the moon; whose true form is of profound color, inconceivable, unborn, and seated within the heart; who is the navel of the three worlds; whose eyes are like the petals of a dark blue lotus; whose face is smiling; who is the bliss of all. 9.1.

I bow to the Supreme Lord, the dark-complexioned, all-pervading, supreme person, the source of bliss; who illuminates the entire multitude of beings with the splendor arising from his own lotus feet; the true Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Sovereign, the Lord of the Mistress of Māyā, the foremost among the liberated, the Supreme Lord, the sovereign of manifestations, the Supreme Bliss. (92)
Śrī, the daughter of the wish-fulfilling tree, constantly meditates upon her beloved self; Māṇikī, the daughter of divine splendor, prays for the Self as her lord;

and even Lakṣmī, the daughter of the divine ocean of milk, desires a sinless husband—the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama) abiding in the imperishable abode. You are that very one who fulfills the purpose of worldly existence. 93.
Accept our hands in marriage and never release us; as long as your imperishable abode endures, so long shall we remain your wives. (94)
O Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, O compassionate Master, act swiftly;
accept from our hands the garlands of choice offered all at once. (95)
Having thus offered praise, those three ceased; at that very moment, the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Sovereign, manifested himself.
He who is the cause of the manifestation of all things, the cause of all causes, the Lord of the lords of all lords, the supreme Brahman, the illustrious Puruṣottama. ||97||
In the sky of consciousness, he drives a celestial vehicle known as a *vimāna*, drawn by white elephants, extending for ten million *yojanas* and filled with liberated souls. ॥98॥
Having consoled the three [goddesses] in Vaikuṇṭha, he offered to them the celestial trees of plenty and divine splendors;
and having paid obeisance to the Ocean of Milk, they were presented by him according to the prescribed rites. ||99||
Requested by his fathers, O Kṛṣṇa, he accepted the three maidens;
however, he said, "O Keśava, act in such a way that there may be no separation from us. (100)
Then Hari took hold of their hands;
Śrī, Lakṣmī, and Māṇikyā shone forth, equal to Kṛṣṇa.
Having caused two forms of each of them to be made, that best of men, having well protected three shadow-forms of them under the supervision of his father, [placed them in the fire]. (102)
Having assumed three divine forms suitable for Puruṣottama, worthy of residence in the imperishable abode (Akṣaradhāma), and taking the form of consorts, they [approached him]. || 103 ||
Having caused the three [queens] to ascend the celestial chariot, Hari himself, the Supreme Person, departed for his divine abode of imperishable syllables, accompanied by his wives. 104.
And thus, by virtue of their vow on the fourteenth day of the intercalary month, Śrī, Lakṣmī, and Māṇikyā became the three eternal wives of Hari. (105)
In this eternal abode, what indeed is difficult to attain?
There is no doubt that such a fruit shall accrue both to the listener and to the speaker. 106.

Thus ends the three hundred and sixth chapter, titled "The Description of how Māṇikyā—the daughter of Śrī, who possesses divine opulence and is the daughter of the Kalpavṛkṣa tree, and Lakṣmī, the daughter of the divine Ocean of Milk—attained the status of wife to the Supreme Brahman Puruṣottama Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa in the imperishable realm (Akṣaradhāma) through the vow on the fourteenth day of the intercalary month," within the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, in the first section concerning the lineage of the Kṛta Yuga, specifically the majesty of the month of Puruṣottama, following the hearing of the celestial drum in Vaikuṇṭha.
