Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī! To this story originating from a previous kalpa.
In Saurāṣṭra, on the Raivata mountain, there was one named Samitpīyūṣa. || 1 ||
There was a king, and he had twenty-seven wives:
Ūrjāhuti, Puṣkariṇī, Padmapatrā, and Karīṣiṇī; || 2 ||
Viśvapriyā, Ādityavarṇā, Hariṇī, Hemamālinī, Vasudhīti, Vahniśikhā, Padmākṣī, and Padmamālinī. (3)
Prabhāsā, Jagatī, Paṅkti, Bṛhatī, Iḍā, Piśaṅginī, Suṣumṇā, Purītat, Viśvārcis, and Padmanemikā. || 4 ||
Hiraṇyavarṇā, Candrā, Padmavarṇā, and Vamrikā,
as well as Vidyullekhā— all of them were devoted solely to their husbands.
Devoted to the practice of charity and righteousness, they performed devotion to the Blessed One and honored guests with sincere feeling. (6)
They perform bathing, meditation, worship of the gods, and the recitation of mantras with devotion;
likewise, they perform the well-conducted sacrifice for the gods, the ancestors, and the elemental spirits.
Only after having fed their dependents do they themselves eat and drink, even though they possess hundreds of thousands of female servants, using their own hands. (8)
They perform service to Viṣṇu and service to their husband according to their own dharma;
for the sake of Viṣṇu, they cook and purify rice and other grains. (9)
Pounding [grain], carrying water, sweeping the house,
as well as scrubbing and washing the vessels for the worship of the deity, and so forth— (10).
Every day, they always gather the first leaves and flowers of the *tulasī* with great devotion, and never by means of another person. (11)
Indeed, for the sake of Hari, what indeed could be an improper act for devotees?
For when everything has been offered there, even the body—is it not produced [as his own] by that very fact? 12.
One should acquire eternal merit by means of this impermanent body, so that through the grace of Kṛṣṇa there may be both worldly enjoyment and liberation. (13)
That Supreme Lord alone is to be saluted, worshipped, and propitiated in every way, from whom everything arises—the objects of enjoyment, the food to be consumed, pleasure, and so forth. (14)
Since it bestows prosperity, wealth, a wife, a husband, sons, daughters, and so forth, as well as land, heaven, and great sovereignty, the wise man should indeed worship Him. (15)
As long as health remains in the body, the circle of the senses is under control, the digestive fire is youthful and a proper digester, and there is favorability regarding bodily functions. (1.6)
First, one should accomplish what is beneficial for oneself, whether it be that which is desired or free from desire;
namely, the state of the Supreme Lord, which is eternal, full of perpetual bliss, and everlasting. (17)
If the state were absent or impaired, there would indeed be no vision and so forth;
therefore, one should always joyfully perform the act of beholding Śrī Hari with the eyes. 18.
If one were deaf and devoid of discernment, there would indeed be no hearing of Hari’s name; but since this path is easy and favorable, one should perform the hearing of the infallible Lord. 19.
O Hari, for the virtuous, service to you does not truly exist when [the body] is cut or impaired;
rather, Hari himself should be served directly while one possesses great strength and favorable conditions at hand. (20)
When the foot is strong and easy to traverse, one may go to the divine abode;
when the mind is undisturbed, vigilant, and filled with vigor. (2.1)
The Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the bestower of happiness, should be meditated upon; the Lord, who is the inner self, should indeed always be worshipped by means of one's own self. (22)
When the city is broken, all the inauspicious forces will abandon it and depart;
there, in that place characterized by firm foundations, the venerable Puruṣottama is to be accomplished.
Having thus resolved, all those women, who were like nectar to the sacrificial fire, eternally serve Śrī Hari in the auspicious palace that had been constructed. (24)
King Samitpīyūṣa always performed the three daily ablutions;
he offered worship to Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa at the three times of day. (25)
As they were living in this manner, a great deal of time passed;
in that kalpa, the eighth day of the dark fortnight of Kārttika—the Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī—indeed arrived. (26)
Starting from the full moon of the month of Āśvina, with a seven-day interval before the day of the Dīpotsava festival, they observed the practice of eating only once a day. ||27||
On the eighth day, they joyfully observed a fast without water before the auspicious image of Kṛṣṇa known as Puruṣottama. ||28||
And having had a golden image made of Kṛṣṇa’s mother,
named Kaṃbhārā, he likewise had those [other images] fashioned out of gold.
Having had a golden image of Gopāla, the father of Kṛṣṇa, fashioned,
and having constructed a pavilion, they worshipped Śrī Puruṣottama.
They performed a dance accompanied by musical instruments, blended with the melodies of their voices;
at that moment, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, Hari, appeared.
Four-armed, adorned with the Kaustubha gem, wearing yellow garments and other celestial raiment,
dark as a fresh rain-cloud and resplendent with white luster.
Having beheld the wondrous Śrī Puruṣottama, they were struck with amazement for a moment; thereafter, they became transfixed there by his enchanting, divine form.
Bringing divine ornaments and other such items, they respectfully presented them to him; then she offered him an oblation of vigor and a golden crown. (34)
She gave him a lotus-pool and two beautiful earrings made of gold;
she drew a sandalwood mark upon his forehead with a lotus leaf. || 35 ||
Karīṣiṇī applied excellent kohl to his eyes,
while Viśvapriyā gave garlands of golden flowers to the wielder of the Śārṅga bow.
Ādityavarṇā gave him two bracelets as armlets, while Hariṇī presented nine golden rings.
Hemamālinī gave him a beautiful chain-girdle,
and Vasudhīti gave him golden anklets adorned with small bells.
Padmākṣī offered a pair of sandals fashioned from gold, which she had placed upon the crest of the fire, as well as a sacred thread and a meditation band.
Padmamālinī gave him sweet food consisting of vegetables and milk-porridge;
Prabhāsā gave him cool water to drink. ||40||
Jagatī offered betel-leaf along with its fruit;
Paṅkti gave fragrant Puṣpasāra and incense.
Bṛhatī gave him a most auspicious ghee lamp, and Iḍā held over his head a golden, radiant parasol. ||42||
The two white chowries, Suṣumṇā and Piṅgalā, and the Purītad, holding a fan, perform the offering of the vital breath. ||43||
Then Viśvārci gave a beautiful nakta-fruit into Kṛṣṇa’s hand;
then Padmanemi gave a cluster of flowers into Kṛṣṇa’s hand. (44)
Hiraṇyavarṇā gave him a discus with a thousand rims;
Candrā gave a lotus made of gold into the hand of Kṛṣṇa. ||45||
Padmavarṇā gave him a conch shell, and Vamrī then gave him a mace;
Vidyullekhā gave a kiss to that Supreme Soul. ||46||
She became the object of the Supreme Soul's exceeding love above all others;
moreover, by virtue of that merit, she became even more the recipient of her husband’s affection. ||47||
"She was indeed Rohiṇī, the wife of the Moon, in a previous birth.
Having spoken thus, they offered gifts and performed the *ārārtika* ceremony. 48.
But others, upon seeing the kissing, felt shame in their hearts;
for them, the fruit they obtained from the moon was not excessive pride. (49)
A maidservant named Sarvajitā performed the massaging of his feet;
because she was devoted to service, she then became an object of his affection. (50)

Then they all offered flowers, unbroken grains of rice in their joined palms, and the arghya water; thereafter, they performed circumambulations, prostrations, hymns of praise, and other such rites. ||51||
Kṛṣṇa, being exceedingly gracious, gave them the milk-pudding of his favor;
having received it, they attained satisfaction and meditated upon him within the lotus of their hearts. ||52||
Kṛṣṇa said to those goddesses: "Become consumers of nectar;
adorned with necklaces of gold, gems, and jewels, you shall be divine beings who have made their homes in heaven. (53)
Having thus bestowed these blessings, Keśava became invisible;
they, having completed the worship, reported the news to their husband. (54)
King Samītipīyūṣa became exceedingly delighted;
accompanied by his wife, he constantly desired heaven after performing worship. (55)
The wives also desired the sovereignty of heaven spoken of by Kṛṣṇa;
thus, as time passed, this was indeed heard by Kṛṣṇa at the end of the kalpa.
Sounding the proclamation of the command of the Supreme Person from the drum:
"Let men and women, and gods and goddesses alike, hear my words! (57)
To whomever, whatever, and in whatever manner I shall give, that shall be exactly so;
for I am known as Puruṣottama, the eternal Supreme Brahman. (58)
I speak indeed out of compassion, without weighing merit;
even when a small deed is performed, I grant an incalculable fruit in every way. (59)

Those people who, performing rites for specific desires, shall offer me fruit, flowers, leaves, sandalwood, and unbroken grains on the fourth lunar day during the intercalary month—[to them I shall grant my grace]. (60)
I, the Supreme Person, shall fulfill all their desires;
for everything exists in me, everything is in me, and by me the entire world of moving and non-moving beings is pervaded.
Indeed, there exists nothing whatsoever, whether insentient or sentient, that is separate or independent;
yet my own reality is, in every way, both insentient and sentient. (62)
All the abodes of liberation, as well as the sites of supernatural powers and sovereignty, the manifestations of the lords, and indeed the stations of the gods; ||63||
The prosperities of humans as well as those dwelling in the netherworld—all this is mine alone; whatever they desire, I shall give it.
For one who has performed the vow of Puruṣottama-māsa—whether it be the fortnightly, the daily, or even the nightly rite—nothing whatsoever is difficult to attain. (65)
The king should perform vows, give gifts, and offer worship according to his power;
the subjects should perform vows, give gifts, and make offerings according to their wealth.
Whether a man or a woman, one should perform my monthly rite according to dharma; I shall never forget your vow or your people. (67)
Whether today or at another time, I shall surely grant abundant fruit according to my satisfaction; of this there is no doubt, for my devotee shall never be without reward.
For the sake of those with desire, the worlds such as heaven have been created by me;
for the sake of those without desire, the world of Brahmā has been preserved by me.
I bestow an abundance of happiness upon all, and indeed an infinite amount in the world of Brahmā, upon the devoted one who has taken refuge in me and performs vows for my sake.
There is no price for what one has done oneself; rather, the price is my word.
For whoever upholds my word, even his reward shall be infinite. (7.1)
For when a rain-bestowing sacrifice is performed, the rain that falls is not like that which occurs during the rainy season—measurable yet infinite. ||72||
The Blessed Lord Śrī Hari, the Supreme Person, rains by himself;
through his grace, I have indeed become the cloud-form during the month of Puruṣottama.
May they accept what is offered by me according to their capacity and according to their need;
having made the fruit into a cloth-sack, let it be scattered and let them depart after that. //74//
Those who shall offer praise during the month of Puruṣottama will also attain the highest happiness according to their desire. (75)
Furthermore, those other embodied beings who grant their approval for the sake of the vow during the month of Puruṣottama shall likewise partake in the happiness of heaven. (76)
Furthermore, to those men who provide assistance to the observer of the vow during the intercalary month, I shall grant happiness according to their desires. (77)
What indeed could be difficult for me to obtain during this intercalary month? To my devotee, I shall surely grant a dwelling, I shall grant wealth, I shall grant wives, sons, and cattle. (78)
"I shall grant a husband, I shall grant a daughter, I shall grant a cow,
a kingdom, long life, health, the bliss of the senses, and even eternal happiness.
Having heard this from the drum, King Samitpīyūṣa—
And his twenty-seven wives were indeed established in extreme devotion. ||80||
And the maidservant, having bowed to Dundubhi and worshipped him with unbroken rice, flowers, fruits,
and other offerings, prepared to perform the excellent Caturthī vow.
Having performed the worship of Hari in the morning and also at midday along with their meal,
they performed the final worship in the evening.
Having fed them with milk-rice and fried cakes, they performed the ārārtika rite;
and with dancing, singing, and instrumental music, they kept vigil throughout the night. ||83||
Having bathed in the morning and worshipped Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa with devotion, let them give gifts of jewels, liquids, and likewise sacrificial fuel. (84)
They gave sacrificial fees consisting of oblations, nectars, and sweet foods, as well as gifts of gold and silver, and indeed various fruits and articles. ||85||
They gave gentle moonstones that were cool and bestowed golden gifts;
at that time, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person, appeared in the form of a brāhmaṇa. 86.
Then King Samitpīyūṣa, accompanied by all his beloveds, arrived as a worthy recipient, desiring the jewels. (87)
He gave him a garland rich with jewels and bowed down with great devotion.
The Brahmin said, "O King, ask for a boon; it shall be so. (88)
Having heard [the praise] of the nectar of the sacrificial fuel (samit), he chose the lunar kingdom;
indeed, for the sake of the sacrificial fuel, he requested a form that would shower forth nectar. ||89||
The wives likewise chose the status of being the wives of the Moon in heaven;
having granted the boon, saying "So be it," the Brahmin vanished. ||90||

At the end of the kalpa, having undergone dissolution, that king, at the beginning of creation, acted for the sake of the one named Samitpīyūṣa, fulfilling his purpose through the will of Hari. ||9.1||
And the moon, the possessor of nectar-like rays, became the nourisher of medicinal herbs in the sky; his wives were the daughters of Dakṣa, and from them he begot offspring. (92)
Those twenty-seven [stars] were given to him by Dakṣa according to the prescribed rite;
among them, Vidyullekhā became the foremost and was thus dearer than Rohiṇī. ||93||
And others as well: Mṛgaśīrṣa, Ārdrā, Punarvasu, Puṣya, Āśleṣā, Maghā, Pūrvaphālgunī, and Uttaraphālgunī. (94)
Hasta, Citrā, as well as Svātī, Viśākhā, Anurādhā, Jyeṣṭhā, Mūlā, Pūrvāṣāḍhā, Uttarāṣāḍhā, and Śravaṇa; ॥95॥
Dhaniṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣā, and likewise Pūrvabhādrapadā;
Uttarabhadrapadā, Revatī, and likewise Aśvinī. ॥96॥
Bharaṇī and Kṛttikā—these twenty-seven joined together became the goddesses who are the wives of the Moon in heaven and bestowers of nectar. (97)
A maidservant named Devayuti was born under the asterism called Abhijit;
staying at midday brings her success in all undertakings. (98)
And by virtue of the merit of the vow on the fourth day, they remain so for an entire kalpa;
therefore, one should perform the preliminary consecration (adhivāsa) and the fasting on the subsequent fourth day. ||99||
Eating once a day, or eating only at night, or subsisting on fruit—this constitutes my worship; both the listener and the speaker of this shall partake in the merit of the Caturthī vow. || 100 ||

Thus ends the three hundred and eleventh chapter, titled "The Description of King Samitpīyūṣa and His Twenty-seven Wives Attaining the Kingdom of the Moon and the Constellations in Heaven, as well as the Maidservant’s Attainment of the Status of Abhijit, Following the Hearing of the Dundubhi Drum after Performing the Vow of the Fourth Day of the Second Fortnight," in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the first section on the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga, concerning the majesty of the month of Puruṣottama. 1.311.

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī! To this story concerning the origin of the past creation, involving King Vasudhāna and his wife Rādhyāsā.
At the end of a previous creation, there was a king in the south named Vasudhāna, a great devotee and a servant of Mahādeva. (2)
And his wife Rādhyā was a servant of Mahādeva, constantly performing the worship of her husband, who is Mahādeva himself. (3)
Devoted to her husband, she acts with undivided affection;
having herself bathed every morning, she constantly bathes her lord, the master.
One should worship Mahādeva with various liquids such as milk and the like,
as well as with leaves, flowers, fruits, garments, serpents, sugar, and water.
Having offered the nightly lamp, sandalwood paste, incense, and light, she remained in the service of Vasudhāna like a maidservant. (6)
The king also, having awakened at dawn and abandoned sleep for a moment,
meditated upon the Brahman Śrī Śaṅkara and performed his bath and worship.

Having performed meditation upon Śambhu in his heart and likewise having offered worship, and having distributed food and other provisions among his dependents, the king, accompanied by his wife, partakes of the meal. (8)
Filled with compassion, those two performed the affairs of the subjects as their own royal duties;
they constantly carried out the service of the gods and the distribution of gifts as if they were their own.
He gave food to mendicants, garments to those who desired them,
vessels to worthy recipients, as well as wealth and fruits.
The word "giving" never ceases at their door, nor does the act of giving ever come to rest day or night. (11)
In the homes of those two, there occurs day and night the honoring of Śambhu, as well as that of sacrifices, Brahmins, virtuous women, and the righteous.
Those husband and wife repeatedly gave gifts of cows, gifts of liquids, and gifts of sweets, just as donors are pleased when their requests are fulfilled. (13)
In that kingdom there was no drought, nor was there a year without a sacrifice;
there were no festivals without Kṛṣṇa, and no chanting of praises without Śambhu.
The two of them indeed caused the righteous laws of Śiva to be promulgated in the kingdom, and they had worship performed in all the temples of Śiva. || 15 ||
Having summoned all the village chiefs residing within their domain, the two of them commanded them: "Worship must be offered at the temple of Śiva. (16)
Otherwise, this will indeed be true, and he shall become punishable to us both;
moreover, through worship and gifts, Śiva, together with Śivā, will be gratified. (17)
Indeed, there in that temple of Śiva, the lamps are filled with ghee and remain unbroken;
and for whomever there are temples of Śiva surrounding their village, however many there may be—18.
In each of those places, an unbroken lamp must be lit by the king’s command;
for anyone who violates the king’s command, his head shall be severed. (19)
The worship of the king must be performed with the sixteen auspicious articles;
otherwise, the king will undoubtedly cut off the head of one who performs it deficiently.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, worship was indeed performed by those two everywhere; out of fear of them, lamps were lit in every temple of Śiva. (21)
Those two, O Great Śambhu, traveled by means of a celestial vehicle throughout the kingdom at night for the purpose of beholding [the Lord] wherever there were temples of Śiva. ||22||
Having performed the ritual viewing of the worship everywhere until dawn, those two returned to their residence and performed bathing and worship once again. ||23||
Just as the two were sitting down while intending to break their fast,
two mendicants, Śiva and Aśiva, arrived there.
Knowing that the two virtuous ones were hungry, they offered them excellent food; however, seeing that it was empty except for a *tulasī* leaf, both of them spoke to them. (25)
If there is the grace of Nārāyaṇa, we two shall eat the sacred food;
as the two Vaiṣṇavas, the best of Vaiṣṇavas, Śivā and Śiva will not eat.
If that which is offered by Śrī Puruṣottama were not pleasing, then the supreme dharma of the Vaiṣṇavas and the highest austerity of Vaiṣṇavism would be in vain. (27)
We shall accept with great devotion whatever is performed or given by Vaiṣṇavas;
indeed, we shall never at any time accept what is given by those who are not Vaiṣṇavas. (28)
"Offerings, food, and lamps are constantly presented to you both;
we merely observe them, we do not take them, for they have been offered to Brahman. (29)
This is considered the eternal duty for devotees who have surrendered their very selves:
never, under any circumstances, should one consume or drink anything that has not been offered to Brahman. (30)
Clothing, a leaf, fruit, a flower, water, food, as well as a seat;
even a single grain of medicine, or powder, or even something for chewing. (3.1)
Today, whatever is to be tasted, chewed, enjoyed, or worn as my offering—whatever is to be massaged, given, or presented—all that which has been offered to Brahmā [is now offered to you]. (32)
Therefore, let us accept this and nothing else; for this is our eternal duty:
everything—house, clothing, wealth, and so forth—must be accepted as an offering to Brahman.
Whatever one considers to be one's own—whether insentient or sentient—the king of devotees should offer that indeed to the Blessed Lord and eat only what remains. 34.
In the house pillars, in beautiful water-jars,
on grinding stones, on beds, and even on couches and other items in the home,
one should certainly use them only after tying a garland of *tulasī* around them.
Of domestic animals, birds, trees in the palace, and the cart. 36.
One must never utilize food, clothing, discus-emblems, or vehicles unless they belong to a Vaiṣṇava. (37)
One must never employ for one's livelihood bellows made of iron, storehouses, or merchandise, except for those dedicated to Viṣṇu. (38)
Furthermore, musical instruments, weapons, missiles, and objects bearing names [of deities] must be endowed with the insignia of the Lord by means of the self-consecration. (39)
Sons, daughters, wealth, wives, male servants, female servants, houses, wife, husband, family, and indeed everything—one should offer all to Hari. (40)
That which has not been offered to Hari is unfit to be eaten or enjoyed;
likewise, that which has been offered to Hari alone is fit to be eaten, enjoyed, and drunk. (41)
Understand this, both of you: that indeed is the supreme hermitage of Badarī.
Previously, I reached it there from Nārāyaṇa along with the sacred mantras. ||42||
Then, along with the mantras, the state of being a Vaiṣṇava was bestowed by me upon the goddess Pārvatī and also upon all the Gaṇas in every respect. (43)
My son Gaṇeśa is indeed a Vaiṣṇava, an expansion of Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
Skanda has also become a Vaiṣṇava, and even the Rudras are Vaiṣṇavas. ||44||
And the goddesses, foremost among them Vaiṣṇavī, are solely devoted to Nārāyaṇa;
Kailāsa has been made by me entirely dear to the Vaiṣṇavas. (45)
Through his connection with Badarikāśrama, even Himālaya was a Vaiṣṇava;
their ancestors were Vaiṣṇavas, and their daughter Menā was also a Vaiṣṇavī. (46)
Even the Milky Ocean is a Vaiṣṇava, for he always bears Viṣṇu;
his daughters Śrī, Ramā, and Lakṣmī, as well as the Moon—these too are Vaiṣṇavas. ||47||
Even the Vaiṣṇavī Gaṅgā was touched by the big toe of Vāmana;
and Vāsuki, the kinsman of Śeṣa, who is a Vaiṣṇava, has been held by me. (48)
The trident was born from the sun; Viṣṇu, the king of the suns, is the twelfth.
The bull came from Gokula; he is the king of the devotees of Kṛṣṇa in Goloka. (49)
He who is Siṃha of the Nṛsiṃha lineage is indeed a great Vaiṣṇava;
and the Meghas, Vairājakas, and Keśas are Vaiṣṇavas nourished by sacrifice. ||50||
The peacock and Meghamitra have their feathers resting upon the crown;
indeed, through union with Kṛṣṇa and through union with the clouds, their Vaiṣṇava nature is eternal. ||51||
What more need I say? Indeed, by wearing the head of Nṛsiṃha upon my neck, I am truly a Vaiṣṇava and a devotee of Viṣṇu in every respect. (52)
Viṣṇu is indeed the all-pervading Brahman; I am that splendor, Sadāśiva. Meditating upon Him, I have become manifest in the form of Bāṇa, though possessing a physical body. ||53||
Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Brahman who is the soul of all and higher than the highest—from him I am born, and likewise everything else is born; into him all is dissolved. (54)
"Therefore, O King, receive with reverence this Vaiṣṇava mantra;
I, Śambhu, bestow it upon you, and Pārvatī will give it to the Queen. (55)
Thus instructed, Vasudhāna received the eight-syllabled mantra;
"May Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa protect me," he thus received from Śaṅkara. (56)
And Queen Rādhikā received that from the mouth of Pārvatī;
they both also took the tulasī necklace and the crescent moon tilaka. ||57||
They both took the water used for the worship of Nārāyaṇa and the sacred remains (prasāda) of Acyuta; having partaken of these there, they were born as Vaiṣṇavas. ||58||
They offered food and drink mixed with *tulasī* leaves to Viṣṇu,
and they also presented them to Śambhu.
Then they both joyfully gave [the food] to Pārvatī and received it from her; they drank water and were filled with happiness. || 60 ||
Śivā and Śiva became exceedingly satisfied and truly joyful;
they bestowed blessings upon the two wealthy ones, who were themselves unimpaired.
"May you both possess a most prosperous and eternal kingdom with ten million servants.
Having said this, Śiva and Śivā vanished from sight. (6.2)
The king and his queen constantly worship the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa with devotion according to the Vaiṣṇava tradition, regarding Him as the very soul of Śiva. (6.3)
Thus, while Kṛṣṇa was being constantly worshipped by those two, the Supreme Person [remained there];
the most divine month arrived, and it passed day by day. (64)
Then, on the fifth day of the dark fortnight, they heard a drum being beaten:
"Let the celestial bodies and the human forms of kings listen! (65)
I am Surā, endowed with divine prosperity, among those who are both stationary and moving;
I am Dundubhi, beloved of Hari, in this month of Puruṣottama.
By the command of Hari, I proclaim: let those who perform a single day's *kṛcchra* penance in this month obtain a jewel as the fruit of their cowrie-shell offering and the entire earth. (67)
[He saw] Alakā, the city of gold, as well as the golden earth;
likewise, [he saw] that which resides in Goloka, and the golden [city] of the other world-protectors.
Let them go to the royal capital, or likewise to the golden city of Hiraṇyapura, or even to a golden body, or indeed to any other empire as they desire—let them attain these things of Hari. (69)
The sovereignty over the tastes, or that of the Sun, or the Moon, or the white-footed deity;
likewise that of Bṛhaspati, or Īśāna, or Agni, or any other deity. ||70||
Whatever may be desired by them, I shall grant that; of this there is no doubt.
Whether it be the fortnightly or the daily [rite], even when the intercalary month is complete. || 71 ||
Having performed the vow and the worship, may they attain supreme bliss, or even the station of the Parameṣṭhin, the Vairāja state, or indeed the Truth itself. //72//
May the fierce Śiva, Brahmā, and Viṣṇu, as well as their abodes, graciously accept [this offering] from me today by virtue of the mere observance of the Pañcamī vow. (73)
Having spoken thus, Dundubhi then ceased; thereafter, both of them bowed to Dundubhi and meditated upon Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person. ||74||
They indeed honored that musical instrument with golden flowers and unbroken grains of rice;
there they entreated it for the great state of being made of gold. ||75||
Thinking thus within his heart, Dundubhi then departed elsewhere; the two of them performed the Pañcamī vow. (76)
Having bathed in the morning, meditated upon Hari, and bowed with devotion to Śambhu,
they worshipped their preceptor according to the rules and performed their daily rites of worship.
Having fashioned a golden image in the form of Puruṣottama, he invoked Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person, into it. ||78||
Having offered water for sipping (ācamana), they both bathed him with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) and likewise purified him with water. ||79||
And these two massaged [him] with sandalwood paste, fragrant and moist, and they also donned garments made of gold-threaded cloth. (80)
They adorned themselves with ornaments such as crowns and the like, and they beautified themselves with collyrium, saffron, and other cosmetics. || 8.1 ||
They perfumed them with the finest substances such as flowers and incense, and they illuminated them with lamps, lustrations, and other rites. ||82||
And they propitiated him with hymns of praise, circumambulations, and other such acts;
they asked for forgiveness for their offenses by offering precious gifts. ||83||
And they both satisfied him with sweet foods, milk-rice, and other delicacies;
they gratified him with the chewing of betel leaves, cardamom, and other spices. ||84||
In this manner they performed worship at the time of midday; likewise they offered food, and they acted in the same way at night as well. ||85||
The pavilion was likewise adorned with plantain pillars, leafy arches, and very beautiful water-pots as well as lamps. ||86||
The two of them fashioned a beautiful mandala called Sarvatobhadra and filled it in the center with ever-fresh grains. ||87||
Then they both established a golden pitcher;
into that vessel [they placed] five jewels, water, fruit, and likewise a garment. (88)
Having carefully placed a vessel filled with sesame seeds, they two offered worship with devotion;
having installed an image there, they worshipped it with excellent articles. (89)
Bath, clothing, sandalwood paste, saffron, flowers, unbroken grains of rice, ornaments, necklaces, incense, lamps, and fruits. || 90 ||
They performed the nightly lamp-offering, offered praise, circumambulated, partook of sweet food, and presented water, betel, flower-offerings, and prayers. (91)
Then they performed dancing and singing accompanied by instrumental music; thereafter, during the night-watch at midnight, the Supreme Person [appeared] there. (92)
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is the manifest Lord of Lakṣmī and Śrī Rādhikā;
he is the Master of Pārvatī and Māṇikī, the Lord of Light, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama). ॥93॥

The Lord who protects those seeking worldly pleasure and those seeking the supreme good, the husband of Śrī Jayā and Lalitā, the sovereign of the imperishable, the lord of the liberated, and the master of the gopīs. 94.
And Hari, the Lord of all, the inner self, and the abode of auspiciousness, suddenly manifested, smiling and illuminating the quarters of the sky. ||95||
"I am exceedingly pleased because of your observance of the vow on the fifth day," he said.
"I grant you a boon; choose whatever you desire. (96)
"Because two Vaiṣṇavas have been born through my devotion, I am exceedingly gratified.
I shall give you my very everything; what else is there that is so difficult to obtain? (97)
Having heard this and prostrated like a staff, the two spoke to Puruṣottama:
"O Lord, nothing remains unknown to you regarding the earth and Rādhikā. (98)
O Lord, we do not desire even the sovereignty over the fourteen worlds, for that is but a small wealth; indeed, it only brings satisfaction to the wretched. (99)
O Lord, that supreme state consists of the activities of a potter;
therefore, we do not desire that state, but rather the position of Indra, which is subject to oppression by the Daityas. || 100 ||
We do not desire those states, but rather that which is beyond them—that which is supreme even among all lords, such as Vairāja and the others. || 10.1 ||
That which is beyond Mahāviṣṇu, the station of Hiraṇyādhipati, that which is beyond the city called Śrīpura, and the splendor beyond Vaikuṇṭha— 102.
The station of the Lord of Gold (Kubera) is indeed superior to the station of Viṣṇu; it belongs to the Great Kubera, the Person who is Fullness, and consists of a treasury. 103.
That which exists as the greatest among the millions of lords is indeed such that even a single atom of it brings satisfaction to infinite Kuberas of cosmic eggs. (104)
That great kingdom arises, consisting of an abundance of treasures and a treasury; for it is from this that the acquisition of divine gold belongs to all the lords. (105)
Therefore, we truly desire that sovereignty over gold; may you have compassion for us.
For there is nothing whatsoever that masters do not grant for the sake of their devotees. (10.6)
O Supreme Person, if what we have desired is improper, may it be forgiven;
O Kṛṣṇa, we desire nothing else than that the Supreme Person be pleased with us. (107)
Having thus entreated him, the two then fell at the feet of Śrī Hari;
"So be it," Hari said, and he spoke again to them.
At the end of the lifespan of the current Hiraṇyādhipati,
you two shall indeed become such [beings] again in another creation.
Having spoken thus, the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa vanished from that place;
there occurred the destruction of infinite lords of the Hiraṇyas. (11.0)
Day after day, this occurs for Vāsudeva; of this there is no doubt.
At that time, the destruction of one lord of gold took place there.
The Lord Hari led Vasudhāna and Rādhyāsa to that station; and Hari bestowed upon them the station of Mahākauberaka and the station of Īśa.
Having become the lord of gold, the possessor of wealth shines resplendent; and Rādhyāsā, the supreme sovereign Kuberaṇī, likewise shines forth. 1.13.
Of this four-faced Brahmā, born from the lotus, Virāṭ is the father; his father is Mahāviṣṇu, who is beyond that.
That man named Bhūmānārāyaṇa became a lord of treasuries, a king known as Vasudhāna. (1.15)
This lord of the treasury of the earth acts as the sovereign of all;
he shall remain as the lord of wealth until the dissolution of the primary elements.
Because I see directly through immediate perception, I know [all things], O Lakṣmī, my beloved; for there is no one else who is omniscient except me. 1.17.
"I am the very nature of the Supreme Brahman; I know all, for I am the omniscient and all-knowing.
Thus indeed was it said by me to those two at the time of the end of the previous creation.
Indeed, at the conclusion of the fifth vow, an eternal fruit was granted;
for who else besides me would be capable of bestowing such a fruit? (1.19)
Indeed, all things are swallowed by Time, except for Nārāyaṇa alone.
Having created everything, I enter it, I dwell within it, and I withdraw from it.
Nevertheless, I alone possess unimpeded knowledge, and no one else;
therefore, I have related this account of the previous creation to you.
On the fifth [lunar day], for the man or likewise for the woman who observes the vow, as well as for the listener and the speaker, such a fruit indeed certainly comes to pass. 122.

Thus ends the three hundred and twelfth chapter, titled "The Description of the Attainment of the Great Office of Kubera, Consisting of Sovereignty over Hiraṇyakośa, in the Current Creation within the Creation of Īśvara— following the Bestowal of Vaiṣṇava-hood by Śiva upon King Rādhyāsa and Queen Vasudāna, who were devotees of Śiva existing in a previous creation as a result of performing the vow on the fifth day of the second fortnight during the Majesty of Puruṣottama-māsa," in the first section, the Continuation of the Kṛta Yuga, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.

Chapter 314 →
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī! This narrative centered upon Śrī Puruṣottama bestows prosperity, grants happiness, and always fulfills all desires.
In a former kalpa, in the desert region of Maru, there lived a very righteous and wealthy Brahmin named Devayava. || 2 ||
His wife was the auspicious Devajuṣṭā, who was devoted to her husband; their servant was Girikṣita, and likewise their female servant was Adridyuti. (3)
They were always devoted to Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa;
having performed their duties as servants, they engaged in the service of Kṛṣṇa. (4)
Constantly devoted to the duties of a Brahmin and dedicated to the sixfold duties and others, those four indeed became solely intent upon devotion to Kṛṣṇa. (5)
The two Brahmins were their masters, and the two Brahmin women were their servants;
for the sake of Hari, they spent every moment with their minds, speech, and bodies.
A temple of Viṣṇu was indeed caused to be built by King Devasakha, the lord of Marudeśa, in the city named Bhāsvatī.
Resplendent with seven peaks, enchanting with its three-pointed sphere, beautiful with golden pillars at its base, and captivating with its three enclosures; || 8 ||
In the center, however, upon a lion-throne situated within the pinnacle, is the four-armed Viṣṇu Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, accompanied by Lakṣmī and Rādhā. (9)
Within the interior of each peak of Mount Dakṣa, the auspicious triad of Śrī, Prabhā, and Pārvatī shines forth, each attended by her own respective handmaidens. (10)
Within the interiors of the left peaks are Māṇikyā, Lalitā, and Jayā;
each shines resplendently among the three, attended by her own respective handmaidens.
Those four, each separately engaged in his service, being seekers of the divine, always perform worship in the central portion.
Girikṣita became the performer of external rites such as those with sandalwood;
on the right side was the worship of the splendor of the fortune of Pārvatī, frequented by the gods. || 13 ||
On the left side, the lightning-like flash performs the worship with rubies and other gems;
the king indeed bestows his wages according to their respective divisions. (14)
A dwelling fit for habitation, a livelihood such as a garden and so forth, annual wealth, and likewise a thousand pieces of gold. (15)
During festivals, the king bestows garments, food, ornaments, and other gifts in abundance; he also provides offerings for the worship of the gods, such as excellent sacrificial foods. (16)
Indeed, for one who lives in this manner, though he is a brahmin devoted to the gods, his mind is drawn by greed and he eventually seizes a gambling-dice. (17)
In some places, however, he plundered the temple property consisting of silver coins and gold medals that had indeed been offered to the deity by those seeking to undertake pilgrimages. (18)
And by that evil act of theft, the excellent substance of the divine grain was mixed with the wealth of the gods; thus, O fickle one, it became defiled. (1.9)
He desired to go elsewhere, for fortunes are considered fickle;
indeed, that which is possessed of divine property goes to destruction along with its very roots. (20)
Even if one's own wealth is acquired through righteous means, if it comes into contact with the property of the gods, it becomes defiled;
indeed, having taken a hundred thousand such items, one perishes as one departs.
Even food mixed with liquor, meat, and the like perishes quickly;
clothing adorned with divine garments surely brings ruin to the embodied being. (22)
Whatever material substance has been acquired through theft, and not given as a gift by the worshiper, the preceptor, or the guru, that is of the very nature of the deity. 23.
Wherever it is cast, even that which is rooted [in the ground] is consumed;
like the fire from wood in a hearth, it burns down the entire forest. (24)
The food of cows, the food of mendicants, the food of Brahmins, the food of women, the food of the helpless, and the food of the destitute—Agni indeed becomes enraged at these. (25)

The property of a Brahmin, the property of a widow, the property of a deity, the coin of a monk, the property of one who is not wealthy, and a great fire—wherever these fall, that place is consumed by fire. (26)
Whatever fruit of a deity’s worship, as well as food and a wooden cup, must not be accepted if one lacks the status of a deity, for it will consume that family. (27)
The gambling coin was stolen by those of old and even by those of yore;
indeed, it is just that the mouse steals yet another such coin.
Even those seeking the gods, in the temple of the Lord in the presence of Hari, offered and cast into [the fire] ladles and other such implements by those eager for the festival procession. (2.9)
He indeed nourishes his own wealth and deposits it for its increase;
yet, by some cause or other, that wealth comes to destruction. (30)
A terrible war indeed took place between the two kings of Maru and Kosala;
the lord of Maru was then utterly defeated by the armies of Kosala. || 31 ||
Then the entire city was devastated by the troops;
indeed, the wealth of those rich in riches was forcibly seized by them. || 3.2 ||
Knowing him to be a Brahmin honored by the king, they seized all of his wealth;
he was then expelled from that place, accompanied only by his wife and servants.
Subsisting on roots and fruits, he went to the auspicious bank of the Hiraṇyā on Mount Raivata, near Somanātha in the forest. (34)
Accompanied by his servants and wife, he passes his days wandering;
having gone to the Sarasvatī river flowing eastward, he reaches the Pippala tree.
Having drunk water, he sat down and rested for a moment;
then he remembered Hari, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the teacher of the world. (36)
They reflected among themselves upon the defeat caused by their enemy;
then a servant of Girikṣit spoke to the brahmin Devayāva. (37)
Even though our worship was performed perfectly by that wielder of the Śārṅga bow, we, his servants, were not protected from the enemy's assault. (38)
Indeed, all his possessions were seized by the soldiers, as was the gold of the palace;
even there, Śrī Viṣṇu did not provide any protection at that time. (39)
"How can one who does not protect himself protect another?
When this was said, the Brahmin Devayava spoke to his own servant.
"Do not speak thus, O twice-born one; it is not as you say.
Śrī Hari protects all living beings, and we are His protectors. (4.1)
Indeed, protection has been afforded to the four of us so that we may live together here; however, the sin of misappropriating the property of the gods is without end. (42)
Indeed, that was done by me, and that substance was mixed with my own substance; because of that, all our wealth has indeed perished through my transgression. (43)
If divine property and divine food are digested within one's own treasury, it will certainly result in the destruction of all one's possessions. 44.
All one's possessions have gone to him, and the appropriate fruit has been earned right here;
indeed, even the world of Yama must now be experienced, for it remains. (45)
Nevertheless, this fruit of our service does not protect us here;
for we have been slain and have not been protected by the Supreme Self. (46)
One must not consume the property of the deity, such as leaves, flowers, fruits, and so forth;
nor should one ever, under any circumstances, use its clothing, vehicles, dwellings, or vessels. (47)
If it is consumed through injustice, greed, ignorance, or even by force, then that [food] will bring about the destruction of the eater. (48)
O twice-born one, we have been utterly destroyed; this is surely not the mercy of Hari.
Therefore, an effort must be made so that Yama may not advance. (49)
For those who have surrendered, Hari is the protector; Yama shall not move there.
Indeed, the sixfold nature of surrender was revealed by Nārāyaṇa. 50.
Trust, choosing [the Lord], surrendering, humility, and firm resolve;
the determination to act favorably and the avoidance of what is unfavorable. (5.1)
In this regard, one should maintain such confidence: "Whatever Hari does for my sake is entirely appropriate for my benefit. (52)
One should request the bridegroom’s acceptance with the words, "You are mine and I am yours.
Then one should perform the ritual deposit (nyāsa), saying, "I, my entire being, am placed at your feet."
Even when one is a sovereign ruler of the entire earth, one should act with meekness like a servant;
even in the face of total ruin, one should not give way to grief but should maintain a steady mind.
"One should reflect well: 'Your satisfaction is my satisfaction; it is not otherwise.
Thus, whatever is delightful to him is indeed delightful to me as well. (5.5)
Thinking always of the devotion to Hari, one should indeed not perform anything else;
having obtained forgiveness for our offenses, He will surely deliver us. (56)
Whatever sinful acts, such as theft, have been committed out of greed for the sake of the belly, the Blessed One will surely consume them all through devotion. 57.
Uttering the name of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Brahman, while remembering Him, he who departs, casting off the body, goes to the supreme abode. (5.8)
Therefore, having dwelt for a long time right here at this sacred ford (tīrtha) and having propitiated that Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, we shall indeed return once more. ||59||
Or rather, upon the exhaustion of our lifespan, we shall attain his desired abode;
Śrī Hari will forgive even thousands of our offenses. (60)
Having reflected thus, the four of them performed the sacrifice of japa, chanting the name Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa at the site of Prācīsarasvatī.
Having bathed in the morning and meditated upon Hari, they worshipped Him daily with whatever was available—petals, flowers, fruits, water, roots, and so forth. (62)
They offered prayers and other petitions to Hari for the sake of water;
they did so repeatedly in the morning, at midday, in the evening, and at night. ||63||
While they were thus traveling along the path of the sky, they heard the sound of the drum of the intercalary month, proclaimed by the illustrious Puruṣottama. (64)
On the sixth day, at dawn, during the month of Puruṣottama, there is indeed a proclamation from the drum that bestows liberation, or for those with desires, it bestows enjoyment. ||65||
That delightful [song], having reached the path of his ears, proceeded forth;
yet, though it was contemplated by the four [sages] with meditation, it was not grasped within their hearts. (66)
Let all human beings listen—whether they be poor or wealthy, innocent or guilty, as well as women and men. (67)
Even if many offenses against me occur during my worship, whether committed by anyone at all, I shall certainly not take them even slightly to heart. (68)
Let them observe the vow this very day on the sixth lunar day of the second fortnight;
in this month of Puruṣottama, I shall indeed expiate my sin.
Today, by means of this vow, I shall indeed wash away sins such as those committed with adamantine glue;
I shall subsist on a single meal or eat only at night, arriving [at the time] without begging. (70)
Having undertaken it on the sixth lunar day, my vow must indeed be performed here;
for one may eat fruit, drink water, or even consume air. || 7.1 ||
I must perform a vow on the sixth lunar day; I shall grant him whatever he desires.
I shall by no means forget that which was previously done wrongly by me. (72)
Today, out of compassion, I, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), shall grant that which is desired;
for this month of Puruṣottama prevails throughout the three worlds. (73)
Even in the world of Īśa, this month proceeds by my command;
it is the foremost of all months, derived from the Supreme Person who is the foremost of all. (74)
"Therefore, bestow the fruit of the *mūrdhan* stage; choose whatever supreme boon you desire.
Having spoken thus, the drum departed from that place to another location. (75)
Those four Brahmins, however, afflicted by the suffering of poverty, undertook a vow on the sixth lunar day after hearing the sound of a drum. (76)
Poverty shall go to destruction, and happiness born of prosperity shall arise;
moreover, vast wealth and riches shall become even greater than before. (77)
If vehicles, carriages, palatial mansions, male servants, and radiant female attendants—all these—were to exist in greater abundance than even a kingdom, then there would be happiness. (78)
Having thus desired, they all undertook the vow of fasting;
for those who have previously enjoyed pleasures later desire the abundance of enjoyments. //79//
Living beings follow their own inherent nature, but restraint is difficult to maintain;
as long as desire is not pacified, the knower continues to act. (80)
Even for devotees, there is engagement with desired objects of enjoyment;
however, for one who perceives equally and is free from passion, there is no engagement at all. //81//
If passion does not subside even after one has reflected upon it and abandoned it as if it were poison, then, when a favorable opportunity arises, one desires to take it up once again. (82)
Therefore, those who are well-yoked in yoga establish the weakness of the senses; having washed away the power of sin through austerity, they conquer that which is illusory. 83.
Victory comes through fasting, or victory through the overcoming of many afflictions;
and victory also comes through relaxation for those who indulge in food. 84.
But victory was not achieved by these Brahmins, even though they were accompanied by their wives;
indeed, they desired a kingdom that was illusory and even greater than before. (85)
Whether it be the station of the Supreme Lord (Brahmā), or the station of the sun, the moon, and so forth, there is nothing else equal to the station of Indra, like that of the King of the Gods. 86.
Brahmā, however, is always subject to old age with respect to his own progeny;
the sun, moon, and other celestial bodies revolve in the sky under the control of another. (87)
For those who dwell abroad, there is no happiness and indeed no rest anywhere; being constantly weary and distressed due to this lack of rest, the station of Indra is better. (88)
Indeed, he shall possess the sovereignty of all the gods, as well as wives, dwellings, wealth, and so forth;
and in heaven, there exists for him the eternal Lakṣmī and the prosperity of Indra. (89)
Therefore, one should take up the state of Indra, which is auspicious and bestows the highest enjoyment;
thereafter, having acquired Vaikuṇṭha through devotion, it becomes a divine means of accomplishment. ||90||
Having thus resolved, they all performed the auspicious vow on the sixth lunar day;
having bathed in the morning, they then had an image of Hari fashioned from clay.
Then, having placed a crystal stone at their side, they invoked Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person. ||92||

Having bathed [the deity] with the nectar of the five milks and so forth, as well as with water, [he should worship him] with garments, ornaments, flowing substances, unbroken grains, flowers, and sandalwood paste. ||93||

Having worshipped with incense, lamps, excellent food offerings, fruits, leaves, water, and so forth, and having offered the *arghya* consisting of *bilva* fruits, one should perform the salutation and praise. (94)
Having offered prayers, hymns of praise, and handfuls of flowers to Viṣṇu, they caused themselves to swing upon swings made of creepers, ropes, and other materials. ||95||
At midday, as well as in the evening and at night, they performed worship accompanied by a vigil, including dance, song, and other arts; thereupon, Keśava appeared before them. (96)
"Choose boons, for you are my devotees; through my vow, your suffering has come to an end.
I have arrived to grant whatever you desire, and I am well-pleased. (97)
Having seen and heard of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Hari, the four-armed one, they bowed at his feet and then offered a handful of flowers and water. ||98||
They chose the abode of the gods, the prosperous station of Mahendra;
having granted the boon, saying "So be it," Hari vanished from sight. ||99||
In the intercalary month, on the bank of the Sarasvatī in the east, at Supippala, four [ascetics] abandoned their bodies on dry land and ascended to heaven. 100.
Upon the destruction of Prāntendra’s lifespan, following the dissolution of the ten worlds, those four went to the auspicious Maharloka and remained there for a long time. || 10.1 ||
Furthermore, at the beginning of another kalpa, four [beings] arrived in heaven;
indeed, through the merit of their vows, Mahendra became a Devayava.
Devajuṣṭā became Mahendrāṇī, the beloved of Hari;
Indrakṣita became the son of Indra, named Jayanta. (103)
Adridyuti was born as the mind-born daughter of Vijaya;
she is the daughter of Viśvakarman and is considered the daughter-in-law of Indra. || 104 ||
Pulomajā became Indrāṇī; she was his mind-born daughter and became the wife of Indra, accompanied by tens of millions of male and female servants.
By means of the Ṣaṣṭhī-vow, those brahmins attained the auspicious station of Indra;
through the grace of the illustrious Hari, they reached the blissful state of the Lord of Gods. || 106 ||
Whoever recites this narrative or listens to it with a concentrated mind shall indeed obtain the fruit of the sixth [vow] and likewise attain their desired goal. (107)

Thus ends the three hundred and thirteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Attainment of the Titles Mahendra-jayantī and Mahendrāṇī-jāyantī by Means of the Vow on the Sixth Day of the Second Fortnight of the Intercalary Month, Following the Total Loss of All Possessions Due to the Theft of Divine Property by the Brāhmaṇas Devaya and Girikṣita of Marudeśa and Their Wives Devajuṣṭā and Ārdradyuti," within the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, in the first section concerning the continuity of the Kṛta Yuga, specifically the majesty of the month of Puruṣottama.
← Chapter 313: Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā – Section 1 (The Lineage of the Kṛta Yuga) Chapter 314 [[Author: Chapter 315 →
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Listen, O Lakṣmī! I shall tell you of that wonder which arose from the vow of the seventh lunar day (Saptamī) performed by Sandhyā, the daughter of Brahmā. 1.
At the commencement of creation, Brahmā himself, the creator, [beheld] his mind-born sons:
Atri, Marīci, Pulaha, Pulastya, Aṅgiras, and Kratu.
She brought forth the great lords Vasiṣṭha, Nārada, Dakṣa, and Bhṛgu, who were handsome and endowed with youth as soon as they were born. || 3 ||
Then, from those divine beings who were skilled in their tasks yet caused agitation to the mind, there was born a woman of beautiful form whose mind was unborn (Ajamanas). || 4 ||
By name she was Sandhyā; she was Divakṣāntā during the day and Japantikā in the evening.
She was exceedingly beautiful, with lovely eyebrows, and she enchanted the minds of the sages. (5)
At that time, creation did not arise from the womb of desire and the like;
rather, Dakṣa and others, who followed their own desires, were then meditated upon by the Creator.
There, Kāma, the mind-born son of Brahmā, appeared;
he shone with a golden complexion, was restless, and had a face like the moon. (7)
With his hands, eyes, face, feet,
and arms slightly reddened, with eyes like the petals of a full-blown lotus, he is adorned with a flowery bow.
Then Sandhyā, Dakṣa, and the others beheld that charming man, who was captivating their two eyes with the casting of side-long glances.
They experienced supreme longing as well as the restlessness characteristic of the *rajas* quality;
they attained a state of sensory delight, and she [the mind] reached the state of desire. (10)
Then Kāma indeed took up the flower-arrows known as Harṣaṇa (the exhilarating), Rocana (the pleasing), Mohana (the bewildering), Śoṣaṇa (the withering), and Drāvaṇa (the liquefying). || 1 || 1 ||
Then Brahmā said to Kāma: "Deluding both men and women with your five flower-arrows, provide assistance for the work of creation. (12)
Whether it be I, or Vāsudeva, or Sthāṇu, the Supreme Person—we shall all come under your control here; what need is there to mention other mere sustainers of life? (13)
Entering the hearts of living beings always in a concealed form, become yourself the cause of their happiness and carry out the eternal creation. 14.
Having given him his command, Brahmā sat down upon his own seat;
Dakṣa and the others sat down as well, and Sandhyā also took her place nearby.

Thus, in the first section of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the *Puruṣottama-māsa-māhātmya* (The Greatness of the Month of Puruṣottama) in the lineage of the Kṛta Yuga, [it is told] how at the beginning of creation Dakṣa and the others, as well as Sandhyā and Brahmā, were overcome by desire; following their transformation, by the words of the god Dharma, Sandhyā attained the state of being the daughter of a *śvapaca* (outcaste). The residence on the bank of the Candrabhāgā; the manifestation of Gaurī; the manifestation of Puruṣottama through the observance of the Saptamī-vrata; the regulation regarding the birth of Kāmadeva in his youth; the creation of the two daily sandhyās (dawn and evening); the entry into the sacrificial pit constructed by the sage Medhātithi while remaining invisible; the purification of the body; the departure of the divine Aruṇā to the abode of Brahmā in her own form; and [the account] following the marriage of the daughter born from the fire-pit, named Arundhatī, with Vasiṣṭha.

(3) The word of Kṛṣṇa and likewise the word of Nārāyaṇa—which bestows exaltation upon the intercalary month—was thus protected by the Supreme Self.

Indeed, the great removal of the intercalary month was accomplished by the two of them. featuring various displays such as wrestling matches and other games; elsewhere with many mechanical contrivances, and elsewhere with bull-fights;
with dramas based on ancient history, with arts such as the *bhūta-nāṭya*, with music, dancing, narrative recitations, and sacrifices.
When such a great festival had thus arisen there, the Great Lakṣmī named Rukmiṇī joyfully said to her husband:
"O Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, O Viṣṇu, O Supreme Soul, O Puruṣottama! Celebrate a festival in my palace with dancing, singing, and instrumental music.
Saying "Om," he arranged a magnificent festival in the palace of Śrī, just as Puruṣottama, the Great Emperor of all abodes, arrived.
He likewise arranged a festival in honor of them; therein, he caused a splendor to be manifested that was superior to the beauty of all other abodes.

(15) Even the lion-thrones for the lords of all those abodes were installed there in the pavilion according to their respective rank. (16) And there, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, Kṛṣṇa, collected from all the abodes offerings of every kind of divine object. (17)

The Gandharvas, Devagandharvas, Gāndharvas, and those dwelling in the celestial abodes (dhāmavāsinaḥ); the Gāndharvīs, Devagāndharvīs, and Gāndharvīs established in the celestial abodes—(21)—they performed a sweet song with voices of very melodious and pleasant speech. (24) While the *rāsa* dance of the cowherd girls, the consorts of Kṛṣṇa, was proceeding, His divine powers, ornaments, weapons, and attendants—having assumed embodied forms—performed dances there in that *rāsa*. When everything had become composed of that [ecstasy], everything became full of rasa. Kṛṣṇa, through the surge of rasa, began leaping and enjoying that delight. (30) As he leaped with rhythmic clapping, moving from one wife to another, his crown shook incessantly and trembled again and again. (31) Meditating upon him, the Great Lord, pervaded by the bliss of supreme joy, stepped from one place to another, taking delight in lifting and pulling her along. (32)
At that moment, the jewel which had been fastened at the root of the upright *kālī* hair-tuft—having become loose from the crown—fell away.

Along with the falling of the jewel, the *kālī*-moonlight fell as well; yet, indeed, Kṛṣṇa did not cease from the *rāsa* dance. Out of fear of being trampled by his feet, those two of divine form—the jewel and the *kālī*-moonlight—remained there and truly rejoiced.
In the circle of the *rāsa*, the two became embodied and took delight; they did not reach their respective abodes until the very end of the *rāsa*.

"I shall certainly not wear this necklace, devoid of jewels and lacking ornaments; I shall wear another crown adorned with peacock feathers.

Ānarta, too, having bowed to Hari, took the sword, the jewel, the earring, and other pearls and gems that had fallen from the crown offered by Kṛṣṇa.
In the western ocean, he released a single drop of water; that drop immediately expanded and became known as Saurāṣṭra.
There, the crest-jewel descended from the sky, and other jewels also descended there from the path of the heavens.

Sitting down comfortably on the surface of the banyan tree, he performed his supreme recitation: "Oṃ! O Lord of Śrī Lakṣmī, Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, salutations unto You!
(63) By virtue of his austerity, Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa indeed arrived there; they then obstructed that king in order to grant him a boon.
(64) The king desired their dwelling place for the sake of obtaining a vision of them. Having promised, "So be it," both of them vanished from sight. (65)

She who was Lakṣmī became Rukmiṇī, possessing the form of Śrī and a divine appearance. He who was Nārāyaṇa indeed became Kṛṣṇa; he was truly the Lord of Śrī. (66) Endowed with Śrī, that very Kṛṣṇa then meditated upon his parents, who were the embodiments of the Kaḷki-jewel and were protected by him himself. (67) Having established them there with his divine body, Kṛṣṇa reflected within the temple of the goddess Miṣṭā and the god Nimbadeva. (68)
Where Gopāla was born, in that very vicinity of Aśvapaṭṭa, within a leaf-hut, he—being of mental origin—became possessed of youth as soon as he was born.
He became divine, possessing a truly celestial form from Goloka; he is indeed Kṛṣṇa, the Gopāla who protects the cow (gām) which is speech (vāṇīm).

Furthermore, he is the Gopāla who takes (lāti) and protects (rakṣati) the king who is the guardian of the earth (goḥ pṛthivyāḥ); that Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Gopāla, remains present in the proximity of the king.
On the fifth day of the dark fortnight of Āśvina, Gopāla Kṛṣṇa himself was born at dawn in the temple of Nimbadeva by the Kukuma lake.
As for the other jewels who had been abandoned by Ānarta in Surāṣṭra, they were all born there in the land of Surāṣṭra as devotees of Kṛṣṇa.
Among them, in that very place, in the field of Śatrūñjaya within Omālaya, there appeared Premamaṇi, possessing a most divine form resembling the sun.

In that field of the twice-born known as Premā, the divine Kaṃbharā—born merely by the power of resolve—was born as Lakṣmī on the fifth day of the dark fortnight of Phālguna. Indeed, she is called Kaṃbharā because she bears (bibharti) eternal bliss (kaṃ), which is of the nature of Kṛṣṇa. As soon as she was born, that divine girl was of the very form of Śrī.
Having recognized her as Śrī worthy of Kṛṣṇa through his divine vision, her father invited Gopāla Kṛṣṇa himself according to the rites of marriage.
In the presence of Koṭideva and others, he gave Kaṃbharā to him. Thus, Kaṃbharā and Gopāla became the divine couple Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

Those two holy ones, possessing divine forms, became ascetics and were always established in a palace rich with the splendor of seven stories. Once, on the morning of the eighth lunar day (Aṣṭamī) in the month of Āśvina, a pleasant sound of kettledrums was heard by them near the Aśvapaṭṭa lake.

"Let Maṇikalya and the others, as well as the servants of Śrīpati, listen! I, known as Puruṣottama, desiring to please the Supreme Lord, have made this intercalary month—which resides in the abode of the Imperishable Brahman—pure and of my own nature. Therefore, in this additional month named Puruṣottama," [81-83]

By performing the vow here for even a single day, a person observing the vow shall, through my grace, attain everything here as well as my own abode. Today’s vow on the eighth day of the dark fortnight bestows infinite merit; there, I myself, as Hari, shall grant whatever is desired to one who seeks the vow. Having spoken thus, Dundubhi bathed in the waters of Aśvapaṭṭa, bowed to Kālyāṇika Nimbadeva and the great chaste lady Miṣṭā.

Having worshipped Kaṃbharā, Śrī, Kṛṣṇa, and Gopāla as well, and having received the hospitable reception offered by them both, he indeed went to Raivata. (87) The vow of the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the intercalary month was performed by Kaṃbharā with a fast and by Gopāla likewise without water.
(88) In the morning, at midday, and also at night, the Lord Śrī Puruṣottama was properly worshipped with one hundred and eight ritual offerings. (89)
Fifty-six varieties of edible offerings were presented, and likewise, a brilliant *ārārtika* lamp-offering was performed with one hundred and eight wicks.

(90) A hundred thousand-fold sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) was given during the night-long waving of lights (*nīrājana*). Then the Blessed Lord Hari, the Supreme Person dwelling in His own abode, appeared.
(91) Smiling, showering affection born of His heart, and delighting the two of them, He said: "I am pleased; O Lord of Goloka, what is desired? (92)

"Like Śrī herself, what does Kaṃbhārā Lakṣmī desire by seeking this vow? Your residence here is entirely by my will alone. As for the performance of the Khaṭvāṅga penance, it is merely a pretext; even the separation of the jewel from the crown is by my will. The Rāsa dance and other such events are likewise entirely due to my will. Therefore, I am the granter of boons to you both; choose whatever you desire."

"I have come here for that very purpose, being Śrī Puruṣottama himself. Having heard these heartfelt words, full of devotion, from the Supreme Soul of all, the two of them bowed to him and, meditating upon his primordial form, said: "O Blessed One, if this is your desire and if we are present here as the cause [for it], then you should indeed be entreated by us: remain forever established here. For us, there is always the attainment of service to Puruṣottama."
The union with the beginningless Kṛṣṇa is difficult for one devoid of fortune to attain. You are our very essential nature; remain right here and protect us both.
(99) Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, who is without beginning, is served by Lakṣmī and Śrī, and you are served by those possessing the sovereignty of liberation. O Puruṣottama, dwell here!
(100) Loving care, protection, play, nourishment, and so forth—even for the divine—should be performed by you in accordance with the appropriate place and time. (101)

"Having performed this, we shall attain here your stable, supreme bliss. Having thus entreated Śrī Puruṣottama, Kaṃbharā and Gopāla bowed down to Him, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, Śrī Puruṣottama. The Blessed Lord, the Soul of All, having replied, "So be it," signaled with His eyes toward His beloved Dhāma-Lakṣmī; she, who had approached the heart of Hari, vanished within Puruṣottama.
This very Śrī Puruṣottama, who is higher than the highest and beyond Brahman, assumed the form of a child there; yet as soon as he was born, the Lord became a youth.

Kaṃbharā and Gopālakṛṣṇa both became delighted, for their son was the divine Śrī Puruṣottama himself, attainable through vows. Indeed, the vow was merely the instrumental cause, while his own will was the true cause; for the Supreme Person, his own divine play alone is the cause.

Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is indeed that Anādi-Puruṣottama, endowed with sovereign power and qualities equal to those of Śrī, Ramā, and His other attendants. By His own will, for the sake of protecting dharma and promoting devotion, He Himself has manifested in the very form of Pativratā. That quality known as Pativrata, which had been revealed in Goloka from the mouth of Kṛṣṇa together with the Lakṣmī known as Pātivratya, [is He]. (108–110)

Thus, for the sake of establishing righteousness, Śrī Puruṣottama himself became the son of Śrī Kṛṣṇa during the intercalary month (adhimāsa), [known as] Puruṣottama. (111) The celestial drums resounded and a rain of flowers fell; there, the Apsarases danced and the singers performed songs.
(112) In every abode, the Lords, the gods, the great sages, the incarnations, their divine consorts, and the Śaktis—numbering in the hundreds of millions—resided. (113)

Accompanied by shouts of victory, they worshipped the Supreme Lord throughout all the universes, in every incarnation of the Lord of living beings and elsewhere. (1.14) There was a great festival with an infinite feast for the Brahmins; it became a source of gratification and libation for all the creatures of creation.
(1.15) On the eighth day of the bright fortnight of Kārtika, under the asterism Punarvasu, when five *ghaṭikās* had passed after the setting of the sun—(1.16)

At the beginning of the night, the primordial, beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Puruṣottama, Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, was born in the abode of Gopāla Kaṃbharā. (1.17) His light shines everywhere here and beyond, like many suns. Knowing that He had been born, the Vedas and all the sciences offered their praise. (1.18) He is the supreme beloved of Kṛṣṇa, the treasury of all branches of knowledge, the Lord and Master of Prabhā, Lakṣmī, Pārvatī, Māṇikī, Śrī, and the others. (1.19)
The compassionate one displayed countless miracles. On the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Kārttika, he received initiation and the sacred thread.
At dawn on the eighth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha, he descended into Kāśī. On the ninth day, the Lord established the transmission of the Brahma-vidyās.
Having heard from the mouth of his own father that the entire knowledge consisting of the Vedas was established within himself, he indeed taught it to Lakṣmī.

Listen, Lakṣmī! What shall I say? He who is Hari, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), the Supreme Brahman beyond the Imperishable (Akṣara), the beginningless Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa—he alone exists as the Lord of Rādhā in the abode of Goloka; he is the Lord of Rukmiṇī, the Cowherd (Gopāla), and the Lord of Kaṃbharā;
he is the Sovereign of Vaikuṇṭha, the Lord of Lakṣmī, Nārāyaṇa; he is this very Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of All, the Supreme Person.
O Lakṣmī! I am that Nārāyaṇa, and you are that Lakṣmī, my beloved. Through the differentiation of states, the multiplicity of my forms is perceived by me.

(126) I, Puruṣottama, am the speaker of the sciences of the Vedas and Āgamas; you are my beloved female disciple, the manifestation of the listener and my servant. (127) O Lakṣmī! Here, by me, Nārāyaṇa, is bestowed upon you that knowledge and realized wisdom which resides within the Self—my own direct and eternal realization. (128)
The *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā*, consisting of ten million verses, is born from the sequence of creation, dissolution, and the ever-earlier and more ancient origins.

You should give fifty lakhs of it to Vairāja, wherein the preeminence of the Īśvaras is described for the sake of the Lord’s creation. You should indeed give twenty-five lakhs to Brahmā (Vedhas), wherein there are countless accounts of the cosmic eggs (*golaka*) and other such universes.

"O beloved! You must offer one million two hundred and fifty thousand [verses] to the ancestors, wherein all their branches are honored as the ultimate truth. O beloved! You must give five hundred thousand [verses] in heaven to your own preceptor; that is the Bārhaspatya knowledge of the gods, which indeed follows the divine path.
Furthermore, you must give five hundred thousand [verses] to Śukra for the sake of the Daityas who dwell in Pātāla and other regions—that which follows the path of Tamas and the like."

One hundred and twenty-five thousand [verses] should be given as the purifying Brahma-ārṣa portion, which brings about the attainment of Brahman for those supreme sages who have renounced the world. Indeed, one hundred and twenty-five thousand [verses] should be given to the Brahmins among men, by studying which men shall accomplish the four aims of life.
When time has passed into dissolution, I shall appear again and again in the form of the sage Vyāsācārya to illuminate that respective knowledge.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, have I reminded you of our past history as it truly was. In the beginning, all things—whether moving in water or on land—first go to their dissolution.

Billions upon billions of Vairāja Brahmās have perished; what then can be said of those such as Brahmā himself? I am the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), the agent of the great dissolution, the creator of the universe, possessed of eternal consciousness, the Self of all, and the inner controller. A treasury of inconceivable power and eternally firm, I do not forget even the slightest thing.

Where there are mountains, there water shall appear at another time; where there is water, there shall be dry land; and where there is dry land, there shall likewise be a dwelling or a forest. In battle there shall be a forest, and in a forest a city or a chasm; within the chasms there shall be a great bridge, and upon every layer of grass there shall be the sky. Where, when, and what has come to be—I know that, and I also know what is yet to be. Everything indeed occurs within me; nothing exists apart from me.

At the commencement of creation, O Lakṣmī, this nectar of our life-story was indeed made known to you by me under the pretext of the vow for the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the intercalary month. It is purifying for embodied beings who hear it, bestowing heaven upon those who recite it, granting liberation, and yielding the supreme merit of the vow.
In this festival, there is no doubt that the performer of the vow attains both worldly enjoyment and liberation; one desiring a son obtains a son, and a wife longing for a husband shall obtain one.

One seeking wealth shall obtain riches; one seeking land shall obtain land; one seeking merit shall become meritorious; and one with desires shall attain their fulfillment. (147) One attains fame and renown, and achieves preeminence among the virtuous. By reciting this [text], in every way, all that is inauspicious comes to destruction. (148) A Brahmin shall become possessed of wisdom, a Kṣatriya shall obtain victory, and likewise a Vaiśya shall be endowed with the prosperity of wealth, grain, and abundance. (149)

By hearing this, a Śūdra shall indeed become prosperous in every way and happy; he shall attain spiritual welfare and supreme fortune, and acquire splendor and valor. (150) He shall obtain strength, beauty, virtues, wealth, cattle, fields, and gardens; wives, sons, male and female servants, houses, kingdoms, and the like, as well as voices and other assets. (151) He shall attain health, independence, and freedom from bondage; likewise, he shall attain fearlessness, immunity from calamity, and even liberation. (152)
Thus, O beloved, the fruit arising from the eighth-day vow has been described to you. By performing the vow and worshipping, one shall attain Puruṣottama.
My incarnations are indeed innumerable, for I am Śrī Puruṣottama; I am the incarnator, the Great King, the eternal Supreme Brahman.
As long as Brahmā, Virāṭ, and the realms of Vaikuṇṭha endure, I, Puruṣottama, shall remain everywhere as the intercalary month.
As long as the moon and the sun shall remain, and likewise the earth, so long shall this eternal [site] endure at the Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa-tīrtha.
I myself, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, adorned with the banner, the Śārṅga bow, and other [emblems], served by Lakṣmī and others, shall abide there as Puruṣottama.

Thus, in the first section, the *Kṛtayuga-santāna*, within the *Puruṣottama-māsa-māhātmya* of the *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*: when the presiding deity of the intercalary month (*malamāsa*) was born as Puruṣottama, and a great festival of the *rāsa-dance* was performed in Goloka, the moonlight from the crest-jewel of Kṛṣṇa’s crown separated from the crown; these two descended upon the earth in the land of Ānarta in the forms of Nimbadeva and Iṣṭādevī. In their home, Kṛṣṇa descended in the form of Gopālakṛṣṇa, and Rukmiṇī-Lakṣmī [descended] in the house of Premamaṇi.
